entries.name: Nested antithetic modification
entries.definition: A finite conditional transition construction that starts with independent draws from the conditional distribution and successively applies maximal antithetic changes between a focal state and its remaining tail in a supplied ordering.

definition_evidence.locator: Section 6, PDF pp. 14–17, Equations 28–34 and Algorithm 2

claims.statement: Let pi be a normalized, strictly positive probability mass function on a finite state space and let sigma be a permutation of its states. Start with P(u,v)=pi(v). At stage i, the focal set is the singleton {sigma(i)} and the tail contains the states later in sigma. The same ordering defines every row for this target. When used as a conditional update, a probability-based ordering may change when the other variables change the full conditional, but independently choosing a new ordering from the current label is not the specified construction.

evidence.locator: Section 6, PDF pp. 14–15 and 21; Algorithm 2, p. 17; current-dependent-order negative control in research/discovery/nam-boundaries.py

claims.statement: Before a stage, write the remaining block as P(u,v)=r*pi(v), let q be the focal mass and s the total tail mass. For a nonempty tail, use delta=r*min(q/s,s/q). Increase focal-to-tail entries by delta*pi(v) and tail-to-focal entries by delta*q; decrease the focal diagonal by delta*s and each tail-to-tail entry by delta*pi(v)*q/s. Transitions involving previous focal states remain unchanged. If q<s, the focal diagonal becomes zero and the next stage operates on the tail. If q>=s, the entire tail block becomes zero and the construction stops. With only one state, the initial one-by-one identity matrix already defines the update.

evidence.locator: Section 5, PDF p. 10, Equation 19; Section 6, pp. 14–15, Equations 28–34

claims.statement: Every antithetic stage preserves nonnegative row sums of one and detailed balance with pi. The final NAM kernel therefore preserves pi and has at most one positive diagonal entry. Algorithm 2 computes only the current row by tracking remaining target mass s and remaining transition mass f. Before the current state becomes focal, an earlier focal mass q receives f*q/s after q has been removed from s, unless q>=s, in which case it receives all f. A zero residual f assigns zero to all remaining destinations. Once the current state is focal, its remaining probabilities follow the same maximal stage.

evidence.locator: Section 5, PDF p. 10, Equation 19; Section 6, pp. 16–20, Algorithm 2 and Equations 35–63

claims.statement: This parameterized construction includes a supplied fixed order, the upward policy UNAM using nondecreasing pi, and the downward policy DNAM using nonincreasing pi. These policies can produce different kernels. UNAM is unchanged by permutations within equal-probability groups and does not decrease any off-diagonal probability relative to the independent draw. DNAM can depend on its tie order, can zero an entire tail block and can decrease off-diagonal probabilities. Neither direction is an exact alias for the entire parameterized construction. Neal also uses unprefixed NAM specifically for a fixed-order policy; this record states the broader construction-level scope explicitly.

evidence.locator: Section 6, PDF p. 21, naming and ordering discussion; Section 7, pp. 22–24, Algorithm 3 and Equations 66–75; Section 8, pp. 28–30, Algorithm 4 and Figure 6

claims.statement: NAM is distinct from one Liu excluded-current Metropolis correction. The upward full construction has historical counterparts discussed by Neal, but an incomplete first-stage variant is not automatically the same kernel. The separately named UDNAM chooses UNAM or DNAM with equal probability and averages their matrices. Such a mixture is not generally one NAM ordering: for pi=(4/9,3/9,2/9), it has two positive diagonal entries, whereas each of the six supplied-order NAM matrices has one. The zero-self ZDNAM completion also changes the construction rather than merely choosing a different focal permutation.

evidence.locator: Section 7, PDF pp. 25–27, full and truncated historical constructions and iterated Metropolis modifications; Section 8, p. 28, UDNAM definition; Section 9, pp. 31–35; exact six-order comparison in research/discovery/nam-boundaries.py

claims.statement: Using this kernel for a valid full conditional while holding other variables fixed preserves the joint target. Fixed mixtures and fixed sequential compositions preserve that target, although a sequential sweep need not be reversible. Reduced self transitions do not establish aperiodicity or exploration of every joint state. For a uniform binary conditional the modified update flips deterministically; systematic compositions can therefore remain within a proper subset of joint states. This record makes no general variance, burn-in, finite-run accuracy or runtime claim.

evidence.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 2–3, Equations 1–4 and composition; Section 5, pp. 13–14 and footnotes 7–8

evidence_sources.title: Modifying Gibbs Sampling to Avoid Self Transitions
evidence_sources.version: Author-hosted technical report dated 26 March 2024; 84 PDF pages. Independently pinned from arXiv:2403.18054v1; byte equivalence between versions is not asserted.

aio_mappings.rationale: The construction defines conditional Markov transitions preserving a target. AIO MarkovChain denotes a stochastic process/model, so this is a method-to-process association without equivalence, subclass status or inheritance of Network and ProbabilisticHiddenLayer assertions.

limitations: The maintained mathematical scope uses a finite positive-support distribution with exact normalization and a consistent focal ordering. Zero-current conventions, floating arithmetic and countably infinite extensions are not specified here.

The source Figure 3 caption on PDF p. 16 says off-diagonal probabilities become smaller, contrary to its displayed matrix and the Section 7 inequalities. This caption direction error is not adopted. No author implementation was executed.

Historical attribution to the full Frigessi–Hwang–Younes construction is mediated through Neal’s report; that original full text was not obtained. The local Tjelmeland index-selection kernel does not identify its entire multiple-proposal and weighted-estimator framework with NAM.

All fixed/upward/downward policies are covered as parameter choices, without broad exact aliases. UDNAM remains a distinct mixture identity and ZDNAM a separate completion; this construction does not exhaust the source family.

entries.name: Zero-self downward nested antithetic modification
entries.definition: A finite conditional sampling construction that follows downward nested antithetic modification and replaces stages retaining avoidable self probability with a reversible two-focal-state completion that minimizes self transitions.

definition_evidence.locator: Section 9, PDF pp. 31–34, Equations 91–94 and Algorithm 5

claims.statement: Let pi be a normalized strictly positive probability mass function on a finite state space. Choose a consistent nonincreasing order sigma, including a specified tie rule. Handle a maximum mass of at least one half separately. Otherwise follow the downward NAM stages, but at each stage i examine the next focal mass q2=pi(sigma(i+1)) and the mass s2 of states after it. When q2>=s2, complete the remaining block jointly instead of taking separate DNAM steps for the two focal states. Previously determined transitions to and from earlier focal states remain unchanged. Equality belongs to the completion branch of Algorithm 5.

evidence.locator: Section 9, PDF pp. 31–34, Equations 91–94 and Algorithm 5; Section 8, pp. 28–29, downward ordering

claims.statement: At completion let a=sigma(i), b=sigma(i+1), q=pi(a), q2=pi(b), and let f be the transition mass still assigned to the block containing a, b and the remaining tail. When s2>0, set A=(q+q2-s2)/2, B=(q-q2+s2)/(2*s2), and C=(s2+q2-q)/(2*s2). The block entries are P(a,b)=f*A/q, P(b,a)=f*A/q2, P(a,j)=f*B*pi(j)/q, P(b,j)=f*C*pi(j)/q2, P(j,a)=f*B and P(j,b)=f*C for tail states j. Both focal diagonals and all tail-to-tail entries are zero. The relations A+B*s2=q, A+C*s2=q2 and B+C=1 give the required residual row sums; the paired flows satisfy detailed balance. Algorithm 5 has a separate zero-tail guard; formulas dividing by s2 are not used at s2=0.

evidence.locator: Section 9, PDF p. 32, Equations 92–94; Algorithm 5 Part 2, p. 34

claims.statement: If a maximum state a has mass h>=1/2, the positive-support kernel moves every other state to a with probability one, while P(a,j)=pi(j)/h for j!=a and P(a,a)=(2*h-1)/h. At h=1/2 the maximum has no self transition. For a one-state point mass, it stays with probability one. Thus zero-self in the name does not mean that positive self probability is eliminated when a state has more than half the target mass.

evidence.locator: Algorithm 5 Part 1, PDF p. 33, both half-mass branches; Section 2, p. 3, footnote 1

claims.statement: The NAM prefix and final balanced block preserve pi. If no state has mass greater than one half, every diagonal is zero. Otherwise only the dominant state retains the unavoidable self probability. The stationary probability of a self transition is therefore max(0,2*max(pi)-1), attaining the lower bound from invariance. This is a statement about the specified finite transition kernel, not a guarantee of convergence for every multi-variable update schedule.

evidence.locator: Section 9, PDF pp. 31–34, reversible completion; Section 2, p. 3, footnote 1; Section 13, p. 51, Equations 112–114

claims.statement: The choice among tied downward focal states can change ZDNAM even on positive support. For pi=(1/7,2/7,2/7,2/7), orders (2,3,4,1) and (3,2,4,1), using one-based labels, give different supported rows in the original exact calculations. ZDNAM is also not generally a different single NAM order: for pi=(4/9,3/9,2/9), its diagonal is zero while every one of the six NAM orders retains a positive diagonal entry. The source’s DNAM/ZDNAM comparison does not assert that reducing self transitions always improves efficiency relative to DNAM.

evidence.locator: Section 9, PDF pp. 31–35, Algorithm 5 and Equation 95; Section 8, p. 30, limits of single-order NAM; explicit tie and six-order comparisons in research/discovery/nam-boundaries.py

claims.statement: Using the reversible kernel for a valid full conditional while keeping other coordinates unchanged preserves the joint target. Fixed mixtures and fixed sweeps also preserve it, but a fixed sweep need not be reversible or explore all states. Uniform binary conditionals give deterministic flips, so eliminating self transitions alone does not establish aperiodicity or joint exploration. This record does not adopt a universal variance, finite-run accuracy, burn-in or wall-clock advantage.

evidence.locator: Section 2, PDF pp. 2–3, conditional invariance and composition; Section 5, p. 14, footnotes 7–8; Algorithm 5, p. 33

rows.definition: A large language model that generates natural language descriptions from structured data sources like tables, graphs, and knowledge bases, requiring grounding in meaning representations.

rows.name: Decision Tree
rows.definition: A classification that uses a tree-like model of decisions and their possible consequences including chance event outcomes resource costs and utilities.

rows.name: Decoder LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that uses a decoder-only architecture consisting of only a decoder trained to predict the next token in a sequence given the previous tokens.

rows.name: Deconvolutional Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network that uses deconvolution for unsupervised construction of hierarchical image representations.

rows.name: Deep Active Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that combines deep learning and active learning to maximize model performance while annotating the fewest samples possible.

rows.name: Deep Belief Network
rows.definition: An unsupervised pretrained network composed of multiple layers of latent variables that learns to probabilistically reconstruct inputs and perform classification.

rows.name: Deep Convolutional Inverse Graphics Network
rows.definition: An autoencoder network that learns interpretable disentangled image representations through convolution and de-convolution layers trained with the stochastic gradient variational Bayes algorithm.

rows.name: Deep Convolutional Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network specialized for analyzing visual imagery using shared-weight architecture and translation-equivariant feature maps.

rows.name: Deep Feed-Forward Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network that processes information in one direction—from input nodes through hidden nodes to output nodes—without cycles or loops.

rows.name: Deep Neural Network
rows.definition: An artificial neural network characterized by multiple hidden layers between the input and output layers.

rows.name: Deep Transfer Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that relaxes the hypothesis that training data must be independent and identically distributed with test data to address insufficient training data.

rows.name: Denoising Auto Encoder
rows.definition: An autoencoder network trained to reconstruct the original undistorted input from a partially corrupted input.

rows.name: DenseFeatures Layer
rows.definition: A layer that produces a dense tensor based on given feature columns.

rows.name: Dense Layer
rows.definition: A layer that is a regular densely-connected neural network layer.

rows.name: Deployment Bias
rows.definition: A group bias arising when systems are used as decision aids for humans since the human intermediary may act on predictions in ways that are typically not modeled in the system.

rows.name: DepthwiseConv1D Layer
rows.definition: A convolutional layer that performs depthwise 1D convolution

rows.name: DepthwiseConv2D Layer
rows.definition: A convolutional layer that performs depthwise 2D convolution

rows.name: Detection Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias characterized by systematic differences between groups in how outcomes are determined potentially over- or underestimating effect size.

rows.name: Dialogue LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is optimized for engaging in multi-turn conversations understanding context and generating relevant coherent responses continuously over many dialogue turns.

rows.name: Differentiable LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that has an architecture amenable to full end-to-end training via backpropagation without relying on teacher forcing or unlikelihood training objectives.

rows.name: Dimensionality Reduction
rows.definition: An unsupervised learning focused on the process of transforming data from a high-dimensional space into a lower-dimensional space while retaining meaningful properties of the original data.

rows.name: Discretization Layer
rows.definition: A numerical features preprocessing layer which buckets continuous features by ranges.

rows.name: Distillation
rows.definition: A preprocessing that trains a smaller model to replicate the behavior of a larger model aiming to compress the knowledge into a more compact form without significant loss of performance.

rows.name: Domain-Adapted LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which is pre-trained on a broad corpus and then fine-tuned on domain-specific data to specialize its capabilities for particular domains or applications, like scientific literature or code generation.

rows.name: Dot Layer
rows.definition: A layer that computes a dot product between samples in two tensors.

rows.name: Dropout Layer
rows.definition: A regularization layer that applies Dropout to the input

rows.name: Dunning-Kruger Effect Bias
rows.definition: A cognitive bias in which people with low ability in an area overestimate that ability. Often measured by comparing self-assessment with objective performance.

rows.name: Dynamic Conditional Correlation
rows.definition: A model that allows for time-varying correlations between different time series, used in financial econometrics to model and forecast covariances.

rows.name: ELU Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that is x if x > 0 and alpha * (exp(x) - 1) if x < 0 where alpha controls the value to which an ELU saturates for negative net inputs.

rows.name: ELU Layer
rows.definition: An activation layer that applies the Exponential Linear Unit (ELU) function element-wise.

rows.name: Echo State Network
rows.definition: A recurrent neural network with a recurrent hidden layer and sparsely connected hidden neurons that learns output weights to produce temporal patterns.

rows.name: Ecological Fallacy Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias occurring when an inference about an individual is made based on their group membership.

rows.name: Embedding Layer
rows.definition: A layer that turns positive integers (indexes) into dense vectors of fixed size.

rows.name: Embodied LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that integrates language with other modalities like vision audio and robotics to enable grounded language understanding in real-world environments.

rows.name: Emergent Bias
rows.definition: A use and interpretation bias resulting from the use and reliance on algorithms across new or unanticipated contexts.

rows.name: Encoder-Decoder LLM
rows.definition: A large language model introduced in the "Attention Is All You Need" paper. The encoder processes the input sequence to generate a hidden representation summarizing the input information, while the decoder uses this hidden representation to generate the desired output sequence.

rows.name: Encoder LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that uses an encoder-only architecture to encode the input sequence into a fixed-length representation which is then used as input to a classifier or regressor for prediction.

rows.name: Energy-Based LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which models the explicit probability density over token sequences using an energy function, rather than an autoregressive factorization. This can improve modeling of long-range dependencies and global coherence.

rows.name: Ensemble Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods that use multiple learning algorithms to achieve better predictive performance than any of the constituent algorithms alone.

rows.name: Error Propagation Bias
rows.definition: A processing bias characterized by the effect of variables' uncertainties (or errors more specifically random errors) on the uncertainty of a function based on them.

rows.name: Ethical LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is trained to uphold certain ethical principles values or rules in its language generation to increase safety and trustworthiness.

rows.name: Evaluation Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising when testing populations do not equally represent user populations or when inappropriate performance metrics are used.

rows.name: Evolutionary LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that applies principles of evolutionary computation to optimize its structure and parameters evolving over time to improve performance.

rows.name: Exclusion Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias occurring when specific groups of user populations are excluded from testing and analysis.

rows.name: Explainable LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is designed to provide insights into its decision-making process making it easier for users to understand and trust the model's outputs by incorporating mechanisms for interpreting and explaining its predictions in human-understandable terms.

rows.name: Exponential Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function denoted by f(x)=exp or e^{x}.

rows.name: Exponential Smoothing State Space Model
rows.definition: A model that combines exponential smoothing with state space modeling, allowing for the inclusion of both trend and seasonal components. Used in  forecasting.

rows.name: Extreme Learning Machine
rows.definition: A feedback network with randomly assigned hidden nodes that are not updated during training.

rows.name: Factored Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that views each word as a vector of multiple factors such as part-of-speech morphology and semantics to improve language modeling.

rows.name: Factorized LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that decomposes the full language modeling task into multiple sub-components or experts that each focus on a subset of the information enabling more efficient scaling.

identities.value: Factorized Learning Assisted with Large Language Model

rows.name: Feature Extraction
rows.definition: A data enhancement that transforms raw data into a set of measurable characteristics that can be used as input for machine learning algorithms, enhancing the ability to make accurate predictions.

rows.name: Federated LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is trained in a decentralized manner across multiple devices or silos without directly sharing private data enabling collaborative training while preserving data privacy and security.

rows.name: Federated Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network trained across decentralized edge devices or servers holding local data samples without exchanging them.

rows.name: Feedback Loop Bias
rows.definition: A use and interpretation bias occurring when an algorithm learns from user behavior and feeds that behavior back into the model.

rows.name: Feedback Network
rows.definition: An artificial neural network that refines its representations iteratively based on feedback from previous outputs.

rows.name: Fixed Effects Model
rows.definition: A regression analysis in which the model parameters are fixed or non-random quantities.

rows.name: Flatten Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that flattens the input

rows.name: FractionalMaxPool2D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that applies a 2D fractional max pooling over an input signal composed of several input planes.

rows.name: FractionalMaxPool3D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that applies a 3D fractional max pooling over an input signal composed of several input planes.

rows.name: Funding Bias
rows.definition: A group bias arising when biased results are reported to support or satisfy the funding agency or financial supporter of a research study.

rows.name: GELU Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that computes x * P(X <= x) where P(X) ~ N(0 1) weighting inputs by their value rather than gating inputs by their sign as in ReLU.

rows.name: GRUCell Layer
rows.definition: A layer that processes one step within the whole time sequence input for a GRU layer.

rows.name: GRU Layer
rows.definition: A recurrent layer that implements the Gated Recurrent Unit architecture.

rows.name: Gated Recurrent Unit
rows.definition: A long short-term memory network that is a gating mechanism in recurrent neural networks similar to LSTMs but with fewer parameters and no output gate.

rows.name: GaussianDropout Layer
rows.definition: A regularization layer that applies multiplicative 1-centered Gaussian noise.

rows.name: GaussianNoise Layer
rows.definition: A regularization layer that applies additive zero-centered Gaussian noise.

rows.name: Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity
rows.definition: A model that incorporates lagged conditional variances, allowing for more flexibility in modeling time-varying volatility.

rows.name: Generalized Few-shot Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that learns novel classes from few samples per class, preventing catastrophic forgetting of base classes and ensuring classifier calibration.

rows.name: Generalized Linear Model
rows.definition: A regression analysis that relates the linear model to the response variable via a link function and allowing the variance of each measurement to be a function of its predicted value.

rows.name: Generative Adversarial Network
rows.definition: An unsupervised pretrained network framework where two neural networks contest in a game to generate new data with the same statistics as the training set.

rows.name: Generative Adversarial Network-Augmented LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which incorporates a generative adversarial network (GAN) into its training process, using a discriminator network to provide a signal for generating more realistic and coherent text. This adversarial training can improve the quality and diversity of generated text.

identities.value: Generative Adversarial Network-Augmented Large Language Model

rows.name: Generative Commonsense LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is trained to understand and model basic physics causality and common sense about how the real world works.

rows.name: Generative Language Interface
rows.definition: A language model that enables users to engage in an interactive dialogue with an LLM providing feedback to guide and refine the generated outputs iteratively.

rows.name: GlobalAveragePooling1D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs global average pooling operation for temporal data.

rows.name: GlobalAveragePooling2D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs global average pooling operation for spatial data.

rows.name: GlobalAveragePooling3D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs global average pooling operation for 3D data.

rows.name: GlobalMaxPooling1D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs global max pooling operation for temporal data.

rows.name: GlobalMaxPooling2D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs global max pooling operation for spatial data.

rows.name: GlobalMaxPooling3D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs global max pooling operation for 3D data.

rows.name: Graph Convolutional Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network that operates directly on graph structures utilizing structural information.

rows.name: Graph Convolutional Policy Network
rows.definition: A graph convolutional network that generates goal-directed graphs using reinforcement learning and optimizing for rewards and adversarial loss.

rows.name: Graph Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that operates over structured inputs or outputs represented as graphs enabling reasoning over explicit relational knowledge representations during language tasks.

rows.name: Group Bias
rows.definition: A systemic bias characterized by favoring members of one's in-group over out-group members expressed in evaluation resource allocation and other ways.

rows.name: GroupNorm Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies Group Normalization over a mini-batch of inputs.

rows.name: Groupthink Bias
rows.definition: A group bias in which people in a group make non-optimal decisions due to a desire to conform or fear of dissent.

rows.name: Hard Sigmoid Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that is a faster approximation of the sigmoid activation using a piecewise linear approximation.

rows.name: Hashing Layer
rows.definition: A categorical features preprocessing layer which hashes and bins categorical features.

rows.name: Hidden Layer
rows.definition: A layer located between the input and output that performs nonlinear transformations of the inputs entered into the network.

rows.name: Hierarchical Classification
rows.definition: A classification focused on methods that group things according to a hierarchy.

rows.name: Hierarchical Clustering
rows.definition: A clustering that builds a hierarchy of clusters.

rows.name: Hierarchical Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that represents language at multiple levels of granularity learning hierarchical representations that capture both low-level patterns and high-level abstractions.

rows.name: Historical Bias
rows.definition: A bias characterized by long-standing biases encoded in society over time distinct from biases in historical description or interpretation.

rows.name: Hopfield Network
rows.definition: A symmetrically connected network that is a type of recurrent artificial neural network serving as a content-addressable memory system.

identities.value: Ising model of a neural network

rows.name: Hostile Attribution Bias
rows.definition: A use and interpretation bias where individuals perceive benign or ambiguous behaviors as hostile.

rows.name: Human Bias
rows.definition: A bias in human thought based on heuristic principles leading to simplified judgmental operations.

rows.name: Human Reporting Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias that arises when users depend on automated systems as heuristic substitutes for their own information-seeking and processing efforts.

rows.name: Image Augmentation Layer
rows.definition: A layer that performs image data preprocessing augmentations.

rows.name: Image Preprocessing Layer
rows.definition: A layer that performs image data preprocessing operations.

rows.name: Implicit Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias characterized by unconscious beliefs attitudes feelings associations or stereotypes that affect information processing decision-making and actions.

rows.name: Implicit Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that uses an energy function to score entire sequences instead of factorizing probabilities autoregressively better capturing global properties and long-range dependencies.

rows.name: Incremental Few-shot Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network trained on a base set of classes and then presented with novel classes, each with few labeled examples.

rows.name: Individual Bias
rows.definition: A bias characterized by a persistent point of view or limited list of such points of view, applied by an individual.

rows.name: Inherited Bias
rows.definition: A processing bias arising when machine learning applications generate inputs for other machine learning algorithms passing on any existing bias.

rows.name: Input Layer
rows.definition: A layer composed of artificial input neurons that brings the initial data into the system for further processing by subsequent layers.

rows.name: InputLayer Layer
rows.definition: A layer to be used as an entry point into a Network (a graph of layers).

rows.name: InputSpec Layer
rows.definition: A layer that specifies the rank, dtype and shape of every input to a layer.

rows.name: InstanceNorm1D Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies Instance Normalization over a 2D (unbatched) or 3D (batched) input.

rows.name: InstanceNorm2D
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies Instance Normalization over a 4D input (a mini-batch of 2D inputs with additional channel dimension).

rows.name: InstanceNorm3D Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies Instance Normalization over a 5D input (a mini-batch of 3D inputs with additional channel dimension).

rows.name: Institutional Bias
rows.definition: A systemic bias exhibited at the level of entire institutions where practices or norms result in the favoring or disadvantaging of certain social groups.

rows.name: Instruction-Tuned LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which is fine-tuned to follow natural language instructions accurately and safely, learning to map from instructions to desired model behavior in a more controlled and principled way.

rows.name: IntegerLookup Layer
rows.definition: A categorical features preprocessing layer that maps integer features to contiguous ranges.

rows.name: Interpretation Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias where users interpret algorithmic outputs according to their internalized biases and views.

rows.name: Kernel Layer
rows.definition: A layer that obtains the dot product of input values or subsets of input values.

rows.name: K-nearest Neighbor Algorithm
rows.definition: A machine learning task that groups objects by a plurality vote of its neighbors, assigning each object to the class most common among its k nearest neighbors.

rows.name: K-nearest Neighbor Classification Algorithm
rows.definition: A classification and clustering that classifies objects by a plurality vote of its neighbors, assigning each object to the class most common among its k nearest neighbors.

rows.name: K-nearest Neighbor Regression Algorithm
rows.definition: A regression analysis that assigns the average of the values of k nearest neighbors to objects.

rows.name: Knowledge-Grounded LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which incorporates external knowledge sources or knowledge bases into the model architecture, enabling it to generate more factually accurate and knowledge-aware text.

rows.name: Knowledge Transfer
rows.definition: A training strategy in which knowledge is passed from one entity such as a person organization or system to another facilitating learning and adaptation in the receiving entity through various methods such as teaching training or data exchange.

rows.name: Kohonen Network
rows.definition: A network that is an unsupervised technique producing a low-dimensional representation of high-dimensional data preserving topological structure.

rows.name: LPPool1D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that applies 1D power-average pooling over an input signal composed of several input planes.

rows.name: LPPool2D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that applies 2D power-average pooling over an input signal composed of several input planes.

rows.name: LSTMCell Layer
rows.definition: A layer that processes one step within the whole time sequence input for an LSTM layer.

rows.name: LSTM Layer
rows.definition: A recurrent layer that implements the Long Short-Term Memory architecture.

rows.name: Lambda Layer
rows.definition: A layer that wraps arbitrary expressions as a Layer object.

rows.name: Language Interface LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that supports interactive semantic parsing enabling users to provide feedback and corrections to dynamically refine and update the language model.

rows.name: Language Model
rows.definition: A model designed to predict the next word in a sequence or assign probabilities to sequences of words in natural language.

rows.name: Large Language Model
rows.definition: A language model consisting of a neural network with many parameters (typically billions of weights or more) trained on large quantities of unlabeled text using self-supervised learning or semi-supervised learning.

rows.name: Lasso Regression
rows.definition: A regression analysis that performs both variable selection and regularization to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability.

rows.name: Layer
rows.definition: A structure or network topology in a deep learning model that takes information from previous layers and passes it to the next layer.

rows.name: Layer Layer
rows.definition: A layer from which other layers can inherit.

rows.name: LayerNorm Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies Layer Normalization over a mini-batch of inputs.

rows.name: LayerNormalization Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies Layer Normalization over the inputs.

rows.name: LazyBatchNorm1D Layer
rows.definition: A batch normalization layer that lazily initializes the num_features argument from the input size for 1D data.

rows.name: LazyBatchNorm2D Layer
rows.definition: A batch normalization layer that lazily initializes the num_features argument from the input size for 2D data.

rows.name: LazyBatchNorm3D Layer
rows.definition: A batch normalization layer that lazily initializes the num_features argument from the input size for 3D data.

rows.name: LazyInstanceNorm1D Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that lazily initializes the num_features argument from the input size for 1D data.

rows.name: LazyInstanceNorm2D Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that lazily initializes the num_features argument from the input size for 2D data.

rows.name: LazyInstanceNorm3D Layer
rows.definition: A normalization that lazily initializes the num_features argument from the input size for 3D data.

rows.name: LeakyReLU Layer
rows.definition: An activation layer that applies the leaky rectified linear unit function element-wise.

rows.name: Least-squares Analysis
rows.definition: A regression analysis which approximates the solution of overdetermined systems by minimizing the sum of the squares of the residuals.

rows.name: Lifelong Learning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that continually acquires new knowledge over time without forgetting previously learned information maintaining a balance between plasticity and stability.

rows.name: Linear Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that has the form f(x) = a + bx.

rows.name: Linear Regression
rows.definition: A regression analysis that is a linear approach for modeling the relationship between a scalar response and one or more explanatory variables.

rows.name: Linking Bias
rows.definition: A use and interpretation bias arising when network attributes obtained from user connections activities or interactions misrepresent true user behavior.

rows.name: Liquid State Machine Network
rows.definition: A network that is a type of reservoir computer turning time-varying input into spatio-temporal activation patterns.

rows.name: LocalResponseNorm Layer
rows.definition: A normalization layer that applies local response normalization over an input signal composed of several input planes.

rows.name: LocallyConnected1D Layer
rows.definition: A locally-connected layer for 1D inputs where each patch of the input is convolved with a different set of filters.

rows.name: LocallyConnected2D Layer
rows.definition: A locally-connected layer for 2D inputs where each patch of the input is convolved with a different set of filters.

rows.name: Locally-connected Layer
rows.definition: A layer that works similarly to the Convolution1D layer, except that weights are unshared, that is, a different set of filters is applied at each different patch of the input.

rows.name: Logistic Regression
rows.definition: A regression analysis that estimates the probability of an event occurring by modeling the log-odds of the event as a linear combination of one or more independent variables.

rows.name: Long Short Term Memory
rows.definition: A recurrent neural network with feedback connections that processes entire sequences of data.

rows.name: Loss Of Situational Awareness Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias occurring when automation leads to humans being unaware of their situation making them unprepared to assume control in cooperative systems.

rows.name: Low-Resource LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which is optimized for performance in scenarios with limited data, computational resources, or for languages with sparse datasets.

rows.name: Machine Learning Task
rows.definition: A process intended to build methods that learn from data.

rows.name: Manifold Learning
rows.definition: A dimensionality reduction method based on the assumption that observed data lie on a low-dimensional manifold embedded in a higher-dimensional space.

rows.name: Markov Chain
rows.definition: A network that is a stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events where the probability of each event depends only on the previous event's state.

rows.name: Masked Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that is trained to predict randomly masked tokens in a sequence based on the remaining unmasked tokens allowing it to build deep bidirectional representations that can be effectively transferred to various NLP tasks via fine-tuning.

rows.name: Masking Layer
rows.definition: A layer that masks a sequence by using a mask value to skip timesteps.

rows.name: Matched Input-Output Layer
rows.definition: An input layer with a shape corresponding to that of the output layer.

rows.name: Mathematical Function
rows.definition: A mathematical rule that gives the value of a dependent variable corresponding to specified values of one or more independent variables.

rows.name: MaxPooling1D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs max pooling operation for temporal data.

rows.name: MaxPooling2D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs max pooling operation for spatial data.

rows.name: MaxPooling3D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that performs max pooling operation for 3D data (spatial or spatio-temporal).

rows.name: MaxUnpool1D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that computes a partial inverse of MaxPool1D.

rows.name: MaxUnpool2D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that computes a partial inverse of MaxPool2D.

rows.name: MaxUnpool3D Layer
rows.definition: A pooling layer that computes a partial inverse of MaxPool3D.

rows.name: Maximum Layer
rows.definition: A merging layer that computes the maximum (element-wise) of a list of inputs.

rows.name: Measurement Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising when features and labels are proxies for desired quantities potentially leading to differential performance.

rows.name: Memory-Augmented LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which incorporates external writable and readable memory components, allowing it to store and retrieve information over long contexts.

rows.name: Memory Cell Layer
rows.definition: A layer of cells, each with an internal state or weights.

rows.name: Merging Layer
rows.definition: A layer used to merge a list of inputs.

rows.name: Meta-Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task that automatically learns from metadata about machine learning experiments.

rows.name: Meta-Learning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which is trained in a way that allows it to quickly adapt to new tasks or datasets through only a few examples or fine-tuning steps, leveraging meta-learned priors about how to efficiently learn.

rows.name: Metric Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that learns a representation function mapping objects into an embedded space.

rows.name: Minimum Layer
rows.definition: A merging layer that computes the minimum (element-wise) of a list of inputs.

rows.name: Mixture-of-Experts LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which dynamically selects and combines outputs from multiple expert submodels, allowing for efficient scaling by conditionally activating only a subset of model components for each input.

rows.name: Mode Confusion Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias occurring when modal interfaces confuse human operators causing actions appropriate for a different mode but incorrect for the current situation.

rows.name: Model
rows.definition: An abstract representation of a complex system generally assembled as a set of logical mathematical or conceptual properties to simulate or understand the system's behavior.

rows.name: Model Selection Bias
rows.definition: A processing bias introduced when using data to select a single "best" model from many or when an explanatory variable has a weak relationship with the response variable.

rows.name: Modular LLM
rows.definition: A modular language model that consists of multiple specialized components or skills that can be dynamically composed and recombined to solve complex tasks mimicking the modular structure of human cognition.

rows.name: Modular Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that consists of multiple specialized components or skills that can be dynamically composed and recombined to solve complex tasks mimicking the modular structure of human cognition.

rows.name: MultiHeadAttention Layer
rows.definition: An attention layer that allows the model to attend to information from different representation subspaces.

rows.name: Multi-Task LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which is trained jointly on multiple language tasks simultaneously, learning shared representations that transfer across tasks.

rows.name: Multiclass Classification
rows.definition: A classification focused on methods that classify instances into one of three or more classes.

rows.name: Multidimensional Scaling
rows.definition: A dimensionality reduction method that translates information about the pairwise distances among a set of objects or individuals into a configuration of points mapped into an abstract Cartesian space.

rows.name: Multilingual LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is trained on text from multiple languages learning shared representations that enable zero-shot or few-shot transfer to new languages.

rows.name: Multimodal Deep Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that processes and links information using various modalities.

rows.name: Multimodal Fusion LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that learns joint representations across different modalities like text vision and audio in an end-to-end fashion for better cross-modal understanding and generation.

rows.name: Multimodal LLM
rows.definition: A multimodal large language model that learns joint representations across different modalities like text vision and audio in an end-to-end fashion for better cross-modal understanding and generation.

rows.name: Multimodal Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that learns joint representations across different modalities like text vision and audio in an end-to-end fashion for better cross-modal understanding and generation.

rows.name: Multimodal Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task that uses multiple modalities of data such as text audio and images to improve learning outcomes.

rows.name: Multimodal Prompt-based Language Model
rows.definition: A multimodal large language model which processes prompts that include multiple modalities, such as both text and images, to generate relevant responses.

rows.name: Multimodal Transformer
rows.definition: A transformer network that processes and relates information from different modalities such as text images and audio using a shared embedding space and attention mechanism to learn joint representations across modalities.

rows.name: Multiply Layer
rows.definition: A merging layer that multiplies (element-wise) a list of inputs.

rows.name: Natural Language Processing
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on the interactions between computers and human language including programming computers to process and analyze large amounts of natural language data.

rows.name: Network
rows.definition: A system of interconnected nodes or entities for communication, computation or data exchange.

rows.name: Neural Turing Machine Network
rows.definition: A deep feedforward network that combines neural network pattern matching with the algorithmic power of programmable computers.

rows.name: Neuro-Symbolic LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which combines neural language modeling with symbolic reasoning components, leveraging structured knowledge representations and logical inferences to improve reasoning capabilities.

rows.name: Noise Dense Layer
rows.definition: A layer that is a densely-connected neural network layer with added noise for regularization.

rows.name: Noisy Input Layer
rows.definition: An input layer that adds noise to each value.

rows.name: Normalization
rows.definition: A data preparation that transforms data into a standard format or scale typically to reduce redundancy and improve consistency often involving the adjustment of values measured on different scales to a common scale.

rows.name: Normalization Layer
rows.definition: A numerical features preprocessing layer that normalizes continuous features.

rows.name: Numerical Features Preprocessing Layer
rows.definition: A layer that performs numerical data preprocessing operations.

rows.name: One-shot Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that classifies objects from one or only a few examples.

rows.name: Ordinal LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is trained to model ordinal relationships and rank outputs rather than model probability distributions over text sequences directly.

rows.name: Output Layer
rows.definition: A layer containing the last neurons in the network that produces given outputs for the program.

rows.name: PReLU Layer
rows.definition: An activation layer that applies parametric rectified linear unit function element-wise.

rows.name: Perceptron
rows.definition: An artificial neural network with a supervised learning algorithm for binary classification using a linear predictor function.

rows.name: Permute Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that permutes the dimensions of the input according to a given pattern.

rows.name: Personalized LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that adapts its language modeling and generation to the preferences style and persona of individual users or audiences.

rows.name: Policy Layer
rows.definition: A layer that, after taking a set of states or values as input, predicts a probability distribution of actions to take.

rows.name: Pooling Layer
rows.definition: A layer that serves to mitigate the sensitivity of convolutional layers to location and spatially downsample representations.

rows.name: Popularity Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias where more popular items are more exposed under-representing less popular items.

rows.name: Population Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias characterized by systematic distortions in demographics or other user characteristics between represented users and the target population.

rows.name: Preprocessing
rows.definition: A process applied to raw data before it is used in a machine learning model, including tasks such as normalization, scaling, encoding, and transformation, to ensure the data is in an appropriate format and quality for analysis.

rows.name: Preprocessing Layer
rows.definition: A layer that performs data preprocessing operations.

rows.name: Presentation Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias arising from how information is presented on the Web via a user interface due to rating or ranking of output or through users' self-selected biased interaction.

rows.name: Principal Component Analysis
rows.definition: A dimensionality reduction method for analyzing large datasets with high-dimensional features per observation increasing data interpretability while preserving maximum information and enabling visualization.

rows.name: Probabilistic Graphical Model
rows.definition: A machine learning task in which a graph expresses the conditional dependence structure between random variables.

rows.name: Probabilistic Hidden Layer
rows.definition: A hidden layer that estimates the probability of a sample being within a certain category.

rows.name: Probabilistic Topic Model
rows.definition: A probabilistic graphical model that uses statistical techniques to analyze the words in each text to discover common themes their connections and their changes over time.

rows.name: Processing Bias
rows.definition: A computational bias resulting from judgment modulated by affect influenced by the level of efficacy and efficiency in information processing.

rows.name: Prompt-based Fine-Tuning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which is fine-tuned on a small number of examples or prompts, rather than full task datasets. This allows for rapid adaptation to new tasks with limited data, leveraging the model's few-shot learning capabilities.

rows.name: Proportional Hazards Model
rows.definition: A regression analysis for survival analysis where the unique effect of a unit increase in a covariate is multiplicative with respect to the hazard rate.

rows.name: RNN Layer
rows.definition: The base class for recurrent layers.

rows.name: Radial Basis Network
rows.definition: A deep feedforward network that uses radial basis functions as activation functions for pattern recognition and interpolation.

rows.name: RandomBrightness Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly adjusts brightness during training.

rows.name: RandomContrast Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly adjusts contrast during training.

rows.name: RandomCrop Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly crops images during training.

rows.name: Random Effects Model
rows.definition: A regression analysis where the model parameters are random variables.

rows.name: RandomFlip Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly flips images during training.

rows.name: Random Forest
rows.definition: An ensemble learning method for classification regression and other tasks that constructs a multitude of decision trees during training.

rows.name: RandomHeight Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly varies image height during training.

rows.name: RandomRotation Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly rotates images during training.

rows.name: RandomTranslation Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly translates images during training.

rows.name: RandomWidth Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly varies image width during training.

rows.name: RandomZoom Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that randomly zooms in or out on images during training.

rows.name: Ranking Bias
rows.definition: An anchoring bias characterized by the idea that top-ranked results are the most relevant and important leading to more clicks than other results.

rows.name: Rashomon Effect Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias characterized by differences in perspective memory recall interpretation and reporting of the same event by multiple persons or witnesses.

rows.name: ReLU Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that returns max(x 0) the element-wise maximum of 0 and the input tensor.

rows.name: ReLU Layer
rows.definition: An activation layer that applies the rectified linear unit function element-wise.

rows.name: Reasoning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that incorporates explicit reasoning capabilities leveraging logical rules axioms or external knowledge to make deductive inferences during language tasks.

rows.name: Recurrent Layer
rows.definition: A layer composed of recurrent units with the number equal to the hidden size of the layer.

rows.name: Recurrent Neural Network
rows.definition: A network with connections forming a directed graph along a temporal sequence enabling dynamic behavior.

rows.name: Recursive LLM
rows.definition: A language model that uses recursive neural network architectures like TreeLSTMs to learn syntactic composition functions improving systematic generalization abilities.

rows.name: Recursive Language Model
rows.definition: A deep neural network that uses recursive neural network architectures like TreeLSTMs to learn syntactic composition functions improving systematic generalization abilities.

rows.name: Recursive Neural Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network that recursively applies weights over structured input to generate structured or scalar predictions.

rows.name: Regression Analysis
rows.definition: A set of statistical processes for estimating the relationships between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.

rows.name: Regularization Layer
rows.definition: A layer that applies penalties on layer parameters or layer activity during optimization summed into the loss function that the network optimizes.

rows.name: Reinforcement Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods that do not require labeled input/output pairs or explicit correction of sub-optimal actions focusing instead on balancing exploration and exploitation to optimize performance over time.

rows.name: Reinforcement Learning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is fine-tuned using reinforcement learning where the model receives rewards for generating text that satisfies certain desired properties or objectives improving the quality safety or alignment of generated text.

rows.name: RepeatVector Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that repeats the input n times.

rows.name: Representation Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias due to non-random sampling of subgroups making trends non-generalizable to new populations.

rows.name: Representation Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that discovers representations required for feature detection or classification from raw data.

rows.name: Rescaling Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that rescales input values to a new range.

rows.name: Reshape Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that reshapes the inputs into the given shape.

rows.name: Reshaping Layer
rows.definition: A layer that is used to change the shape of the input.

rows.name: Residual Neural Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network that employs skip connections to bypass layers facilitating learning of residual functions.

rows.name: Resizing Layer
rows.definition: An image preprocessing layer that resizes images to a target size.

rows.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine
rows.definition: A Boltzmann machine network that learns the probability distribution of its input data.

rows.name: Retrieval-Augmented LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which combines a pre-trained language model with a retrieval system that can access external knowledge sources. This allows the model to condition its generation on relevant retrieved knowledge, improving factual accuracy and knowledge grounding.

rows.name: Ridge Regression
rows.definition: A regression analysis that estimates the coefficients of multiple regression models in scenarios where the independent variables are highly correlated.

rows.name: SELU Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that multiplies scale (> 1) with the output of the ELU function to ensure a slope larger than one for positive inputs.

rows.name: Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving-Average
rows.definition: A model that extends ARIMA, explicitly supporting univariate time series data with a seasonal component, combining seasonal differencing with ARIMA modeling.

rows.name: Selection And Sampling Bias
rows.definition: A computational bias introduced by non-random selection of individuals groups or data failing to ensure representativeness.

rows.name: Selective Adherence Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias characterized by the tendency to selectively adopt algorithmic advice that matches pre-existing beliefs and stereotypes.

rows.name: Self-Supervised LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which learns rich representations by solving pretext tasks that involve predicting parts of the input from other observed parts of the data, without relying on human-annotated labels.

rows.name: Self-supervised Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task that is intermediate between supervised and unsupervised learning and predicts parts of the input data from other observed parts without relying on human-annotated labels.

rows.name: Semi-Supervised LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which combines self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled data with supervised fine-tuning on labeled task data.

rows.name: SeparableConvolution1D Layer
rows.definition: A convolutional layer that performs depthwise separable 1D convolution.

rows.name: SeparableConvolution2D Layer
rows.definition: A convolutional layer that performs depthwise separable 2D convolution.

rows.name: Sigmoid Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that applies the sigmoid activation function sigmoid(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(-x)) always returning a value between 0 and 1.

rows.name: SimpleRNNCell Layer
rows.definition: A layer that processes one step within the whole time sequence input for a SimpleRNN layer.

rows.name: SimpleRNN Layer
rows.definition: A recurrent layer that implements a fully-connected RNN where the output is to be fed back to input.

rows.name: Simpson's Paradox Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias where the association between two variables changes when controlling for another variable.

rows.name: Societal Bias
rows.definition: A systemic bias characterized by being for or against groups or individuals based on social identities demographic factors or immutable physical characteristics often manifesting as stereotypes.

rows.name: Softmax Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function where the elements of the output vector are in range (0 1) and sum to 1 and each vector is handled independently.

rows.name: Softmax Layer
rows.definition: An activation layer that applies the softmax function to the inputs.

rows.name: Softplus Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that is softplus(x) = log(exp(x) + 1).

rows.name: Softsign Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that is softsign(x) = x / (abs(x) + 1).

rows.name: Sparse Auto Encoder
rows.definition: An autoencoder network with more hidden units than inputs that constrains only a few hidden units to be active at once.

rows.name: Sparse LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that uses techniques like pruning or quantization to reduce the number of non-zero parameters in the model making it more parameter-efficient and easier to deploy on resource-constrained devices.

rows.name: Sparse Learning
rows.definition: A representation learning network that finds sparse representations of input data as a linear combination of basic elements and identifies those elements.

rows.name: SpatialDropout1D Layer
rows.definition: A regularization layer that performs the same function as Dropout but drops entire 1D feature maps instead of individual elements.

rows.name: SpatialDropout2D Layer
rows.definition: A regularization layer that performs the same function as Dropout but drops entire 2D feature maps instead of individual elements.

rows.name: SpatialDropout3D Layer
rows.definition: A regularization layer that performs the same function as Dropout but drops entire 3D feature maps instead of individual elements.

rows.name: Spatial Regression
rows.definition: A regression analysis used to model spatial relationships.

rows.name: Spiking Hidden Layer
rows.definition: A hidden layer that makes connections to an additional, heterogeneous hidden layer; modeled after biological neural networks.

rows.name: StackedRNNCells Layer
rows.definition: A layer that allows a stack of RNN cells to behave as a single cell.

rows.name: Streetlight Effect Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias where people search only where it is easiest to look.

rows.name: StringLookup Layer
rows.definition: A categorical features preprocessing layer that maps string features to integer indices.

rows.name: Subtract Layer
rows.definition: A merging layer that subtracts two inputs.

rows.name: Subword Segmentation
rows.definition: A data preparation that divides text into subword units which are smaller than words but larger than individual characters to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of natural language processing models by capturing meaningful subunits of words.

rows.name: Sunk Cost Fallacy Bias
rows.definition: A bias characterized by the tendency to continue an endeavor due to previously invested resources despite costs outweighing benefits.

rows.name: Supervised Biclustering
rows.definition: A biclustering task focused on methods that simultaneously cluster the rows and columns of a labeled matrix considering data labels to enhance cluster coherence.

rows.name: Supervised Clustering
rows.definition: A clustering focused on methods that group labeled objects such that objects in the same group have similar labels relative to those in other groups.

rows.name: Supervised Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods that learn a function mapping input to output based on example input-output pairs.

rows.name: Support Vector Machine
rows.definition: A network with supervised learning models for classification and regression that maps training examples to points in space maximizing the gap between categories.

rows.name: Survival Analysis
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods for analyzing the expected duration of time until one or more events occur such as death in biological organisms or failure in mechanical systems.

rows.name: Survivorship Bias
rows.definition: A processing bias characterized by the tendency to focus on items observations or people that "survive" a selection process overlooking those that did not.

rows.name: Swish Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that is x*sigmoid(x) a smooth non-monotonic function that consistently matches or outperforms ReLU on deep networks.

rows.name: Symmetrically Connected Network
rows.definition: A network that is a type of recurrent neural network where connections between units are symmetrical with equal weights in both directions.

rows.name: SyncBatchNorm Layer
rows.definition: A batch normalization layer that applies synchronous Batch Normalization across multiple devices.

rows.name: Systemic Bias
rows.definition: A bias resulting from procedures and practices of systems that operate in ways which result in certain social groups being advantaged or favored and others being disadvantaged or devalued.

rows.name: Tanh Function
rows.definition: A mathematical function that is the hyperbolic tangent activation function.

rows.name: Temporal Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising from differences in populations and behaviors over time.

rows.name: Text Preprocessing Layer
rows.definition: A layer that performs text data preprocessing operations.

rows.name: TextVectorization Layer
rows.definition: A text preprocessing layer that maps text features to integer sequences.

rows.name: Threshold Autoregressive
rows.definition: A model that allows for different autoregressive processes depending on the regime or state of the time series, enabling the capture of nonlinear behaviors.

rows.name: ThresholdedReLU Layer
rows.definition: An activation layer that applies the thresholded rectified linear unit function element-wise.

rows.name: TimeDistributed Layer
rows.definition: A recurrent layer that applies a layer to every temporal slice of an input.

rows.name: Time Series Analysis
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods for analyzing time series data to extract meaningful statistics and characteristics.

rows.name: Time Series Forecasting
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods that predict future values based on previously observed values.

rows.name: Tokenization
rows.definition: A data preparation that converts a sequence of text into smaller meaningful units called tokens typically words or subwords for the purpose of analysis or processing by language models.

rows.name: TrainingStrategy
rows.definition: A preprocessing used to train machine learning models including techniques such as supervised learning unsupervised learning reinforcement learning and transfer learning aimed at optimizing model performance.

rows.name: Transfer Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on methods that reuse or transfer information from previously learned tasks to facilitate the learning of new tasks.

rows.name: Transfer Learning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that leverages knowledge acquired during training on one task to improve performance on different but related tasks facilitating more efficient learning and adaptation.

rows.name: Transformer LLM
rows.definition: A transformer language model with large training corpuses and sets of parameters that uses the transformer architecture based on multi-head attention mechanisms allowing it to contextualize tokens within a context window for effective language understanding and generation.

rows.name: Transformer Language Model
rows.definition: A language model that uses the transformer architecture based on multi-head attention mechanisms allowing it to contextualize tokens within a context window for effective language understanding and generation.

rows.name: Transformer Network
rows.definition: A deep neural network that utilizes attention mechanisms to weigh the significance of input data.

rows.name: Uncertainty Bias
rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias favoring groups better represented in training data due to less prediction uncertainty.

rows.name: UnitNormalization Layer
rows.definition: A recurrent layer that normalizes a batch of inputs so that each input in the batch has a L2 norm equal to 1.

rows.name: Unsupervised Biclustering
rows.definition: A biclustering task focused on methods that simultaneously cluster the rows and columns of an unlabeled input matrix to identify submatrices with coherent patterns.

rows.name: Unsupervised Clustering
rows.definition: A clustering focused on methods that group a set of unlabeled objects such that objects in the same group are more similar to each other than to those in other groups.

rows.name: Unsupervised LLM
rows.definition: A large language model that is trained solely on unlabeled data using self-supervised objectives like masked language modeling without any supervised fine-tuning.

rows.name: Unsupervised Learning
rows.definition: A machine learning task focused on algorithms that learn patterns from unlabeled data.

rows.name: Unsupervised Pretrained Network
rows.definition: A network that initializes a discriminative neural net from one trained using an unsupervised criterion.

rows.name: UpSampling1D Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that upsamples the input by repeating each temporal step size times along the time axis.

rows.name: UpSampling2D Layer
rows.definition: A layer that upsamples the input by repeating each row and column size times.

rows.name: UpSampling3D Layer
rows.definition: A layer that upsamples the input by repeating each depth, height and width size times.

rows.name: Use And Interpretation Bias
rows.definition: A computational bias characterized by inappropriately analyzing ambiguous stimuli scenarios and events.

rows.name: User Interaction Bias
rows.definition: An individual bias arising when a user imposes their own biases during interaction with data output results etc.

rows.name: Variational Auto Encoder
rows.definition: An autoencoder network that imposes a probabilistic structure on the latent space for unsupervised learning.

rows.name: Vector Autoregression
rows.definition: A model that captures the linear interdependencies among multiple time series, where each variable is modeled as a linear function of its own past values and the past values of all other variables in the system.

rows.name: Vocabulary Reduction
rows.definition: A data preparation that limits the number of unique tokens in a language model's vocabulary by merging or eliminating less frequent tokens thereby optimizing computational efficiency and resource usage.

rows.name: Weighted Layer
rows.definition: A layer of values to be applied to other cells or neurons in a network.

rows.name: Wrapper Layer
rows.definition: A layer that augment the functionality of another layer.

rows.name: ZeroPadding1D Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that zero-pads the input along the time axis.

rows.name: ZeroPadding2D Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that zero-pads the input along the height and width dimensions.

rows.name: ZeroPadding3D Layer
rows.definition: A reshaping layer that zero-pads the input along the depth, height and width dimensions.

rows.name: Zero-Shot Learning LLM
rows.definition: A large language model which performs tasks or understands concepts it has not explicitly been trained on, demonstrating a high degree of generalization and understanding.

rows.name: Zero-shot Learning
rows.definition: A deep neural network that predicts classes at test time from classes not observed during training.

rows.name: node2vec
rows.definition: A machine learning task designed to learn continuous feature representations for nodes in a graph by optimizing a neighborhood-preserving objective.

rows.name: node2vec-CBOW
rows.definition: A node2vec that predicts the current node from a window of surrounding context nodes, with the order of context nodes not influencing prediction.

rows.name: node2vec-SkipGram
rows.definition: A node2vec that uses the current node to predict the surrounding window of context nodes, weighing nearby context nodes more heavily than distant ones.

rows.name: t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor embedding
rows.definition: A dimensionality reduction for visualizing high-dimensional data by giving each datapoint a location in a two or three-dimensional map.

rows.name: word2vec
rows.definition: A machine learning task that generates distributed representations of words by training a shallow neural network model, which aims to predict the context of each word within a corpus. This algorithm captures semantic meanings of words through their contextual usage in the text.

rows.name: word2vec-CBOW
rows.definition: A word2vec that predicts the current word from a window of surrounding context words, ignoring the order of context words.

rows.name: word2vec-SkipGram
rows.definition: A word2vec that predicts surrounding context words from the current word, giving more weight to nearby context words than distant ones.

rows.name: ABRA-s-fix fixed-sample betweenness approximation
rows.definition: A fixed-sample static-graph betweenness algorithm that averages shortest-path fractions over a user-specified number of uniform endpoint pairs and returns both the estimates and a simultaneous Rademacher-based additive error bound, regardless of the size of that bound.

rows.name: ABRA-s progressive betweenness approximation
rows.definition: A progressive sampling algorithm for static-graph betweenness that averages fractions of shortest paths through each node over uniformly sampled endpoint pairs and checks a predetermined sequence of sample sizes and stops when a Rademacher-based simultaneous error bound meets the requested additive tolerance.

rows.name: AMSGrad
rows.definition: An Adam variant that normalizes first-moment updates with the coordinatewise historical maximum of second-moment estimates.

rows.name: AND/OR abstraction sampling
rows.definition: An importance-sampling algorithm for partition functions of discrete graphical models that samples representatives in a pseudo-tree-guided AND/OR search space, allowing abstractions across branching-ancestor contexts through interleaved ancestor pruning and relative-weight value backup.

rows.name: A-star search
rows.definition: A heuristic graph-search method that selects an open node using the sum of its best known path cost from the start and an estimated remaining cost to a goal.

rows.name: Absolute threshold pruning for sequence beams
rows.definition: A sequence-beam pruning procedure that first applies the beam-size cap, then discards candidates whose score is at least a specified positive margin below the best score in that capped candidate list.

identities.value: Absolute threshold pruning for sequence beams

rows.name: Accelerated graph degree linkage
rows.definition: An approximate graph degree linkage algorithm that selects merges from maintained cluster-neighbor sets and updates those sets locally instead of searching every current cluster pair.

rows.name: Activation-Value Gaussian Pooling
rows.definition: A parameterized neural pooling unit that averages a group of transformed activations using normalized Gaussian-kernel weights determined by each activation’s distance from a learned pool mean.

rows.name: AdaBoost
rows.definition: Boosting that reweights training observations according to prior prediction errors.

rows.name: AdaMax
rows.definition: An Adam-family optimizer using an exponentially weighted infinity-norm gradient scale instead of a second raw moment denominator.

rows.name: AdaMixUp
rows.definition: An adaptive interpolation-training procedure that learns example-dependent mixing-coefficient regions with a policy network and trains a classifier together with an intrusion discriminator intended to separate mixed examples from original data.

rows.name: Adadelta
rows.definition: An adaptive gradient optimization method that rescales gradients using exponentially weighted squared-gradient and squared-update histories.

rows.name: Adafactor
rows.definition: An adaptive gradient optimization method that approximates matrix-valued second-moment statistics using row and column factors.

rows.name: Adagrad
rows.definition: An adaptive gradient optimization method that scales each coordinate's update using accumulated squared gradients.

rows.name: Adam
rows.definition: Stochastic gradient optimization using bias-corrected exponential estimates of first and second gradient moments to scale parameter updates.

rows.name: AdamNC
rows.definition: An Adam-family optimization method that uses time-dependent first- and second-moment decay schedules.

rows.name: AdamW
rows.definition: An Adam optimization variant that applies weight decay directly to parameters separately from gradient moment estimation.

rows.name: Adaptive Alternating Minimization
rows.definition: A two-coordinate minimization procedure that performs one exact alternating sweep over a newly supplied pair of feasible sets at each iteration, aiming at the optimum of their limiting sets.

rows.name: Adaptive Deconvolutional Network
rows.definition: An unsupervised hierarchical image-representation architecture that alternates convolutional sparse synthesis with spatial and cross-map pooling switches and fits each layer through a reconstruction path to the original image.

rows.name: Adaptive Metropolis
rows.definition: A history-adaptive random-walk Metropolis sampler whose Gaussian proposal covariance is estimated from the accumulated retained states, including repetitions after rejected proposals.

rows.name: Adaptive parallel tempering
rows.definition: A parallel-tempering algorithm that adapts temperature gaps and within-replica random-walk proposal parameters through projected stochastic approximation.

rows.name: Adaptive rejection sampling
rows.definition: The Gilks–Wild univariate rejection sampler that uses tangents to a concave log density as a piecewise-linear upper hull and chords as a lower hull, updating these bounds from evaluated proposals.

rows.name: Adaptive scaling Metropolis
rows.definition: A random-walk Metropolis algorithm that adapts its proposal scale through stochastic approximation driven by the proposal acceptance probability relative to a chosen target rate.

rows.name: Adaptive scaling within adaptive Metropolis
rows.definition: An adaptive Metropolis algorithm that combines acceptance-rate-driven scalar proposal scaling with recursive mean and covariance-shape adaptation from retained samples.

rows.name: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields
rows.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family that draws each document from a proper Poisson-MRF base distribution whose canonical unary and interaction parameters are convex combinations of topic parameters under document-specific simplex weights.

identities.value: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields

rows.name: Alternating Expectation Conditional Maximization
rows.definition: A likelihood-optimization framework that alternates cycles of expectation and constrained maximization, permitting the admissible data augmentation and constraint functions to change between cycles while collectively covering the parameter directions.
