rows.name: Alternating Kullback-Leibler Minimization
rows.definition: A paired-distribution optimization procedure that alternately minimizes Kullback-Leibler divergence in its first and second arguments over specified convex probability families.

rows.name: Analytic moment-based Gaussian-process filtering
rows.definition: A Gaussian assumed-density filtering algorithm that uses trained squared-exponential Gaussian-process transition and measurement models, analytically matches predictive moments under Gaussian state inputs, and conditions a moment-matched Gaussian approximation to the joint state/measurement distribution to update the hidden-state estimate.

rows.name: Ancestral Gumbel-Top-k sampling
rows.definition: An exact without-replacement sampler for finite discrete Bayesian-network configurations that propagates conditional Gumbel subtree maxima through a bounded priority frontier, with a configurable number of parallel expansions and parent-respecting variable selection.

rows.name: Annealed importance sampling
rows.definition: A Monte Carlo estimation algorithm that draws from a tractable base distribution, applies Markov transitions invariant for a prescribed sequence of intermediate distributions, and weights each resulting path by successive unnormalized-density ratios to estimate target expectations and normalizing-constant ratios.

rows.name: Ant colony optimization
rows.definition: A metaheuristic framework for optimization in which artificial ants construct solutions using local information and communicate indirectly through shared pheromone information that is adapted from their search experience.

rows.name: Ant Colony System
rows.definition: An ant-colony optimization algorithm that combines a greedy-or-proportional construction rule, local pheromone updates during construction, and global pheromone updates restricted to a selected best tour.

rows.name: AntNet
rows.definition: A distributed adaptive routing algorithm in which forward agents sample network paths and backward agents use the measured trip times to update local traffic models and probabilistic routing tables.

rows.name: Ant-Q
rows.definition: A family of cooperative ant-based optimization algorithms that learns shared edge desirabilities using Q-learning-inspired next-state estimates and delayed reinforcement from completed solutions.

rows.name: Ant System
rows.definition: A constructive combinatorial optimization method in which artificial ants sample solution components using shared pheromone trails and problem-specific heuristic information, then modify those trails through reinforcement and evaporation.

rows.name: Apriori
rows.definition: Frequent-itemset mining using breadth-first candidate enumeration and support-based pruning.

rows.name: Asynchronous Successive Halving
rows.definition: An asynchronous resource-allocation algorithm that promotes promising completed hyperparameter trials through increasing resource levels as workers become available and starts new trials when no eligible promotion is available, without waiting for an entire evaluation stage to finish.

rows.name: Attention-Based Configurable Convolutional Neural Network
rows.definition: A visual-question-answering architecture that derives a convolution kernel from an encoded question to compute normalized spatial attention, then fuses weighted and unweighted image features with the question for answer-word classification.

rows.name: Attention-Based Convolutional Neural Network
rows.definition: A sentence-pair neural architecture that uses cross-sentence distance affinities to add attention feature channels before convolution, reweight local pooling after convolution, or combine both stages when deriving pair-dependent sentence representations.

rows.name: Attention-based Dropout Layer
rows.definition: A training-time convolutional feature-map layer that stochastically applies either a thresholded spatial drop mask or sigmoid importance weights derived from channel-averaged activations, developed for weakly supervised object localization.

rows.name: Attentive Pooling Network
rows.definition: A neural sentence-pair architecture that learns bilinear segment interactions, derives attention by row and column maxima followed by separate softmax normalization, and compares the resulting pair-conditioned pooled representations for answer selection.

rows.name: Author-persona-topic model
rows.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family in which each author has a mixture of personas, each persona has a topic distribution, and one persona shared across a document generates its token topics.

rows.name: Author-recipient-topic model
rows.definition: A generative message model with a topic distribution for each ordered sender-recipient pair, in which each word selects a recipient uniformly from the message's observed recipient set, a topic from that pair, and a word from the selected topic.

rows.name: Author-topic model
rows.definition: A generative document model in which each author has a shared topic-proportion distribution and each word is produced by uniformly selecting an author from the document's observed author set, selecting a topic from that author, and selecting a word from that topic.

rows.name: AutoAugment
rows.definition: An automated augmentation-policy search procedure that trains a controller to propose image-transform subpolicies and rewards those proposals using validation accuracy of a child model trained with the proposed augmentation.

rows.name: Auto-binomial Markov random field
rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for bounded site counts whose full conditionals are binomial with fixed trial counts and log odds linear in neighboring counts, using symmetric interaction coefficients.

rows.name: Auto-exponential Markov random field
rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for nonnegative continuous site values with exponential full conditionals whose rates are positive baseline terms plus nonnegative symmetric linear neighbor interactions.

rows.name: Auto-normal Markov random field
rows.definition: A proper finite Gaussian Markov-field model specified by linear full-conditional means and positive, value-independent site conditional variances, with compatibility enforced by a symmetric positive-definite joint precision matrix.

rows.name: Auto-Poisson Markov random field
rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for unbounded nonnegative integer counts whose full conditionals are Poisson with log means linear in neighboring counts and whose symmetric interaction coefficients are nonpositive.

rows.name: Autoregressive conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture that models each current vector with a conditional RBM whose visible and hidden biases are affine functions of a fixed window of preceding observed vectors, without hidden-to-hidden temporal links.

rows.name: Averaged stochastic gradient descent
rows.definition: A stochastic gradient optimization method that maintains an average of parameter iterates in addition to the current iterate.

rows.name: BIRCH
rows.definition: Clustering that compresses observations into a clustering-feature tree for subsequent grouping.

identities.value: Balanced Iterative Reducing and Clustering using Hierarchies

rows.name: BOHB
rows.definition: A hyperparameter optimization algorithm combining Hyperband resource brackets with model-guided configuration proposals from performance-split multivariate kernel density estimates and a continuing random-sampling component.

rows.name: Beam search using limited discrepancy backtracking
rows.definition: A memory-bounded beam search that explores heuristic-ranked slices using increasing limited-discrepancy budgets and removes backtracked slices so that alternative beams can be examined.

identities.value: Beam search using limited discrepancy backtracking

rows.name: Backpropagation through time
rows.definition: A reverse differentiation algorithm that computes derivatives of a finite dynamic-system objective by propagating adjoints backward through its time-unfolded computation and accumulating contributions for shared parameters.

rows.name: Bagging
rows.definition: Ensemble learning that aggregates predictors trained on bootstrap samples.

rows.name: Balanced Attention Mechanism
rows.definition: A convolutional feature-gating component for single-image super-resolution that computes average-pooled channel attention and maximum-pooled spatial attention in parallel, multiplies their sigmoid gates by broadcasting, and scales the input feature tensor.

rows.name: Balanced largest differencing method
rows.definition: A two-way number-partitioning heuristic that first differences disjoint adjacent pairs in the sorted original list, then repeatedly differences the two largest residuals, preserving subset cardinalities that differ by at most one.

rows.name: Ball vector machine
rows.definition: An approximate SVM training procedure that uses fixed-radius enclosing-ball center updates in a transformed kernel feature space, with multiscale tolerance and radius-refinement variants that avoid CVM’s repeated core quadratic programs.

rows.name: Barber–Agakov mutual information bound
rows.definition: A variational lower bound on mutual information formed by adding input entropy to the expected log probability assigned by a normalized conditional decoder to the input given the output.

rows.name: Barker acceptance rule
rows.definition: An acceptance-probability rule for reversible Monte Carlo proposals that uses R/(1+R), where R is the target-density ratio times the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio.

rows.name: Barlow Twins
rows.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that trains shared encoder and projection networks to make the cross-correlation of two batches of augmented-view embeddings close to the identity, penalizing diagonal mismatch and off-diagonal correlation.

rows.name: BasicILS
rows.definition: A ParamILS algorithm-configuration method that compares candidate configurations using cost estimates on the same fixed number of target-algorithm runs, paired by problem instance and random seed.

rows.name: Basis pursuit
rows.definition: A signal-representation optimization principle that minimizes the L1 norm of real synthesis coefficients subject to exact reconstruction of a supplied signal from a fixed finite dictionary.

rows.name: Batch reciprocal-nearest-neighbor agglomeration
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering procedure that alternates finding reciprocal nearest-neighbor pairs across the current clusters with merging a batch of such pairs and updating cluster dissimilarities, rather than choosing one globally closest pair or extending a reusable nearest-neighbor chain.

rows.name: Bayesian Data Augmentation for Deep Models
rows.definition: Tran et al.’s supervised deep-learning procedure that treats synthetic labeled examples as latent data, repeatedly samples them from an evolving learned model and updates model parameters through a generalized Monte Carlo expectation-maximization formulation.

identities.value: Bayesian Data Augmentation for Deep Models

rows.name: Breadth-first beam search
rows.definition: A heuristic search procedure that advances by depth layers, retaining at most a chosen beam width of the best-ranked candidate nodes for each next layer and discarding the other candidates.

rows.name: Beam-stack search
rows.definition: A layer-based beam search augmented with a stack of admitted evaluation ranges so that backtracking systematically revisits successors previously discarded by beam-width pruning.

rows.name: Best-first search
rows.definition: A search strategy that repeatedly expands the open node with the best value under a specified evaluation rule, adding eligible successors to the open frontier.

rows.name: Binary Multiple Kernel Maximum Margin Clustering
rows.definition: A two-class unsupervised clustering procedure that jointly fits a nonnegative multiple-kernel combination and absolute-margin classifier using cutting-plane constraints and constrained concave-convex updates.

identities.value: Binary Multiple Kernel Maximum Margin Clustering

rows.name: Bivariate counterfactual-fairness sensitivity analysis
rows.definition: A model-based sensitivity procedure that varies the correlation between two structural error terms and measures how a predictor built under an unconfounded additive-noise model changes on counterfactual data generated under the alternative confounded model.

rows.name: Black box variational inference
rows.definition: A variational-inference procedure that estimates evidence-lower-bound gradients from samples of a tractable variational distribution using its score function and model log joint, with mean-field local signals and score control variates to manage estimator variance.

rows.name: Blahut-Arimoto Rate-Distortion Algorithm
rows.definition: An alternating channel-and-marginal minimization algorithm for a fixed-source rate-distortion problem at a specified nonnegative distortion multiplier.

rows.name: Boltzmann chain
rows.definition: A family of tied-weight undirected Boltzmann sequence models with hidden temporal variables, observed variables and chain-derived connectivity chosen to permit exact elimination.

rows.name: Boosting
rows.definition: Ensemble learning that sequentially adds learners to improve an existing predictor.

rows.name: Bootstrap classifier-instability novelty detection
rows.definition: A novelty-detection procedure that trains classifiers on bootstrap resamples of reference data, estimates the variance of their outputs at a query, and rejects queries with unusually high variability relative to a chosen reference-score threshold.

rows.name: Bootstrap Your Own Latent
rows.definition: A self-supervised image representation-learning procedure that trains an online predictor to match a stopped-gradient target projection from another augmented view, while updating the target encoder and projector by exponential moving averages.

rows.name: Bottleneck Attention Module
rows.definition: A convolutional feature refinement component that combines parallel channel and spatial attention branches and adds the resulting gated features back to its input, originally proposed for network downsampling bottlenecks.

rows.name: Bounded adaptive reward for sequence scoring
rows.definition: A beam-dependent sequence rescoring rule that adds per-step rewards derived from the beam’s mean negative log token probability, accumulating them only up to a predicted output-length cap.

identities.value: Bounded adaptive reward for sequence scoring

rows.name: Bounded length reward for sequence scoring
rows.definition: A sequence scoring rule that adds a fixed nonnegative reward per generated position up to a finite length cap, giving score S(y)+r·min(l,|y|) instead of rewarding every additional position without bound.

identities.value: Bounded length reward for sequence scoring

rows.name: Brandes betweenness centrality computation
rows.definition: An exact graph algorithm for computing shortest-path vertex betweenness that combines single-source shortest-path counting with reverse-distance accumulation of dependencies, avoiding explicit summation of every source-target-vertex contribution.

rows.name: Brandes–Fleischer current-flow betweenness computation
rows.definition: An exact network-analysis algorithm that computes current-flow betweenness by forming grounded-Laplacian current-response rows, sorting each edge row, and aggregating rank-weighted contributions with endpoint correction instead of explicitly enumerating all source–sink pairs.

rows.name: Brandes–Fleischer grounded current-flow closeness computation
rows.definition: An exact network-analysis algorithm that accumulates effective-resistance sums from successive columns of an embedded grounded-Laplacian inverse and returns their reciprocals; the inspected Algorithm 2 omits the n-1 normalization used in the same chapter’s closeness definition.

rows.name: Brandes–Fleischer sampled-pair current-flow betweenness
rows.definition: A randomized network-analysis algorithm that estimates normalized, endpoint-excluded current-flow betweenness by independently sampling uniform source–sink pairs, solving their grounded electrical-network systems, and averaging scaled vertex throughputs.

rows.name: Brandes–Pich pivot-based centrality estimation
rows.definition: A network-analysis procedure that estimates shortest-path closeness and betweenness from single-source computations at a selected subset of pivot vertices, aggregating distances or source dependencies and comparing the resulting relative centrality scores.

rows.name: Breadth-first branch-and-bound search
rows.definition: A heuristic graph-search procedure that expands states in breadth-first layers and prunes candidate paths whose accumulated cost plus an admissible remaining-cost estimate exceeds a supplied solution-cost bound; the formulation curated here assumes uniform positive edge costs, scaled to one.

rows.name: Breadth-first iterative-deepening A-star
rows.definition: An iterative-deepening heuristic graph-search algorithm that repeatedly runs breadth-first branch-and-bound within increasing hypothetical f=g+h cost bounds, beginning at the start-state f value, until a solution is found; the curated formulation uses unit edge costs and a nonnegative admissible heuristic with h(goal)=0.

rows.name: Breadth-first search
rows.definition: A graph or state-space traversal that expands vertices in nondecreasing shortest-path distance from a start vertex, where distance counts edges.

rows.name: Breakout method
rows.definition: A finite constraint-satisfaction search method that takes strictly improving local assignment changes under a weighted nogood cost and increases the weights of all currently violated nogoods at a non-solution local minimum to change the search landscape.

rows.name: Brevity-penalty normalization for sequence scoring
rows.definition: A sequence rescoring rule that adds a predicted-length brevity penalty in log space to average token log probability: S(x,y)/|y| + min(1−Lpred(x)/|y|,0).

rows.name: C4.5
rows.definition: Decision-tree induction extending ID3 with tests on continuous-valued features.

rows.name: CART
rows.definition: Decision-tree induction using binary recursive partitioning for classification or regression.

rows.name: CD-PercLoss
rows.definition: A conditional RBM training algorithm that contrasts the observed output free energy with that of a prediction selected by input-initialized stochastic search, treating the selected prediction as fixed during differentiation.

rows.name: CHAMELEON clustering
rows.definition: A graph-clustering procedure that first partitions a sparse neighbor graph into small subclusters and then agglomerates them using interconnectivity and closeness normalized by their internal bisection statistics.

rows.name: CLARANS clustering
rows.definition: A randomized medoid-clustering algorithm that searches fixed-size sets of representative observations by accepting improving single swaps and restarting after a budget of unsuccessful neighbor trials.

identities.value: Clustering Large Applications based on RANdomized Search

rows.name: Clauset–Newman–Moore community detection
rows.definition: A greedy community-detection algorithm that agglomerates graph vertices using modularity changes, with sparse change tables and heap-based maximum tracking to accelerate the construction of a merge hierarchy and selection of a partition by modularity.

rows.name: CTAugment
rows.definition: An online augmentation-policy adaptation procedure that samples image operations and adjusts their parameter-selection weights using classifier feedback on labeled probe images during training.

rows.name: CURE clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering procedure that represents each cluster by several scattered points shrunk toward its mean and merges the pair with the smallest distance between their representative points.

rows.name: Chakrabarti classifier-guided focused crawling
rows.definition: A focused web-acquisition procedure that uses a trained classifier over a supplied topic taxonomy to decide or prioritize hyperlink expansion, with hard and soft focus modes and periodic relevance-weighted hub discovery to promote promising crawl locations.

rows.name: Classification Annealing Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: A stochastic hard-clustering algorithm that samples component assignments from current mixture posterior probabilities raised to an inverse positive temperature, maximizes the completed-data classification likelihood, and lowers the temperature according to a chosen schedule.

rows.name: Classification Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: A model-based hard-clustering algorithm that computes mixture responsibilities, assigns every observation to a highest-responsibility component, and maximizes the completed-data classification likelihood for that assignment.

rows.name: Clique extracted ontology
rows.definition: An overlapping hierarchical clustering heuristic that constructs a directed acyclic hierarchy from pairwise dissimilarities by selecting informative threshold-graph maximal cliques, with persistence-based noise filtering and optional completion of inferred missing edges.

rows.name: Clockwork recurrent neural network
rows.definition: A recurrent architecture partitioning hidden units into modules with prescribed update periods, copying inactive module states and restricting inter-module recurrence from slower modules to faster modules while retaining recurrence within each module.

rows.name: Clustering Data by Melting
rows.definition: A scale-dependent clustering procedure that heats Gaussian-weighted center iterations to build a merging membership tree, then selects clusters by persistence of their within-cluster weight fraction across logarithmic scales.

rows.name: Communication Neural Network
rows.definition: A neural architecture for cooperative multi-agent tasks that alternates shared per-agent hidden-state updates with continuous communication formed by averaging other agents’ hidden states, allowing task losses to train communication and agent computation together.

rows.name: Complete balanced largest differencing
rows.definition: A complete anytime two-way number-partitioning search that carries signed effective cardinalities through difference and sum branches, uses paired initialization before largest-residual branching, and prunes against a prescribed subset-size difference while retaining the best valid partition.

rows.name: Complete greedy number partitioning
rows.definition: A complete anytime number-partitioning search that assigns weights in decreasing order to a fixed number of bins, explores the currently lightest-bin choices first, and retains the smallest load range while pruning by valid bounds and bin symmetry.

identities.value: Complete greedy algorithm for number partitioning

rows.name: Complete Karmarkar–Karp
rows.definition: A complete anytime algorithm for two-way number partitioning that first follows Karmarkar–Karp differencing, then explores complementary sum branches over residual subpartitions, retaining the best partition and using sound bounds or exhaustive search to certify optimality.

rows.name: Complete layer-wise adaptive rate scaling
rows.definition: A layer-wise gradient optimization method whose published rate formula divides the current parameter-block L2 norm by the average L2 norm of individual-example gradients in a minibatch, multiplied by a global rate and trust coefficient. It applies the resulting scalar to the minibatch mean gradient, reducing the basic LARS rate when individual gradient directions disagree.

rows.name: Complete multiway Karmarkar–Karp
rows.definition: A complete anytime multiway number-partitioning search that combines partial bin assignments in alternative relative permutations, explores low-range compositions first, and uses normalized load bounds and symmetry to retain and certify a minimum-range partition.

rows.name: Composite HMM-topic model
rows.definition: A generative sequence model combining an HMM class sequence with a document topic mixture, where one designated class emits words through latent topics and each other class emits words from its own categorical distribution.

rows.name: Condensed nearest-neighbor data domain description
rows.definition: A greedy reference-selection algorithm for the NNDD distance-norm decision rule that uses two passes over the original observations followed by neighbor augmentation to obtain a subset preserving every original-reference decision.

rows.name: Condensed prototype-based domain description
rows.definition: A greedy prototype-selection procedure that constructs kth-neighbor radius offsets from the full reference dataset and repeatedly chooses the prototype covering the most still-uncovered eligible reference locations under the PDD distance rule.

rows.name: Conditional Distribution Prediction for IDA*
rows.definition: A search-effort estimation procedure that predicts the number of expanded nodes in a complete IDA* threshold iteration by recursively propagating conditional heuristic-value frequencies and branching counts while excluding pruned ancestor paths.

rows.name: Conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
rows.definition: A conditional neural probability model that represents an output vector with an RBM whose biases or interactions are determined by a supplied conditioning vector.

rows.name: Conjugate-gradient Monte Carlo
rows.definition: A population Markov sampler that obtains a local-optimization anchor from one population member and updates another member along the anchor line with a multiple-try transition targeting a radial-Jacobian-adjusted density.

rows.name: Consistency model
rows.definition: A generative model family that learns a noise- or time-conditioned function mapping points on a probability-flow ODE trajectory to its common low-noise endpoint, enabling a sample to be obtained with one model evaluation and allowing optional multistep refinement.

rows.name: Context-sensitive emission hidden Markov model
rows.definition: A hidden-state sequence-model family with a first-order Markov prior whose observation distributions depend jointly on hidden states at multiple temporal positions, introducing context beyond the contemporaneous hidden state.

rows.name: Contrastive divergence
rows.definition: A parameter-learning algorithm for energy-based or product-of-experts models that replaces the equilibrium negative-phase expectation by configurations obtained from a short model-invariant Markov chain restarted at observed data, without differentiating through the chain distribution.

rows.name: Contrastive predictive coding
rows.definition: A representation-learning procedure that encodes observations, summarizes preceding representations as context, and jointly trains these components to distinguish future representations from sampled alternatives using InfoNCE.

rows.name: Global Kernel K-Means with Convex Mixture Models
rows.definition: An incremental kernel clustering algorithm that fits a convex mixture over datum exemplars once, restricts each new-cluster seed search to its selected high-weight exemplars, and retains the lowest-error local kernel k-means fit.

identities.value: Global Kernel K-Means with Convex Mixture Models

rows.name: Convolutional Block Attention Module
rows.definition: A convolutional feature refinement component that sequentially applies learned channel attention and then spatial attention to an intermediate feature tensor.

rows.name: Core-set support vector data description
rows.definition: An approximate one-class training algorithm that grows a core subset using the nearest expanded-sphere violator, refits support vector data description and enforces radius growth until the expanded sphere meets an outlier-count stopping rule.

rows.name: Core vector machine
rows.definition: An approximate kernel training algorithm that reformulates supported constant-diagonal simplex quadratic programs as minimum enclosing balls and repeatedly enlarges a core subset with a violating point while reoptimizing its ball.

rows.name: Core vector regression
rows.definition: A support-vector regression training algorithm that approximates a penalized-bias, paired squared-slack formulation with a learned unconstrained margin using a center-constrained minimum enclosing ball over two transformed points per observation.

rows.name: Correlated topic model
rows.definition: A mixed-membership topic model that draws each document's topic proportions from a logistic-normal distribution and generates its words through latent topic assignments and shared categorical topic-word distributions.

rows.name: Correlation-based Hammerstein identification
rows.definition: A two-stage identification algorithm for a real-valued single-input single-output polynomial Hammerstein cascade that estimates a scaled linear response from Gaussian-excited input/output cross-correlation, then fits the input polynomial by least squares on filtered input powers.

rows.name: Correlation-based Wiener identification
rows.definition: A two-stage identification algorithm for a real-valued single-input single-output polynomial Wiener cascade that estimates a scaled linear response from Gaussian-excited input/output cross-correlation, then fits the output polynomial by least squares on the reconstructed internal signal.

rows.name: Counterfactual fairness
rows.definition: A fairness criterion in a specified causal model requiring a predictor's conditional output distribution, given an individual's observed attributes and protected-attribute value, to remain unchanged under counterfactual interventions that assign other attainable protected-attribute values.

rows.name: Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy
rows.definition: An evolution strategy for continuous optimization that samples a multivariate normal search distribution and adapts its mean, covariance and global step size from ranked offspring and accumulated selected-step paths.

rows.name: Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
rows.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that combines a Crank–Nicolson treatment of the reference precision with an explicit gradient drift of the remaining target potential.

rows.name: Crank–Nicolson Metropolis sampling
rows.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target using a Crank–Nicolson discretization of the unpreconditioned reference Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics as its proposal.

rows.name: Cross-entropy optimization
rows.definition: A stochastic optimization method that iteratively samples a parameterized search distribution, selects high-performing samples using an adaptive threshold, and refits the distribution by maximum likelihood on those selected samples.

rows.name: Cross-validated prior-likelihood conflict diagnostic
rows.definition: A Bayesian hierarchical-model diagnostic that leaves an assessed unit out of population-parameter fitting, generates predictive-prior and reference-prior likelihood replicates of its unit effect, and measures their signed conflict under an explicitly specified replication law. Shared nuisance parameters require controlled feedback and dependence handling.

rows.name: Curriculum Dropout
rows.definition: A neural-network training procedure that starts without unit suppression and gradually increases Bernoulli dropout by decreasing the probability of retaining each unit toward a specified layer-dependent limit.

rows.name: CutMix
rows.definition: A training augmentation procedure that replaces a rectangular region of one image with the corresponding region of another and mixes their class targets in proportion to the retained and pasted image areas.

rows.name: Cutout
rows.definition: A training-image augmentation method that removes information from a randomly located square region by replacing that region with zeros in the normalized input while keeping the original target.

rows.name: Cutting Plane Multiclass Maximum Margin Clustering
rows.definition: A fixed-kernel multiclass clustering procedure that fits latent winning-class margins by adding violated aggregate constraints and repeatedly solving quadratic programs with frozen class winners.

identities.value: Cutting Plane Multiclass Maximum Margin Clustering

rows.name: DBSCAN
rows.definition: Density-based clustering that connects dense neighborhoods and identifies unsupported observations as noise.

identities.value: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise

rows.name: DEHB
rows.definition: A hyperparameter optimization algorithm that combines Hyperband resource schedules with differential-evolution populations at different resource levels, using promising lower-resource configurations to guide proposals evaluated and selected at higher resource levels.

rows.name: DINO self-distillation
rows.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that matches cross-view student probabilities to centered and sharpened probabilities from a momentum teacher, without a separate prediction head or explicit negative-pair objective.

rows.name: Deep autoregressive network
rows.definition: A generative neural architecture that combines directed stochastic hidden layers with autoregressive within-layer conditional dependencies and a separately parameterized recognition network for approximate latent inference.

rows.name: DeepCluster
rows.definition: A visual representation-learning procedure that alternates clustering current neural features into pseudo-labels and training the feature extractor and a classifier to predict those labels.

identities.value: Deep clustering for unsupervised learning of visual features

rows.name: Deep continuous clustering
rows.definition: A clustering algorithm that jointly learns a nonlinear autoencoder and one latent representative per observation by combining reconstruction with robust observation-to-representative and graph-pair losses, then extracts groups from representative distances without a supplied cluster count.

rows.name: Deep deterministic policy gradient
rows.definition: An off-policy actor–critic method for continuous control using neural function approximators and deterministic policy gradients.

rows.name: Deep embedded clustering
rows.definition: A neural clustering procedure that jointly refines an embedding and cluster centers by fitting Student-t soft assignments to periodically refreshed, frequency-normalized squared-assignment targets.

identities.value: Unsupervised deep embedding for clustering analysis

rows.name: Deep InfoMax
rows.definition: A representation-learning procedure that jointly trains an encoder and a dependence critic on matched versus mismatched global or local-to-global features, optionally regularizing the encoder output toward a chosen prior.

rows.name: DeepLIFT
rows.definition: A neural-network attribution method that distributes an output's difference from a reference activation to input differences using backward contribution propagation.

rows.name: Deep Output Recurrent Neural Network
rows.definition: A recurrent neural architecture whose hidden-to-output function uses a multilayer perceptron with intermediate nonlinear feedforward layers to compute an output from the current recurrent hidden state.

rows.name: Deep Output-Transition Recurrent Neural Network
rows.definition: A recurrent neural architecture that uses intermediate nonlinear feedforward layers in both the hidden-state transition from the previous state and current input, and the output function from the current hidden state.

rows.name: Deep Q-network learning
rows.definition: A deep Q-learning method that trains a neural action-value function using replayed transitions and a separate target network.

rows.name: Deep SHAP
rows.definition: A compositional approximation of neural-network Shapley attributions using component-level SHAP values and backward multipliers.

rows.name: Deep Sets
rows.definition: A neural architecture family for unordered collections that combines shared element transformations with symmetric aggregation for invariant outputs, or shared element and pooled-context computations for permutation-equivariant outputs.

rows.name: Deep Sets++
rows.definition: A Deep Sets architecture revision whose encoder combines identity residual paths with set normalization while retaining the original aggregation and decoder.

rows.name: Deep Transition Recurrent Neural Network
rows.definition: A recurrent neural architecture whose state-transition function uses a multilayer perceptron with intermediate nonlinear feedforward layers to compute the current hidden state from the previous hidden state and current input.

rows.name: Definition-filtered Girvan–Newman community detection
rows.definition: A Girvan–Newman variant that retains a branching event in the reported hierarchy only when at least two resulting groups satisfy a selected strong or weak community definition evaluated against the original graph, while continuing betweenness-based edge deletion within the resulting subgraphs.

rows.name: Delayed-rejection adaptive Metropolis
rows.definition: An adaptive Metropolis procedure combining history-based Gaussian proposal covariance updates between transitions with corrected delayed-rejection proposal stages within a transition.

rows.name: Delayed-rejection Metropolis
rows.definition: A Metropolis-Hastings sampling procedure that can propose another candidate after rejection within the same transition, correcting acceptance for the probabilities of the forward and reversed rejected paths.

rows.name: Demographic parity
rows.definition: A group-level prediction criterion requiring the distribution of a decision or prediction to be independent of a specified protected attribute; for a binary decision, the positive-decision rate is equal across the compared groups.

rows.name: Depth-first iterative deepening
rows.definition: A search algorithm that repeatedly performs depth-first searches from the start with successively larger depth limits, redoing shallower work until it reaches a goal.

rows.name: Depth-first search
rows.definition: A graph or state-space traversal that follows a newly chosen successor down the current search branch and backtracks when that branch has no eligible unvisited successor or reaches a stopping boundary.

rows.name: Depth-Gated LSTM
rows.definition: A stacked LSTM architecture that adds a learned, elementwise gated contribution from the current lower-layer memory cell to the upper-layer cell update alongside its temporal memory and input paths.

rows.name: Derivative-observation Gaussian process regression
rows.definition: A Gaussian-process regression procedure that jointly conditions a sufficiently differentiable scalar-function prior on function values and partial-derivative values using differentiated kernel covariance blocks and a specified Gaussian observation-error model.

identities.value: Gaussian process regression with derivative observations

rows.name: Deterministic Annealing Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: A latent-variable likelihood-fitting procedure that performs deterministic powered-posterior EM updates along a warm-started cooling schedule from a small positive inverse temperature to one, including an ordinary-likelihood fit at the endpoint.

rows.name: Diaconis–Holmes–Neal fiber sampler
rows.definition: A finite-state Metropolis sampler that uses partitions into ordered lines, retains a binary direction for each partition, and combines a neighbor proposal with a separate probabilistic sign update to preserve a target distribution on the augmented state.

rows.name: Differentiable scheduled sampling
rows.definition: A scheduled-sampling training procedure that replaces discrete model-feedback embeddings with differentiable soft mixtures, allowing later sequence losses to propagate credit through earlier relaxed decoding choices.

rows.name: Differential Evolution
rows.definition: A population-based continuous optimization method that generates trial vectors using scaled differences between population members, combines mutant and target coordinates, and selects replacements through target-trial objective comparisons.

rows.name: Diffusion Maps
rows.definition: A family of spectral embedding algorithms that normalizes a nonnegative symmetric affinity kernel into a reversible Markov operator and represents points by its nontrivial eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues.

rows.name: Dijkstra shortest-path algorithm
rows.definition: A shortest-path algorithm for nonnegative edge weights that repeatedly settles the unsettled vertex with the smallest tentative distance from a source and relaxes its outgoing edges.

rows.name: Direct preference optimization
rows.definition: Preference-based policy fitting using a classification objective on policy-to-reference probability ratios for preferred and dispreferred responses.

rows.name: Dirichlet compound multinomial latent Dirichlet allocation
rows.definition: A topic-model family for grouped documents in which each group draws its own topic-word distributions from corpus-shared topic-specific Dirichlet distributions, while individual documents mix those group-specific topics.

identities.value: Dirichlet compound multinomial latent Dirichlet allocation

rows.name: Diverse beam search
rows.definition: The inference procedure of Vijayakumar and colleagues that partitions a sequence beam budget into groups and updates each group using model log-probability scores augmented by a weighted dissimilarity to the already-updated earlier groups at the same decoding step.

rows.name: Divide-and-conquer beam search
rows.definition: A memory-limited breadth-first heuristic search that discards least-promising open nodes when its chosen capacity is reached and recovers a solution through relay-based divide-and-conquer reconstruction instead of retaining every predecessor layer.

rows.name: Divide-and-conquer beam-stack search
rows.definition: A beam-stack search implementation that retains a small set of search layers and relay information, regenerates missing layers for backtracking, and reconstructs a solution through recursive subproblems.

rows.name: Document NADE
rows.definition: A neural autoregressive document model that predicts successive words from shared additive embeddings of the preceding words, using normalized word conditionals and a deterministic document representation.

rows.name: Doubling slice sampling
rows.definition: A univariate slice-sampling algorithm that expands a randomly placed initial interval by randomly directed doublings and uses shrinkage with a retrospective acceptability test to preserve the target.

rows.name: DropBlock
rows.definition: A training-time feature-map transformation for convolutional networks that suppresses randomly placed contiguous spatial blocks of activations and rescales retained activations.

rows.name: DropConnect
rows.definition: A stochastic neural-network layer that masks individual weights and biases during training, so each example is processed through a randomly selected subset of the layer’s connections.

rows.name: Dropout Boosting
rows.definition: A dropout-mask training procedure proposed to optimize the likelihood of a normalized geometric ensemble, updating through a selected shared-parameter subnetwork while approximating the ensemble prediction by weight scaling.

rows.name: Dual-averaging step-size adaptation for Hamiltonian samplers
rows.definition: A warmup procedure that tunes the logarithm of a Hamiltonian sampler’s integration step size using cumulative discrepancy from a target acceptance statistic, a shrinkage point and a smoothed sequence of iterates.

identities.value: Dual-averaging step-size adaptation for Hamiltonian samplers

rows.name: Dynamic Convolutional Layer
rows.definition: A neural layer that convolves feature maps with filters generated from the current input by a learned subnetwork, allowing the applied kernels to vary between examples during inference.

rows.name: Dynamic Memory Network
rows.definition: A recurrent neural architecture that encodes an input and a question, repeatedly forms question-conditioned episodes from input facts to update a memory state, and generates an answer from that state.

rows.name: Dynamic Memory Network Plus
rows.definition: A recurrent question-answering architecture that fuses text or image facts, aggregates them with question- and memory-conditioned attention gates in a GRU, and updates episodic memory through pass-specific rectified affine transformations.

rows.name: Dynamic topic model
rows.definition: A time-sliced topic-model family that links the softmax natural parameters of corresponding topic-word distributions across slices through Gaussian state transitions, allowing a fixed set of topics to change over time.

rows.name: Early Dropout
rows.definition: A neural-network training procedure that applies dropout during an initial portion of optimization and disables it for the remaining training steps, with the initial-phase rate following a selected schedule.

rows.name: Eclat
rows.definition: Frequent-itemset mining using depth-first enumeration and transaction-set intersections.

rows.name: Elastic net
rows.definition: Linear regression regularized by a combination of L1 and L2 penalties.

rows.name: Elitist Ant System
rows.definition: An Ant System variant that retains the standard all-ant pheromone deposits and adds extra reinforcement to edges of the best-so-far tour after each construction cycle.

rows.name: Elliptical slice sampling
rows.definition: A Markov-chain update for a target factored into a Gaussian prior and a likelihood, which performs an angular slice search along the ellipse defined by the current state and an independent prior draw.

rows.name: End-to-End Memory Network
rows.definition: A neural architecture that answers a query through one or more differentiable soft-attention reads over separately embedded input and output memories, updating a query state between reads and learning from the final prediction loss.

rows.name: Eppstein–Wang RAND closeness approximation
rows.definition: A randomized graph-analysis algorithm that estimates closeness centrality from independent uniformly sampled source vertices, averaging scaled shortest-path distances to estimate mean distance and taking its reciprocal where defined.

rows.name: Epsilon-truncation for Conditional Distribution Prediction
rows.definition: A modification of conditional distribution prediction for IDA* tree size that removes conditional child-type probabilities below a calibrated level-specific cutoff, renormalizes the surviving probabilities and uses the modified tables in node-count propagation.

rows.name: Equal opportunity in binary classification
rows.definition: A binary-classification fairness criterion requiring equal probabilities of a positive prediction across specified protected groups among individuals whose target outcome is the designated positive outcome.

rows.name: Equalized odds
rows.definition: A fairness criterion requiring a predictor's output to be conditionally independent of a specified protected attribute given the target outcome; for binary predictions and outcomes, it requires equal true-positive and false-positive rates across the compared groups.

rows.name: Equalized-odds postprocessing for binary predictors
rows.definition: A randomized postprocessing algorithm that uses a binary predictor and protected-group membership to minimize expected label loss subject to equal false-positive and true-positive rates across groups, within predictors derived from those inputs.

rows.name: Exact PoClustering
rows.definition: A dissimilarity-based clustering construction that accumulates maximal cliques of pairwise-distance threshold graphs and organizes their sets by inclusion with diameter labels, allowing overlapping clusters and multiple parents.

rows.name: Exemplar-Based Convex Clustering
rows.definition: An exemplar-based clustering procedure that fixes candidate component centers at every observed point, fits their simplex weights through a convex soft information-distortion objective, and derives a hard grouping from selected posterior-MAP exemplars.

rows.name: Expectation Conditional Maximization
rows.definition: An extension of expectation maximization that replaces a joint maximization of the expected complete-data log likelihood with a sequence of constrained maximizations, holding the E-step expectation fixed throughout that sequence.

rows.name: Expectation Conditional Maximization Either
rows.definition: An extension of expectation conditional maximization that replaces selected final conditional maximizations of expected complete-data log likelihood with conditional maximizations of actual observed-data likelihood.

rows.name: Expectation maximization
rows.definition: Parameter estimation alternating expected complete-data log-likelihood evaluation and its maximization.

rows.name: Exponential-family harmonium
rows.definition: A bipartite undirected model family coupling visible and hidden exponential-family sufficient statistics through bilinear interactions, with variables conditionally independent within either layer given the other and a finite global joint normalizer.

rows.name: Exponential generalized root model
rows.definition: A generalized root probability model on nonnegative continuous variables with exponential base measure and symmetric root-product interactions, restricted to parameters with a finite joint integral; uniform negative degree-one terms provide a sufficient normalizable regime.

rows.name: Exponential square root graphical model
rows.definition: A graphical probability model on nonnegative continuous variables with unary square-root terms and symmetric products of square roots, derived from an exponential base measure and restricted to parameters giving a finite joint integral.

identities.value: Exponential square root Markov random field

rows.name: Exponentiated-gradient reduction for fair classification
rows.definition: A cost-sensitive classification reduction that alternates classifier best responses with exponentiated-gradient updates of bounded Lagrange multipliers to approximate an error–fairness saddle point and return a randomized classifier mixture.

rows.name: Extended Guided Local Search
rows.definition: The Tsang–Mills–Ford extension of Guided Local Search that combines cost-scaled penalty weighting, aspiration for a new best original-objective solution despite an augmented-objective penalty, and probabilistic random neighborhood moves.

rows.name: FABOLAS
rows.definition: A Bayesian hyperparameter optimization algorithm that jointly chooses a model configuration and training-data subset size using surrogate models of loss and evaluation cost, directing evaluations toward information about the best configuration on the full dataset.

identities.value: Fast Bayesian Optimization on Large Data Sets

rows.name: First-come, first-served beam decoding
rows.definition: The sequence beam-decoding procedure described by Kasai and colleagues that stores completed hypotheses separately from the continuing beam and stops when the accumulated number of completed hypotheses reaches the beam width, returning the highest-scoring stored completion.

rows.name: F-Race
rows.definition: A statistical racing method for configuring metaheuristics that evaluates a finite candidate set on shared problem-instance blocks and eliminates candidates judged worse through a Friedman rank test followed by comparisons with the best-ranked candidate.

rows.name: Factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model
rows.definition: A conditional neural word model that factorizes position-specific word-to-hidden weights through a shared word-embedding matrix and couples the next categorical word to binary hidden units in a context-conditioned restricted Boltzmann machine.

identities.value: Factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model

rows.name: Factorial hidden Markov model
rows.definition: A directed latent sequence-model family in which several independently evolving hidden Markov chains jointly determine the observation distribution at each time.

rows.name: Factorized LHUC Adaptation
rows.definition: An acoustic-model adaptation procedure that combines separately estimated speaker and environment LHUC transforms by interpolating their transformed hidden-unit amplitudes for a known target environment.

rows.name: Factorized variational sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process inference
rows.definition: The Gal–Turner finite spectral regression inference procedure that explicitly optimizes diagonal Gaussian output-coefficient factors and independent spectral variational factors using an evidence lower bound written as a sum of per-observation expected log likelihoods and global KL penalties.

rows.name: FAIRLEARNING
rows.definition: A causal-model-dependent learning procedure that minimizes predictive loss averaged over inferred background variables, restricting the latent predictor to those variables and observed non-descendants of protected attributes.

rows.name: Fairness LP
rows.definition: A finite-population optimization procedure that assigns outcome distributions to individuals to minimize expected loss under pairwise Lipschitz similarity constraints, expressible as a linear program for the total-variation or relative-infinity distribution distances used by Dwork et al.

rows.name: Family-of-harmonium
rows.definition: A classification model family comprising separately parameterized harmoniums for each class, with binary text features and Gaussian image features coupled to Gaussian latent variables and compared through normalized class-conditional likelihoods.

rows.name: Fast AutoAugment
rows.definition: An augmentation-policy search procedure that evaluates candidate transformations on held-out training examples using a fixed classifier trained on another split, combines high-scoring policies across splits and uses them for final classifier training.

rows.name: Fast condensed prototype-based domain description
rows.definition: A heuristic for selecting PDD prototypes that samples remaining reference observations, computes their radius offsets against the full dataset, accumulates eligible candidates, and greedily selects them by uncovered-reference gain with an adaptive sampling schedule.

rows.name: Fast Dropout Training
rows.definition: A dropout approximation procedure that replaces masked weighted sums by Gaussian distributions with matched means and variances, using Gaussian sampling or moment integration to approximate training and prediction computations.

rows.name: Fast Global Kernel K-Means
rows.definition: An incremental kernel clustering algorithm that chooses each new singleton seed by maximizing a computable lower bound on error reduction, then runs one local kernel k-means fit for that stage.

rows.name: FastICA
rows.definition: A family of independent-component estimation algorithms that repeatedly apply normalized approximate-Newton fixed-point updates to nonlinear projection contrasts, using deflation or symmetric decorrelation to obtain multiple components.

rows.name: Fast Local Search
rows.definition: A neighborhood-search procedure that uses activation bits to scan selected subneighborhoods, deactivating unsuccessful ones and reactivating those affected by accepted improvements.

rows.name: Fast persistent contrastive divergence
rows.definition: A persistent-chain RBM learning algorithm that adds rapidly updated, rapidly decaying auxiliary parameters to the sampling energy while retaining separate regular parameters for the model distribution.

rows.name: Feature-wise Linear Modulation
rows.definition: A neural conditioning layer that applies a feature-wise affine transformation whose scale and shift are generated from conditioning information, modifying an intermediate representation for subsequent computation.

rows.name: FiLM Parameter-Arithmetic Inference
rows.definition: A post-training visual-question-answering procedure that uses a parser to construct related questions and combines their generated FiLM scale/shift vectors by addition and subtraction before running the conditioned visual network.

rows.name: Fill algorithm
rows.definition: An idealized finite constraint-satisfaction search algorithm that takes any strictly cost-reducing single-variable change when available and otherwise increases only the stored cost of the current non-solution assignment.

rows.name: FixMatch
rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that fits labeled examples and trains on strongly augmented unlabeled inputs using hard pseudo-labels retained only when the corresponding weakly augmented prediction reaches a confidence threshold.

rows.name: Fixed-Component Mixture-Weight EM
rows.definition: An expectation-maximization specialization that keeps every component distribution fixed and updates only their simplex mixing weights by averaging current component responsibilities.

rows.name: Fixed-length Poisson MRF topic model
rows.definition: A probabilistic topic model that allocates a document total among topics, draws an independent fixed-length Poisson-MRF count vector for each allocated topic total, and sums those latent vectors to produce the observed document counts.

rows.name: Fixed-length Poisson Markov random field
rows.definition: A finite-total count distribution whose probability on nonnegative integer vectors summing to a specified total is proportional to a Poisson factorial base measure times exponentiated linear and symmetric quadratic count potentials.

rows.name: Flake exact-flow community identification
rows.definition: A seeded web-graph grouping procedure that adds infinite-capacity source arcs to seed vertices, makes original hyperlink connections bidirectional with a common capacity, connects nonseed vertices to an artificial sink with unit capacity, and extracts source-reachable original vertices from the residual graph after maximum flow.

rows.name: Flake focused community crawling
rows.definition: A flow-based focused-crawling family that alternates gathering a local web graph around positive seed pages, extracting a group through seeded maximum flow, promoting selected discovered pages to seeds and recrawling, with version-specific graph augmentation and seed-ranking rules.

rows.name: FlashAttention
rows.definition: An exact attention computation algorithm using tiling and recomputation to reduce transfers between GPU memory levels.

rows.name: FlashConv
rows.definition: An execution algorithm for state-space sequence convolutions that fuses FFT-based convolution in GPU on-chip memory, uses block FFT matrix multiplications and passes state between chunks for longer sequences.

rows.name: Flattened slice sampling
rows.definition: A finite categorical conditional-update algorithm that splits excess probability from a maximum-probability state into additional bars and samples a directed move to the preceding bar intersecting a random height, while retaining the given state order.

rows.name: Flow matching
rows.definition: A generative-model training method that fits a time-dependent vector field by regression to velocities associated with a chosen probability path between a base distribution and a data distribution, with conditional flow matching providing a tractable training objective.

rows.name: FocusedILS
rows.definition: A ParamILS algorithm-configuration method that adaptively extends paired evaluation prefixes until one configuration dominates the other, and allocates bonus evaluations to configurations that win the comparison.

rows.name: Fully factorized mean-field inference
rows.definition: A variational inference method that restricts its approximating distribution to a product of single-variable factors and adjusts those factors to reduce the approximation-to-target Kullback–Leibler divergence.

rows.name: Fully visible sigmoid belief network
rows.definition: A fully observed binary autoregressive probabilistic model whose conditional probability at each position is a logistic function of a bias and a weighted sum of preceding visible variables.

rows.name: Graph attention network v2
rows.definition: A graph neural architecture whose neighborhood attention scorer applies a learned scalar projection after a nonlinear transformation of the query-neighbor pair, allowing attention rankings to depend on the query node.

rows.name: GENET
rows.definition: A connectionist architecture for finite constraint satisfaction that represents variable assignments by active label nodes and alternates input-maximizing assignment updates with increased inhibitory weights on violated constraints when the network stabilizes without a solution.

rows.name: GRINCH clustering
rows.definition: An incremental hierarchical clustering algorithm that uses set-wise linkage scores to revise a binary cluster tree through local rotations, nonlocal subtree grafting and restructuring.

rows.name: GSAT
rows.definition: A randomized local-search SAT procedure that repeatedly flips a Boolean variable giving the largest change toward more satisfied CNF clauses, breaks tied choices randomly, and restarts from a random complete assignment under specified flip and attempt budgets.

rows.name: GSAT averaging-in strategy
rows.definition: A GSAT restart-initialization strategy that reuses agreements between earlier complete assignments, randomizes their differing positions, and periodically resets to a fresh random start.

rows.name: GSAT clause-weighting strategy
rows.definition: A GSAT extension that starts each clause with weight one, uses weighted clause counts to select flips, and increases the weights of clauses unsatisfied by the current assignment at the end of each search attempt.

rows.name: GSAT with random noise
rows.definition: A GSAT variant that mixes a random flip drawn from all formula variables with a globally best GSAT flip, without restricting the random choice to variables in currently unsatisfied clauses.

rows.name: GSAT with random walk
rows.definition: A GSAT variant that mixes a uniformly chosen flip from the distinct variables currently occurring in unsatisfied clauses with a globally best GSAT flip, using a fixed probability to choose the focused random move.

rows.name: Gamma filter
rows.definition: A linear adaptive filter family that combines a direct input tap with weighted cascaded first-order gamma-memory traces, using one shared memory coefficient to control the restricted feedback.

rows.name: Gamma neural model
rows.definition: A neural architecture family that represents delayed inputs or neural outputs by weighted gamma-kernel memory traces, realized through cascades of first-order leaky integrators.

rows.name: Gated-feedback recurrent neural network
rows.definition: A layered recurrent architecture in which learned input-dependent scalar gates modulate recurrent projections from every previous layer state to each destination layer, including delayed top-down feedback, alongside the current bottom-up computation.

rows.name: Gated Graph Neural Network
rows.definition: A graph neural architecture that initializes node states from annotations, repeatedly combines edge-type- and direction-specific neighbor messages with shared gated recurrent updates for a fixed propagation depth, and reads out node or graph predictions.

rows.name: Gated Graph Sequence Neural Network
rows.definition: A graph-to-sequence neural architecture that repeatedly runs gated graph propagation to predict an output and update node annotations, using those predicted annotations to initialize graph computation for the next output position.

rows.name: Gaussian Differentiable Pooling
rows.definition: A spatial pooling and unpooling component whose nonnegative, unit-L2 weights are square-root normalized axis-aligned Gaussian samples, with each region’s location and precision inferred jointly with image-specific features under a reconstruction objective.

rows.name: Gaussian Factor Analysis
rows.definition: A linear Gaussian latent-variable model in which observed variables share a lower-dimensional Gaussian factor and have conditionally independent residuals with variable-specific nonnegative variances.

rows.name: Gaussian loss-smoothed mixed-model variational inference
rows.definition: A nonconjugate variational inference procedure for a loss-defined mixed-effects generalized posterior that retains a joint Gaussian over fixed and random coefficients, factors inverse-gamma random-effect variances, and uses one-dimensional Gaussian expected-loss derivatives to alternate exact variance coordinates with a full-Gaussian natural proposal. This record denotes the base NCVB-UF procedure with the precision sign reconciled against its gradient/Hessian derivation.

rows.name: Gaussian message conflict diagnostic
rows.definition: A Bayesian GLMM screening procedure that separates Gaussian prior and likelihood natural-parameter messages at local variational fixed points and computes conflict scores from an approximately independent Gaussian difference. It approximates predictive-prior versus unit-likelihood disagreement using full-data fitted factors.

rows.name: Gaussian-process moment matching for Gaussian inputs
rows.definition: A Gaussian-process prediction procedure that analytically integrates a fixed squared-exponential posterior over an independently prescribed Gaussian test-input distribution and represents the resulting latent prediction by a Gaussian matching its exact first two moments.

identities.value: Gaussian-process moment matching for Gaussian inputs
Gaussian input Gaussian process moment matching

rows.name: Gaussian process regression
rows.definition: Probabilistic regression conditioning a Gaussian-process prior on observed training data.

rows.name: Taylor approximation for uncertain-input Gaussian-process prediction
rows.definition: A local Gaussian-process prediction algorithm that expands a fixed posterior mean to first order and its latent variance to second order about the mean of a prescribed Gaussian test input, integrates those expansions, and uses the resulting approximate moments for a Gaussian predictive representation and iterative covariance propagation.

identities.value: Taylor approximation for uncertain-input Gaussian-process prediction

rows.name: Generalized advantage estimation
rows.definition: An advantage-function estimator for policy-gradient learning formed from an exponentially weighted sum of temporal-difference residuals.

rows.name: Generalized Alternating Minimization
rows.definition: An information-geometric fitting framework that updates a generating distribution constrained by the observations and model parameters to decrease their joint Kullback-Leibler objective, allowing inexact distribution and parameter minimization.

rows.name: Generalized component analysis
rows.definition: An undirected latent-component model family coupling categorical text and heterogeneous document attributes to positive lognormal hidden variables, with variables conditionally independent within either layer given the other and shared attribute-specific interaction weights.

rows.name: Generalized core vector machine
rows.definition: A kernel optimization algorithm that converts a quadratic program with a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix and simplex constraints into a center-constrained minimum enclosing ball, then approximates its solution by repeatedly enlarging and reoptimizing a core subset.

rows.name: Generalized Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: A latent-variable likelihood-fitting framework that computes the expected complete-data log likelihood under the current exact posterior and replaces full maximization with a parameter update that does not decrease that same expected objective.

rows.name: Generalized root model
rows.definition: A family of finite undirected probability models that retains univariate exponential-family base measures and couples coordinatewise roots of sufficient statistics in symmetric interactions of configurable order, restricted to parameters with a finite joint partition function.

rows.name: Generative Topographic Mapping
rows.definition: A nonlinear latent-variable density model with a uniform discrete prior on fixed latent grid nodes, mapped through a shared smooth function to the centers of an equal-weight Gaussian mixture with common isotropic covariance.

rows.name: Generic lazy-neighbor agglomerative clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that caches candidate nearest neighbors and lower bounds on row-minimum dissimilarities in a priority queue, rescanning a stale row only when necessary to certify the next globally closest pair before merging it.

rows.name: Generic tree sampling
rows.definition: An importance-sampling generalization of Chen heuristic tree sampling that merges representatives of ordered tree strata using specified positive selection probabilities and inverse-probability survivor weights to estimate an additive tree functional.

rows.name: Genetic algorithm
rows.definition: Evolutionary optimization using fitness-based selection and genetic variation of candidate solutions.

rows.name: Genie clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that normally selects a nearest pair by single-link distance and, when cluster-size inequality exceeds a threshold, restricts that selection to pairs containing a globally smallest cluster.

rows.name: Gibbs sampling
rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that repeatedly draws a coordinate or block from its full conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining coordinates.

rows.name: Girvan–Newman community detection
rows.definition: A divisive community-detection algorithm that repeatedly removes an edge with maximal current shortest-path betweenness and recalculates affected betweenness scores, using the resulting connected-component splits to form a hierarchy of graph-vertex groups.

rows.name: GloVe
rows.definition: Word-vector learning from global word co-occurrence statistics.

rows.name: Best-first beam search with a global frontier cap
rows.definition: A best-first search procedure that limits the entire open frontier to a fixed number of nodes by discarding the worst-ranked frontier nodes when that capacity is exceeded.

identities.value: Best-first beam search with a global frontier cap

rows.name: Global Kernel K-Means
rows.definition: An incremental kernel clustering algorithm that adds a singleton datum cluster at each stage, runs kernel k-means from each such candidate partition, and retains the candidate with the smallest feature-space clustering error.

rows.name: Gradient-weighted class activation mapping
rows.definition: A convolutional-network localization method weighting activation maps by spatially averaged gradients of a selected target output.

rows.name: Gradient boosting machine
rows.definition: Boosting that adds predictors fitted to negative loss-function gradients.

rows.name: Gradient norm clipping
rows.definition: A gradient transformation that bounds the Euclidean norm of a chosen joint parameter-gradient vector by uniformly scaling it down to a positive threshold when its norm exceeds that threshold, while retaining smaller gradients.

rows.name: Graph attention network
rows.definition: A graph neural architecture that updates node representations using learned attention weights over graph neighborhoods.

rows.name: Graph degree linkage
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that merges the pair with greatest symmetric graph-degree affinity, formed by summing products of cluster-normalized incoming and outgoing edge weights on a fixed directed nearest-neighbor graph.

rows.name: Graph isomorphism network
rows.definition: A graph neural architecture using multilayer perceptrons on sums of neighboring representations and a separately weighted self-representation.

rows.name: GraphSAGE
rows.definition: An inductive graph representation architecture that learns neighborhood aggregation functions to generate node embeddings from features.

rows.name: Greedy best-first search
rows.definition: A best-first search algorithm that prioritizes open nodes by a heuristic estimate of remaining cost to a goal, without adding the cost already incurred to that priority.

rows.name: Grid Long Short-Term Memory
rows.definition: A neural architecture family whose grid blocks couple hidden representations across computational dimensions while maintaining separate gated memory flows along their LSTM-equipped axes, including depth and data dimensions.

rows.name: Grid-search reduction for fair classification
rows.definition: A fairness-aware classification reduction that evaluates cost-sensitive classifier best responses over a grid of Lagrange-multiplier-derived costs and selects a deterministic candidate with a desired empirical accuracy–fairness tradeoff.

rows.name: Grid Search for Hyperparameter Optimization
rows.definition: A hyperparameter optimization procedure that evaluates a finite Cartesian product of chosen values for each configuration variable and selects a configuration using its validation performance.

rows.name: Group-topic model
rows.definition: A probabilistic model family jointly assigning topics to relation-bearing events and topic-specific latent groups to entities, using event text and event-specific group-pair agreement probabilities.

rows.name: Guided Genetic Algorithm
rows.definition: The Lau–Tsang genetic-search framework that uses shared adaptive solution-feature penalties both to modify fitness and to construct per-chromosome gene weights that bias crossover and mutation.

rows.name: Guided Grad-CAM
rows.definition: A visualization method combining an upsampled Grad-CAM localization map with guided-backpropagation input-space scores.

rows.name: Guided local search
rows.definition: A local-search metaheuristic that repeatedly minimizes an objective augmented by feature penalties, increasing selected penalties at local minima to alter subsequent search while retaining solutions according to the original objective.

rows.name: Gumbel-Softmax relaxation
rows.definition: A continuous relaxation of a finite categorical random variable obtained by applying softmax to independent Gumbel-perturbed log weights divided by a positive temperature, producing a differentiable random vector in the simplex interior.

rows.name: Gumbel-Top-k trick
rows.definition: A categorical sampling construction that adds independent standard Gumbel noise to each category’s log weight and returns the indices of the k largest perturbed values in descending order, producing an ordered sample without replacement under successive renormalization of the remaining weights.

rows.name: Gustafson guided-walk Metropolis sampler
rows.definition: A continuous-state Metropolis sampler that augments a univariate state with a binary direction, proposes a half-normal displacement along that direction, retains direction after acceptance and reverses it after rejection.

rows.name: Hungry Hungry Hippos layer
rows.definition: A sequence layer that combines projected queries, keys and values with shift and diagonal state-space models, using multiplicative interactions to associate and retrieve sequence information.

rows.name: HAC-E network clustering
rows.definition: A hierarchical network-clustering variant that greedily guides agglomeration by the observed edge density between two vertex groups and uses the resulting group hierarchy for link-probability estimation.

rows.name: HAC-ES network clustering
rows.definition: A hierarchical network-clustering variant that guides agglomeration by the sum of cross-group edge density and Jaccard overlap of the groups’ external neighboring vertices.

rows.name: HAC-ML network clustering
rows.definition: A greedy network-clustering algorithm that builds a hierarchical stochastic block structure by merging groups with the least loss of profiled network likelihood, using separate Bayesian criteria to collapse terminal groups and stop top-level merging.

rows.name: HAC-Q network clustering
rows.definition: A hierarchical network-clustering variant that uses a degree-corrected modularity contribution to guide group merges and retains hierarchical group structure for link prediction rather than using only a modularity-selected flat partition.

rows.name: HDBSCAN
rows.definition: Hierarchical density-based clustering that selects clusters across density scales.

rows.name: HITS hub and authority ranking
rows.definition: A link-analysis ranking algorithm that constructs a query-focused directed page graph and alternately propagates authority scores from incoming hub scores and hub scores from outgoing authority scores, normalizing the vectors and selecting their largest coordinates.

rows.name: HSAT
rows.definition: A GSAT variant that breaks ties among best-scoring variable flips by choosing the variable flipped least recently in the current attempt, using a fixed arbitrary order for ties among never-flipped variables.

rows.name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for differentiable continuous targets that augments positions with momenta, proposes a state through reversible volume-preserving numerical Hamiltonian dynamics, and applies a Metropolis correction for the Hamiltonian change.

rows.name: Hammerstein model
rows.definition: A real-valued, single-input single-output, discrete-time deterministic nonlinear dynamical model family formed by a memoryless static nonlinearity followed by a causal linear time-invariant system.

rows.name: Hammerstein–Wiener model
rows.definition: A real-valued, single-input single-output, discrete-time deterministic dynamical model family formed by a memoryless static input function, a causal linear time-invariant block, and a memoryless static output function, with nonlinear behavior supplied by the static functions.

rows.name: HashCRBM
rows.definition: A conditional RBM training and prediction method that uses spectral hashing of inputs to retrieve distinct training-output configurations and normalizes the conditional model only over that input-dependent support.

rows.name: Helmholtz machine
rows.definition: A hierarchical probabilistic neural model that pairs a top-down generative model with a separately parameterized bottom-up recognition model approximating the distribution of hidden causes given observed input.

rows.name: Heuristic tree sampling
rows.definition: A randomized estimator of additive properties of an implicit rooted tree that processes ordered strata using one sampled representative and an accumulated weight per stratum.

rows.name: Scaled Legendre HiPPO operator
rows.definition: The HiPPO projection operator using the uniform measure over the full elapsed interval from zero to the current time, with scaled-Legendre coefficients evolving under explicitly time-dependent linear memory dynamics.

rows.name: High-order polynomial projection operators
rows.definition: A family of time-dependent operators that represents a signal's past by coefficients of its optimal finite-dimensional polynomial approximation under a chosen time-varying measure.

rows.name: Hidden Markov decision tree
