rows.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family that extends a probabilistic hierarchical decision tree by coupling each decision level to the same level at the previous time.

rows.name: Hidden Markov model
rows.definition: A sequence model whose hidden Markov states generate observations through state-dependent emission distributions.

rows.name: Hidden Markov model with auxiliary memory
rows.definition: A hidden-state symbol-sequence model family in which paired states write emitted symbols to auxiliary memory and later read them to condition emissions and memory-dependent state transitions.

identities.value: Hidden Markov model with auxiliary memory

rows.name: Hidden Markov random field
rows.definition: A latent-variable graphical-model family whose unobserved label field has the Markov property on a specified neighborhood graph, with observations conditionally independent across sites given the labels and each depending only on its corresponding hidden state.

rows.name: Hidden Markov tree
rows.definition: A latent-variable model on a fixed rooted tree in which hidden states factor into a root distribution and conditionally independent parent-to-child transitions, with observations emitted independently by their corresponding hidden states.

rows.name: Hidden–observed pair Markov random field
rows.definition: A latent-variable spatial-model family in which each site contains a hidden label and an observation, and their joint paired field has a normalized Gibbs factorization on a specified neighborhood graph, without requiring either marginal field to be Markov on that graph.

rows.name: Hidden semi-Markov model
rows.definition: A latent-state sequence-model family that assigns explicit distributions to state sojourn durations, with state changes governed by an embedded transition process and observations conditioned on the hidden states.

rows.name: Hierarchical harmonium
rows.definition: A labeled harmonium model family coupling binary words, Gaussian image features and binary category indicators to shared Gaussian latent variables, with a proper joint Gaussian precision and classification through posterior label probabilities.

rows.name: Hierarchical log-bilinear language model
rows.definition: A next-word language architecture that computes one linear context feature vector and uses its dot products with internal-node vectors to assign normalized vocabulary-tree probabilities, summing path probabilities when a word has multiple codes.

rows.name: Hierarchical mixture of experts
rows.definition: A conditional mixture-model family that organizes output experts as leaves of a tree and forms each leaf’s mixture weight by multiplying input-dependent probabilistic gates along its root-to-leaf path.

rows.name: Hierarchical pachinko allocation model
rows.definition: A pachinko topic-model family that associates word-emission distributions with internal topic nodes as well as terminal topics, allowing document tokens to use multiple paths and emit from different levels of a topic DAG.

rows.name: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model
rows.definition: A neural next-word architecture that factors word probabilities along a binary vocabulary tree and shares a nonlinear branch predictor conditioned on context-word embeddings and a separate embedding of the current tree node.

identities.value: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model

rows.name: Hierarchical softmax
rows.definition: A neural categorical-output component that assigns a probability to each vocabulary leaf by multiplying normalized branch probabilities along its path through a word tree.

rows.name: Hill climbing
rows.definition: A family of local-improvement search procedures that replaces a current solution with a strictly better neighbor and stops when no improving neighbor exists under the specified move set.

rows.name: Hyperband
rows.definition: A hyperparameter resource-allocation algorithm that runs successive-halving brackets with different initial configuration counts and starting budgets, balancing broad early screening against more conservative evaluation.

rows.name: IA3 Activation Rescaling
rows.definition: A transformer adaptation method that learns task-specific vectors to rescale attention key/value channels and intermediate feedforward activations while freezing the pretrained network parameters.

identities.value: Infused Adapter by Inhibiting and Amplifying Inner Activations

rows.name: ID3
rows.definition: Decision-tree induction that selects categorical attributes by information gain.

rows.name: IDA* with an Incremental Model
rows.definition: An iterative-deepening heuristic search algorithm that learns a conditional model of search-tree cost increments, predicts later cost thresholds to target increased expansion counts, and completes the goal-finding iteration by branch-and-bound.

rows.name: IHSAT
rows.definition: A GenSAT variant that chooses the least recently flipped variable among all flips that do not decrease the satisfied-clause count, or among all variables when no nondecreasing flip exists.

rows.name: INLA group node conflict diagnostic
rows.definition: A group-wise Bayesian model diagnostic for latent Gaussian models that uses two INLA fits per selected group to compare remaining-data and within-group information about its latent linear predictor vector. Fitted mean and covariance summaries yield a quadratic conflict score with a rank-based Gaussian chi-square reference. Nuisance-parameter updating, replication dependence and numerical rank choices determine the interpretation.

rows.name: Identity-initialized rectified recurrent neural network
rows.definition: A recurrent neural sequence architecture using rectified linear hidden units, zero initial recurrent biases, and a trainable recurrent matrix initialized to the identity, with a scaled-identity initialization variant for shorter memory.

rows.name: Improved consistency training
rows.definition: The consistency-model training procedure of Song and Dhariwal that learns directly from paired shared-noise data perturbations using a stop-gradient teacher with current student parameters, a Pseudo-Huber discrepancy, revised noise weighting and sampling, and a staged increase in noise-discretization intervals.

rows.name: Improved limited discrepancy search
rows.definition: Korf’s discrepancy-search variant that uses a supplied maximum search depth and remaining discrepancy count to generate each path to that depth in the pass corresponding to its exact number of nonpreferred choices, avoiding the original method’s repeated maximum-depth paths.

rows.name: Incremental Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: An EM variant for independent observed cases that refreshes selected cached case posteriors at the current parameters and then fits parameters using the complete collection of refreshed and retained case expectations.

rows.name: Independence Metropolis–Hastings sampling
rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler whose proposal distribution is fixed independently of the current state, with proposal-density ratios still included in acceptance.

rows.name: InfoNCE
rows.definition: A contrastive log-softmax objective that identifies a joint positive among sampled candidates and, under independent marginal-negative sampling, gives an expectation-level lower bound on mutual information.

rows.name: Infomax Independent Component Analysis
rows.definition: An unsupervised source-separation learning algorithm that adjusts an invertible square linear transform and biases by the ordinary gradient of the differential entropy of coordinatewise sigmoid-transformed outputs.

rows.name: Information maximizing self-augmented training
rows.definition: A discrete representation-learning procedure that combines self-augmentation consistency with an information objective, using categorical outputs for clustering or a pairwise approximation for multi-bit hashing.

rows.name: Input-output hidden Markov model
rows.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family whose discrete hidden-state transitions and state-specific observation distributions depend on the current external input.

rows.name: Integrated gradients
rows.definition: A feature-attribution method that integrates a prediction's input gradients along the straight path from a chosen baseline to the input.

rows.name: Interaction Network
rows.definition: A graph-based neural architecture that applies a shared relation model to supplied directed attributed object relations, sums predicted effects for each receiver, and applies a shared object model to predict object outputs, with an optional aggregated global readout.

rows.name: Interpolated variational information bound
rows.definition: A family of multi-sample mutual-information lower bounds that interpolates the critic’s empirical partition estimate with a positive variational normalizer inside a ratio, connecting NWJ and InfoNCE parameterizations.

identities.value: Nonlinearly interpolated mutual information lower bound

rows.name: Interpolation consistency training
rows.definition: A semi-supervised training procedure that encourages a student’s prediction at an interpolated pair of unlabeled inputs to match the same interpolation of predictions from a moving-average teacher, while also fitting labeled examples.

rows.name: Invariant information clustering
rows.definition: A neural clustering procedure that maximizes mutual information between discrete cluster-assignment variables for paired unlabeled samples, estimating their joint distribution from the network’s soft assignment probabilities.

rows.name: Isomap
rows.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm that estimates manifold geodesic distances by shortest paths in a local neighborhood graph and applies classical multidimensional scaling to those estimated distances.

rows.name: Iterated conditional modes
rows.definition: A deterministic conditional-mode optimization algorithm that repeatedly updates one variable to a mode of its conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining variables, seeking a coordinatewise mode of a fixed joint distribution.

rows.name: Iterated local search
rows.definition: A metaheuristic that builds a single search trajectory among solutions returned by an embedded optimizer by perturbing the current accepted solution, rerunning that optimizer, and applying an acceptance criterion to the resulting candidate.

rows.name: Iterated Wiener Filter
rows.definition: An iterative MAP image-denoising algorithm that majorizes a fixed Product of Student-t log-potential and alternates response-dependent precision updates with a Gaussian Wiener linear solve.

rows.name: Iterative broadening
rows.definition: A tree-search strategy that repeats depth-first search with increasing limits on the number of ordered successors considered at each parent, widening the allowed search tree after an unsuccessful pass.

rows.name: Iterative conditional estimation
rows.definition: An incomplete-data parameter-estimation procedure that repeatedly replaces a chosen complete-data estimator by its conditional expectation given observed data under the current parameter estimate.

rows.name: Iterative-deepening A-star search
rows.definition: A heuristic search algorithm that repeats depth-first passes bounded by f=g+h, starting with the start-state heuristic and raising each cutoff to the smallest value that exceeded the preceding cutoff.

rows.name: Iterative weakening
rows.definition: A policy for selecting a sufficient search bias by trying a fixed family of search-space restrictions in increasing order of known evaluation complexity, progressively admitting more costly searches until an acceptable result is found.

rows.name: Joint term-citation model
rows.definition: A latent-factor document model that shares each document's fixed topic proportions between categorical term and citation-incidence channels, with topic-specific distributions for each channel.

rows.name: Joint unsupervised learning of deep representations and image clusters
rows.definition: An image representation and clustering procedure that alternates periods of graph-based agglomerative merging with convolutional-network updates from a cluster-derived weighted triplet objective.

identities.value: Joint unsupervised learning of deep representations and image clusters

rows.name: Jumping Knowledge network
rows.definition: A graph neural architecture that sends intermediate node representations from multiple neighborhood-aggregation depths to a final layer-aggregation mechanism.

rows.name: KADABRA adaptive betweenness approximation
rows.definition: An adaptive sampling algorithm for static-graph betweenness that averages internal-node indicators of uniformly sampled shortest paths and stops when node-specific confidence radii meet an additive tolerance or a predetermined sample horizon is reached.

rows.name: KADABRA balanced bidirectional shortest-path sampling
rows.definition: A shortest-path sampling algorithm that expands complete breadth-first-search frontiers from opposite endpoints according to frontier edge volume, then samples a connecting edge and its two path segments with shortest-path-count weights to obtain a uniform shortest path.

rows.name: k-means
rows.definition: Clustering that partitions observations around centroids by minimizing within-cluster squared distances.

rows.name: Karmarkar–Karp differencing
rows.definition: A two-way number-partitioning heuristic that repeatedly replaces the two largest remaining nonnegative residuals by their difference, then reconstructs a partition whose absolute sum difference is the final residual.

rows.name: Kernel K-Means
rows.definition: A clustering algorithm that alternates nearest-feature-mean assignments and mean updates to minimize within-cluster squared distances in a kernel-defined feature space, with an observation-weighted extension.

rows.name: Kernel Principal Component Analysis
rows.definition: A spectral feature-extraction algorithm that performs principal component analysis on centered implicit feature vectors by eigendecomposing a positive-semidefinite kernel Gram matrix and evaluating new-point coordinates through kernel expansions.

rows.name: Kernel SHAP
rows.definition: A model-agnostic Shapley-attribution estimator using weighted linear regression on feature-presence subsets.

rows.name: Key-Value Memory Network
rows.definition: A neural memory architecture that answers a query by attending to keys and reading corresponding values from supplied key-value memory pairs, with repeated query updates and a learned candidate-answer scorer.

rows.name: Kleinberg nonprincipal hub-authority extraction
rows.definition: A link-analysis procedure that uses paired nonprincipal eigenvectors of the authority and hub Gram matrices of a query-focused directed page graph, selecting extreme coordinates to obtain additional hub and authority lists that implicitly summarize different linked topics.

rows.name: Knuth backtrack-tree estimation
rows.definition: A randomized estimator of additive properties of a fixed backtracking tree that follows a sampled root-to-terminal path and weights each visited node contribution by the inverse probability of reaching it.

rows.name: L2-loss support vector data description
rows.definition: A support-vector data-description algorithm that learns a feature-space sphere using squared-hinge penalties on squared-distance violations, yielding a unique optimal center, squared radius and slack vector for a fixed positive penalty and feature map.

rows.name: Limited-memory BFGS
rows.definition: A limited-memory quasi-Newton optimization method using a bounded history of parameter and gradient differences to compute approximate inverse-Hessian search directions.

rows.name: Local interpretable model-agnostic explanations
rows.definition: A prediction-explanation method fitting an interpretable surrogate to locally weighted samples of a model's behavior.

rows.name: Laplacian Eigenmaps
rows.definition: A spectral embedding algorithm that builds a weighted neighborhood graph and uses nonconstant generalized eigenvectors of its graph Laplacian to place strongly connected points close together.

rows.name: Large margin nearest neighbor
rows.definition: A supervised metric-learning method that fits a positive-semidefinite distance matrix by pulling fixed same-class target neighbors together while penalizing margin violations by differently labeled observations.

rows.name: LargeVis
rows.definition: A dimensionality-reduction and graph-visualization algorithm that constructs an approximate weighted nearest-neighbor graph and learns low-dimensional coordinates with sampled attractive-edge and repulsive-pair likelihood terms.

rows.name: Late Dropout
rows.definition: A neural-network training procedure that begins without dropout, activates it after a selected training cutoff and continues optimization with dropout for the remaining steps.

rows.name: Latent Dirichlet allocation
rows.definition: A hierarchical model for collections of discrete observations in which each document draws a Dirichlet-distributed mixture over a fixed finite set of topics, and each token draws a topic and then an observation from that topic’s categorical distribution.

rows.name: Layer-wise adaptive moments
rows.definition: A gradient optimizer that combines coordinate-wise Adam moment scaling with layer-wise normalization of the resulting update direction, optionally including weight decay, and scales each block by a function of its parameter norm and a global learning rate.

rows.name: Layer-wise adaptive rate control
rows.definition: A parameter-block learning-rate control rule whose clipping form limits a vanilla stochastic-gradient step by using the smaller of a global learning rate and a trust coefficient times the block parameter-norm to gradient-norm ratio.

rows.name: Layer-wise adaptive rate scaling
rows.definition: A gradient optimization method that multiplies each selected layer or parameter block direction by a scalar based on its current weight L2 norm relative to its gradient L2 norm, together with a trust coefficient and global learning rate. Its stated weight-decay extension scales a combined gradient-and-decay direction using a sum-of-norms denominator and can be composed with momentum.

rows.name: Layer-wise relevance propagation
rows.definition: A prediction-decomposition framework that redistributes relevance backward through a classifier's computational layers toward its input features.

rows.name: Learned-Norm Pooling Unit
rows.definition: A parameterized neural unit that pools a group of learned linear projections by the power mean of their absolute deviations from learned centers, with a trainable norm order for each unit.

rows.name: Learning Fair Representations
rows.definition: A prototype-based representation-learning algorithm that jointly balances reconstruction, supervised prediction and differences between group-average prototype assignment probabilities.

rows.name: Learning Hidden Unit Contributions
rows.definition: A neural acoustic-model adaptation method that learns speaker- or environment-specific multipliers on hidden-unit activations while keeping the pretrained network weights and biases fixed during test-time adaptation.

rows.name: Learning real-time A*
rows.definition: A real-time heuristic learning algorithm that moves to a minimum estimated path-cost neighbor, stores that minimum edge-cost-plus-heuristic value at the state it leaves, and retains learned state estimates across repeated problem-solving trials with the same goals.

rows.name: Least-angle regression
rows.definition: Regression that advances along directions equiangular to predictors most correlated with the residual.

rows.name: Leave-one-out mutual information upper bound
rows.definition: An expectation-level upper bound on mutual information that compares a known conditional density for each paired sample with a mixture of conditional densities from the other independent inputs in its batch.

rows.name: Lee-Seung Multiplicative Updates
rows.definition: The Lee-Seung block multiplicative algorithms for nonnegative matrix factorization, using objective-specific elementwise factor rescaling to reduce squared reconstruction error or generalized KL divergence with the other factor held fixed.

rows.name: Lifted structured embedding loss
rows.definition: A metric-learning objective that penalizes a positive pair’s Euclidean distance against negative distances incident to either endpoint, using a squared hinge and a hard maximum or its log-sum-exp relaxation.

rows.name: Limited discrepancy search
rows.definition: A backtracking tree-search strategy that repeatedly explores paths under an increasing upper limit on deviations from a successor-ordering heuristic; in the original binary formulation, taking the nonpreferred child consumes one discrepancy.

rows.name: Linear discriminant analysis
rows.definition: Gaussian discriminant classification sharing one covariance matrix across classes.

rows.name: Linear state-space layer
rows.definition: A sequence-to-sequence layer defined by discretizing a linear continuous-time state-space system, with a state recurrence and, for zero initial state, an equivalent convolutional representation plus a direct input term.

rows.name: Lipschitz individual fairness
rows.definition: An individual-fairness criterion requiring the distance between the output distributions assigned by a randomized classifier to any two individuals to be no greater than their task-specific similarity distance.

rows.name: List-augmented recurrent neural network
rows.definition: A recurrent sequence architecture whose neural controller accesses an external list through a movable read/write head, learning continuous mixtures of left movement, right movement, insertion and optional no-operation updates.

rows.name: Liu modified discrete-state Gibbs sampler
rows.definition: A discrete conditional sampling algorithm that proposes a category from the full conditional distribution with the current category excluded, then applies a Metropolis correction to preserve the original conditional distribution.

rows.name: Llama clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that unions each current cluster with a nearest neighboring cluster in successive rounds and retains the resulting overlapping sets as a directed acyclic clustering structure with multiple possible parents.

identities.value: Lattices by Leveraging Agglomerations and Multiple Ancestors

rows.name: Low-rank adaptation
rows.definition: A parameter-efficient adaptation method that freezes pretrained weights and learns additive low-rank matrix updates.

rows.name: Local outlier factor
rows.definition: An unsupervised local outlier-scoring procedure that compares each observation's inverse mean reachability distance with those of its tie-inclusive nearest neighbors and returns their mean density ratio.

rows.name: Locally Linear Embedding
rows.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm that learns sparse, sum-to-one linear reconstructions of each point from nearby points and computes embedding coordinates by minimizing reconstruction error with those same weights.

rows.name: Log-bilinear language model
rows.definition: A next-word language architecture that linearly combines position-specific transforms of context-word embeddings and normalizes their bilinear compatibility with candidate-word embeddings over the vocabulary.

rows.name: Logarithmic opinion pool
rows.definition: A probability-aggregation method that forms a normalized weighted geometric mean of expert distributions over the same outcomes, using nonnegative exponent weights that sum to one.

rows.name: Lookup Conditional Distribution Prediction
rows.definition: A computational variant of conditional distribution prediction that precomputes or memoizes fixed-model subtree expansion-count estimates for type and remaining-cost contexts, then reuses those estimates when predicting a complete IDA* iteration from a shallow search frontier.

rows.name: MEX Operator
rows.definition: A scalar aggregation operator that returns log(mean(exp(xi times input)))/xi for a nonzero real parameter xi, with its continuous zero-parameter extension equal to the arithmetic mean.

rows.name: Mamba sequence architecture
rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture built from repeated blocks containing input-dependent selective state-space transformations.

rows.name: Manifold Mixup
rows.definition: A neural-network training procedure that interpolates paired examples’ representations at a selected network layer and interpolates their labels with the same coefficient, then trains the entire network on the mixed representation-target pairs.

rows.name: Markov Chain Monte Carlo Stochastic Approximation Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: A stochastic approximation EM extension that advances a persistent latent-state Markov chain targeting the conditional distribution at the current parameter, updates an averaged sufficient statistic from that state, and maximizes the resulting complete-data objective.

identities.value: Markov Chain Monte Carlo Stochastic Approximation Expectation Maximization

rows.name: Markov decision process
rows.definition: A sequential decision model with states, actions, Markov transitions, and rewards.

rows.name: Markov random field
rows.definition: An undirected graphical probability model associating potential functions with variable groups.

rows.name: Matching pursuit
rows.definition: A greedy fixed-dictionary approximation algorithm that repeatedly selects a unit-norm atom by its absolute correlation with the current residual and subtracts the residual projection onto that atom.

rows.name: MAXCFU
rows.definition: A multivariate sensitivity algorithm that uses gradient ascent through fitted additive-noise models to search for large counterfactual prediction discrepancies under bounded correlations of structural error terms.

rows.name: MAX–MIN Ant System
rows.definition: An ant-colony optimization algorithm that reinforces solution components from a single selected best ant per iteration, constrains pheromone trails between lower and upper limits, and initializes trails high to encourage early exploration.

rows.name: Maximum coding likelihood estimation
rows.definition: A conditional parameter-estimation method that selects mutually non-neighboring sites in a Markov field and maximizes their joint conditional likelihood, which factors into sitewise full conditionals given the remaining observed sites.

rows.name: Maximum pseudolikelihood estimation
rows.definition: A parameter-estimation method that maximizes the product of a specified model’s sitewise full conditional probabilities or densities evaluated at the observed configuration.

rows.name: Maxout Unit
rows.definition: A parameterized neural unit that outputs the maximum of a finite group of learned affine functions of its input.

rows.name: Mean-field Boltzmann learning
rows.definition: A deterministic approximation to Boltzmann-machine parameter learning that substitutes mean-field phase statistics for stochastic equilibrium correlations in the positive-minus-negative weight update.

rows.name: Mean shift
rows.definition: Mode-seeking clustering that moves candidate centers toward local density maxima.

rows.name: Mean Teacher
rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that regularizes a student prediction toward the prediction of a same-architecture teacher whose parameters are an exponential moving average of successive student parameters, alongside labeled classification loss.

rows.name: Memory Network
rows.definition: A family of learning models that combines an addressable memory with input conversion, memory updating, output inference and response components, allowing predictions to use stored information through learned or otherwise specified component implementations.

rows.name: Memory-reduced best-first beam search for sequence decoding
rows.definition: A capacity-limited variant of per-length best-first sequence beam search that, when its chosen total queue capacity is reached, removes the worst-scoring active hypothesis from the earliest active sequence length.

identities.value: Memory-reduced best-first beam search for sequence decoding

rows.name: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm
rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a Gaussian step with drift proportional to the target log-density gradient and corrects the asymmetric proposal with an accept/reject test.

rows.name: Metropolis–Hastings sampling
rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that proposes a new state from a specified transition distribution and accepts it with the smaller of one and the target-density ratio multiplied by the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio, otherwise retaining the current state.

rows.name: Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampling
rows.definition: A componentwise Monte Carlo scheme that uses Metropolis–Hastings transitions targeting full conditional distributions for one or more coordinate blocks, optionally combined with exact Gibbs updates for other blocks.

rows.name: Min-conflicts heuristic
rows.definition: A constraint-repair value-selection heuristic that uses a complete assignment to choose a value for a conflicted variable with as few conflicts as possible, breaking tied minimum choices randomly in the inspected formulation.

rows.name: MixMatch
rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that averages predictions over augmented unlabeled inputs, sharpens the resulting soft targets, mixes augmented labeled and unlabeled input-target pairs, and optimizes labeled cross-entropy plus an unlabeled squared-probability loss.

rows.name: MixUp
rows.definition: A training-data interpolation procedure that fits a predictor to convex combinations of example inputs and their corresponding targets using the same random mixing coefficient for both.

rows.name: Mixed-membership model for scientific publications
rows.definition: A generative document model in which one Dirichlet-distributed membership vector mixes aspect-specific word distributions for an abstract and aspect-specific reference distributions for its bibliography.

rows.name: Mixed memory Markov model
rows.definition: A family of compact temporal probability models whose component transition distributions are convex mixtures of transition tables indexed by a single selected predecessor lag or component.

rows.name: Mixture density network
rows.definition: A neural conditional-density architecture whose input-dependent outputs parameterize the mixing weights and component distributions of a finite mixture over target variables.

rows.name: Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analyzers
rows.definition: A finite Gaussian mixture whose components each have a linear standard-normal latent factor and component-specific isotropic observation noise, giving covariance W_i W_i^T+sigma_i^2 I and probabilistic assignments to local principal-component models.

identities.value: Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analyzers
Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analysers

rows.name: Momentum contrast
rows.definition: A contrastive representation-learning mechanism that maintains a queue of encoded negative keys and produces new keys with an encoder updated by an exponential moving average of the query encoder.

rows.name: Monotonic Gaussian process with virtual derivatives
rows.definition: A Gaussian-process inference procedure that promotes monotonicity in selected input coordinates by combining observed outputs with finite virtual derivative-sign factors and approximating the resulting posterior using expectation propagation.

identities.value: Monotonic Gaussian process with virtual derivatives

rows.name: Monte Carlo Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: An expectation-maximization method that approximates the current conditional expected complete-data log objective by Monte Carlo integration and maximizes that sampled objective to update the parameters.

rows.name: Multi-class N-pair loss
rows.definition: A supervised metric-learning objective that averages a joint positive-versus-multiple-negative log-softmax loss across a batch of positive pairs drawn from distinct classes.

rows.name: Multi-label text mixture model
rows.definition: A generative multi-label document model that selects a label subset and a mixture supported on that subset, then generates each word through one of the selected labels and its class-specific word distribution.

rows.name: Multiclass Multiple Kernel Maximum Margin Clustering
rows.definition: A multiclass unsupervised clustering procedure that jointly fits shared nonnegative multiple-kernel weights and latent class-score functions using winner-margin cutting planes and repeated convex conic fits.

identities.value: Multiclass Multiple Kernel Maximum Margin Clustering

rows.name: Multiple-testing node conflict diagnostic
rows.definition: A Bayesian evidence-synthesis diagnostic that partitions information at replicated separator nodes, stacks declared contrasts between transformed copies, and uses their joint covariance and a multivariate reference distribution to assess global and multiplicity-adjusted local conflict. Its single-step max-absolute-statistic adjustment accounts for correlation within an explicitly selected family of comparisons.

rows.name: Multiple-try Metropolis
rows.definition: A Metropolis sampling algorithm that selects a candidate from several weighted forward proposals, draws a backward reference set containing the original state, and corrects acceptance using the ratio of their total weights.

rows.name: Multiple-try Metropolis within Gibbs
rows.definition: A coordinate-update sampler that applies a multiple-try Metropolis transition to a conditional target while holding all other coordinates fixed.

rows.name: Multiview Kernel K-Means
rows.definition: A multiview clustering algorithm that alternates kernel k-means on a power-weighted combination of fixed view kernels with simplex view-weight updates minimizing within-cluster feature variance.

rows.name: Multiway Karmarkar–Karp differencing
rows.definition: A multiway number-partitioning heuristic that represents partial partitions by normalized bin-load vectors and repeatedly combines two selected subpartitions by pairing their largest and smallest bin loads, retaining one composition until a full partition remains.

rows.name: Muon optimizer
rows.definition: A neural-network optimization method that approximately orthogonalizes momentum-based matrix updates using Newton–Schulz iterations.

rows.name: Mutual information neural estimation
rows.definition: A mutual-information estimation procedure that trains a neural statistics function to maximize a Donsker–Varadhan objective contrasting joint samples with product-of-marginals samples, using stochastic optimization and an optional moving-average denominator for gradient estimation.

rows.name: NAdam
rows.definition: An Adam-family optimizer combining adaptive moment scaling with a Nesterov-style momentum update.

rows.name: Normalized temperature-scaled cross entropy loss
rows.definition: A contrastive cross-entropy objective that uses cosine-normalized, temperature-scaled similarities to identify a paired positive representation among nonself candidates, including that positive in the denominator.

rows.name: Naive Bayes
rows.definition: Probabilistic classification assuming feature independence conditional on the class.

rows.name: Natural Evolution Strategies
rows.definition: A family of black-box optimization algorithms that adapts a parameterized search distribution using estimates of the natural gradient of expected fitness with respect to the distribution parameters.

rows.name: NeXO ontology alignment
rows.definition: An iterative ontology-alignment algorithm that combines shared-terminal set overlap with parent and child neighborhood similarities, then greedily selects one-to-one term correspondences while rejecting reversed ancestor relations.

rows.name: NeXO ontology construction
rows.definition: A network-based ontology-construction procedure that starts from a probabilistic hierarchy of gene communities, removes unsupported binary restrictions to permit multiway joins, and adds supported second-parent connections to produce an overlapping term hierarchy.

rows.name: Neal backtracking-suppressed MCMC
rows.definition: A finite-state MCMC construction that augments a reversible chain with its preceding state and replaces a conditional resampling step with a balanced conditional kernel that suppresses immediate backtracking while preserving the target marginal.

rows.name: Nearest-neighbor-chain clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that follows a chain of nearest clusters until its last pair are reciprocal nearest neighbors, merges that pair, and reuses the remaining chain; for suitable distance updates, sorting and relabeling the recorded merges produces a valid stepwise hierarchy.

rows.name: Nearest-neighbor distance-norm data description
rows.definition: A one-class decision rule that forms the ordered distances from a query to its first k reference neighbors and accepts the query when the L_r norm of that distance vector is at most a supplied threshold, with self inclusion and infinite padding when fewer than k references exist.

rows.name: Nearest-neighbor ratio data description
rows.definition: A target-class data-description algorithm that scores a query by its distance to a nearest reference observation divided by that observation's nearest-other-reference spacing, and accepts queries whose ratio does not exceed a chosen threshold, where the denominator and neighbor-selection conventions are well defined.

identities.value: Nearest neighbor distance ratio data description

rows.name: Neighbourhood components analysis
rows.definition: A supervised metric-learning algorithm that learns a linear transformation by maximizing the expected number of correctly classified training examples under stochastic leave-one-out neighbor selection.

rows.name: Neural autoregressive distribution estimator
rows.definition: A fully visible autoregressive density model whose ordered variable conditionals are computed by neural networks that share input-to-hidden parameters and recursively reuse prefix computations.

rows.name: Neural GPU
rows.definition: A recurrent neural architecture that embeds a complete symbolic sequence in a spatial state grid and repeatedly applies shared convolutional gated updates before reading an output sequence from the final grid.

rows.name: Neural network pushdown automaton
rows.definition: A recurrent state-controller architecture whose signed action output pushes or removes fractional quantities of input symbols on an external stack and whose read neurons return the symbol content within a fixed depth at the stack top.

rows.name: Neural probabilistic language model
rows.definition: A neural finite-context language architecture that jointly learns a shared word-embedding lookup and a nonlinear predictor of the next-word distribution using concatenated context embeddings and a vocabulary softmax.

rows.name: Neural variational inference and learning
rows.definition: A method for jointly training a directed latent-variable model and an amortized stochastic inference network by maximizing a variational log-likelihood bound, using score-function inference gradients with learned baselines and adaptive learning-signal normalization.

rows.name: Newman greedy modularity algorithm
rows.definition: Newman’s direct edge-fraction-matrix algorithm for greedy agglomerative community detection, which starts with singleton vertices, joins adjacent communities using modularity changes, updates the matrix by combining their rows and columns, and selects a maximum-modularity cut along the resulting merge history.

rows.name: Newman random-walk betweenness matrix computation
rows.definition: An exact network-analysis algorithm that computes random-walk betweenness from an embedded inverse of a grounded graph Laplacian, explicitly enumerates source–target pairs, and averages their incident-current magnitudes with a specified endpoint convention.

identities.value: Newman matrix algorithm for random-walk betweenness

rows.name: Nguyen–Wainwright–Jordan variational bound
rows.definition: A variational lower bound on Kullback–Leibler divergence that subtracts a product-distribution exponential critic moment from a joint-distribution critic expectation when specialized to mutual information.

rows.name: Noh–Rieger random-walk centrality
rows.definition: A node-scoring method for an undirected random walk that divides each node’s stationary visitation probability by its integrated excess return probability, yielding a centrality whose reciprocal differences determine pairwise mean first-passage-time asymmetry.

identities.value: Random walk centrality of Noh and Rieger

rows.name: Noisy-OR belief network
rows.definition: A directed acyclic binary probabilistic network that models a node’s inactivity as the product of a leak-failure factor and failure factors for its active parents.

rows.name: Noisy rectifier
rows.definition: A stochastic activation that adds zero-mean noise to a preactivation and then applies the positive-part rectifier, producing h=max(0,a+z).

rows.name: Non-local block
rows.definition: A neural-network component that aggregates input-dependent pairwise contributions from positions across a representation, projects the aggregate and adds it to the original features through a residual connection.

rows.name: Non-conjugate variational message passing
rows.definition: An approximate inference algorithm that restricts variational blocks to exponential families and updates their natural parameters by matching expected-log-factor gradients through the sufficient-statistic covariance.

rows.name: Nonlinear autoregressive model with exogenous inputs
rows.definition: A discrete-time nonlinear input-output model family whose current output is a function of finite lagged outputs and exogenous inputs, plus an additive current error, without explicit dependence on lagged errors.

identities.value: Nonlinear autoregressive model with exogenous inputs

rows.name: Nonlinear autoregressive moving average model with exogenous inputs
rows.definition: A discrete-time nonlinear input-output model family whose current output is a function of finite lagged outputs, exogenous inputs and errors, plus an additive current error.

identities.value: Nonlinear autoregressive moving average model with exogenous inputs

rows.name: Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
rows.definition: A matrix-decomposition method that represents or approximates a nonnegative data matrix as the product of two entrywise nonnegative factor matrices, so each data column is expressed by additive nonnegative combinations of basis columns.

rows.name: Nonparametric Bayes pachinko allocation model
rows.definition: A Bayesian pachinko topic-model family using coupled hierarchical Dirichlet-process allocations to infer occupied supertopics and shared subtopics, with subtopic allocation groups determined by latent supertopic assignments.

rows.name: Nonreversible Metropolis uniform update
rows.definition: A Metropolis transition algorithm that retains a signed uniform acceptance variable, updates it by wrapped translation, and rescales it after an accepted state proposal to preserve a joint target distribution while changing the temporal dependence of acceptance decisions.

rows.name: Norm-stabilizer
rows.definition: A recurrent-network regularization procedure that adds a penalty on the average squared change in Euclidean norm between successive selected activation or state vectors during training.

rows.name: Novelty SAT heuristic
rows.definition: A clause-based SAT local-search heuristic that ranks candidate flips by total violation count with oldest-variable tie breaks, normally selects the best candidate, and sometimes selects the second-best when the best was the most recently flipped variable in that clause.

rows.name: Novelty+ SAT heuristic
rows.definition: A Novelty extension that, at each SAT search step, chooses a random variable from a randomly selected unsatisfied clause with a fixed walk probability and otherwise uses Novelty’s recency-conditioned best/second-best selector.

rows.name: NovoGrad
rows.definition: A stochastic gradient optimizer that rescales each parameter block gradient by a scalar running second moment of that block gradient norm before accumulating momentum, with an optional weight-decay contribution added after gradient normalization.

rows.name: Nu support vector classification
rows.definition: A supervised binary-classification algorithm that jointly fits a regularized kernel hyperplane and a nonnegative margin level, using nu to reward that level relative to linearly penalized margin shortfalls.

rows.name: Nu support vector regression
rows.definition: A supervised regression algorithm that jointly fits a regularized kernel expansion and a nonnegative constant epsilon-insensitive tube half-width, using nu to penalize the width relative to linearly penalized residual excesses.

rows.name: OPTICS
rows.definition: Density-based clustering analysis that orders observations using reachability across neighborhood scales.

identities.value: Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure

rows.name: OPTICS outlier factor
rows.definition: An unsupervised local outlier-scoring procedure that uses self-inclusive, tie-inclusive nearest neighborhoods to compute inverse mean neighbor-radius reachability and averages neighbor-to-query density ratios.

rows.name: Oja Learning Rule
rows.definition: A single-output linear-neuron learning rule that combines a Hebbian input-output weight increment with an output-squared weight decay, obtained as a first-order approximation to Euclidean-normalized Hebbian learning.

rows.name: One-class support vector machine
rows.definition: A support-estimation algorithm that optimizes a kernel feature-space score relative to the origin using a norm penalty, a learned offset and linearly penalized shortfalls controlled by nu, then accepts a query when its score meets the learned threshold.

rows.name: One-vs-one N-pair loss
rows.definition: A supervised metric-learning objective that sums separate positive-versus-negative softplus comparisons for each anchor in a batch of positive pairs from distinct classes.

rows.name: Beam decoding with a monotone-score stopping certificate
rows.definition: A layer-based sequence beam decoder that retains the best completed hypothesis seen so far and stops when the highest current prefix score cannot exceed that incumbent under a score that never increases with extension.

identities.value: Beam decoding with a monotone-score stopping certificate

rows.name: Order-agnostic NADE training
rows.definition: A stochastic training procedure that shares neural conditional parameters across variable orderings and estimates the order-averaged NADE log-likelihood objective using a sampled observed prefix and losses for all remaining variables.

rows.name: No-U-Turn sampler (original slice formulation)
rows.definition: The original 2014 slice-based NUTS algorithm, which adapts a Hamiltonian trajectory’s length through randomly directed binary-tree doubling and selects a valid next state while enforcing subtree U-turn and reversibility conditions.

rows.name: Orthogonal least squares forward selection
rows.definition: A greedy fixed-candidate regression algorithm that repeatedly adds the column giving the largest reduction in squared residual after joint least-squares refitting over the augmented selected span.

rows.name: Orthogonal matching pursuit
rows.definition: A greedy fixed-dictionary approximation algorithm that selects an atom correlated with the current residual and recomputes the approximation as the orthogonal projection of the signal onto the span of all selected atoms.

rows.name: Otsu thresholding
rows.definition: A histogram-based threshold-selection algorithm that partitions ordered gray levels by maximizing class-weighted between-class variance, equivalently minimizing within-class variance for a fixed histogram.

rows.name: Overlapping hierarchical clustering (OHC)
rows.definition: A graph-based agglomerative clustering algorithm that expands clusters across increasing distance thresholds when the change in induced edge density is within a tolerance, retaining overlapping groups in a cluster-inclusion hierarchy.

rows.name: PERCH clustering
rows.definition: An online hierarchical clustering algorithm that inserts observations near existing leaves of a binary cluster tree and uses masking and balance rotations to revise subtree placement.

identities.value: Purity Enhancing Rotations for Cluster Hierarchies

rows.name: PHATE
rows.definition: A dimensionality-reduction algorithm that computes diffusion transition probabilities, measures Euclidean distances between their negative-log rows, and uses metric multidimensional scaling to embed those potential distances.

identities.value: Potential of Heat Diffusion for Affinity-based Transition Embedding

rows.name: PaCMAP
rows.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm that embeds neighbor, mid-near and farther point pairs using separate attractive and repulsive losses whose relative weights change through three optimization phases.

rows.name: Pachinko allocation model
rows.definition: A topic-model family that generates each word by traversing a directed acyclic graph from a root through topic nodes to a word leaf, using probability distributions over each node's children.

rows.name: Pachinko allocation topics over time model
rows.definition: A topic-model family combining pachinko allocation paths with topic-specific continuous timestamp densities at multiple path levels, so that words and observed times jointly inform topics and their co-occurrence structure.

identities.value: Pachinko allocation topics over time model

rows.name: PageRank
rows.definition: A link-analysis ranking algorithm that assigns node scores using a random walk mixing normalized outgoing-link transitions with teleportation to a specified restart distribution, under an explicit policy for nodes with no outgoing weight.

rows.name: Paired differencing method
rows.definition: A two-way number-partitioning heuristic that sorts residuals and differences disjoint adjacent pairs in whole rounds, carries an unpaired residual forward, and repeats until one residual remains, producing a partition whose subset cardinalities differ by at most one.

rows.name: Pairwise Markov chain
rows.definition: A hidden-state sequence-model family in which the joint process of a hidden variable and its corresponding observation is first-order Markov, without requiring either marginal process to be Markov or observations to be conditionally independent given the hidden path.

rows.name: Pairwise Markov tree
rows.definition: A latent-variable tree-model family whose paired hidden and observed states factor into a root distribution and parent-to-child conditional kernels on a fixed rooted tree, without requiring the hidden marginal to be Markov on that tree.

rows.name: Papadimitriou 2-SAT random walk
rows.definition: A randomized 2-SAT search procedure that starts from any complete truth assignment and repeatedly selects an unsatisfied clause and flips a uniformly chosen literal’s variable until a satisfying assignment is reached or a selected move budget ends.

rows.name: Parallel alternating Newton-like algorithm for APM
rows.definition: A block-alternating Newton-like method for fitting an admixture of Poisson Markov random fields through a sparsity-penalized nodewise Poisson regression surrogate, alternating topic coefficients with document-specific simplex weights and parallelizing independent subproblems.

identities.value: Parallel alternating Newton-like algorithm for APM

rows.name: Parallel tempering
rows.definition: A population Monte Carlo method that combines within-temperature target-preserving updates with corrected exchanges between replicas targeting differently tempered densities.

rows.name: ParamILS
rows.definition: An iterated-local-search framework for algorithm configuration that searches finite parameter settings through one-parameter neighborhood moves, perturbations and random restarts, with a replaceable procedure for comparing configurations on target-algorithm runs.

rows.name: Parameter-Expanded Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: An expectation-maximization construction that fits an expanded complete-data model with auxiliary parameters, reduces its result to the original observed-data parameterization through a likelihood-preserving map, and resets the auxiliary parameters before the next iteration.

rows.name: Parametric UMAP
rows.definition: A parametric dimensionality-reduction algorithm that trains a neural mapping from input points to embedding coordinates using sampled attractive and repulsive losses derived from a UMAP neighborhood graph.

identities.value: Parametric Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection

rows.name: Tree-size estimation by partial backtracking
rows.definition: A randomized backtracking-tree estimator that explores a uniformly selected subset of successors at each visited branching point and uses inverse inclusion weights to estimate the total cost of candidate examinations in the corresponding complete fixed search.

rows.name: Partial least squares regression
rows.definition: Regression using latent components chosen to capture predictor-response covariance.

rows.name: Partially noncentered GLMM variational inference
rows.definition: A Bayesian generalized linear mixed-model inference procedure that uses cluster-specific partial noncentering to define independent Gaussian fixed-effect and transformed random-effect blocks, factors an inverse-Wishart random-effect covariance, and alternates nonconjugate Gaussian message proposals with an exact covariance coordinate.

rows.name: Partially observable Markov decision process
rows.definition: A Markov decision model in which observations provide incomplete information about the current state.

rows.name: Particle swarm optimization
rows.definition: A population-based optimization method that moves candidate particles through a search space using retained velocities and stochastic attraction toward remembered personal and shared best positions.

rows.name: Path integral clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that merges clusters with the greatest increase in their size-normalized sums of discounted random-walk paths when paths are allowed through the proposed union.

identities.value: Agglomerative clustering via maximum incremental path integral

rows.name: Patience-controlled FCFS beam decoding
rows.definition: A generalization of first-come, first-served sequence beam decoding that retains beam width k for continuing hypotheses but uses a positive patience factor p to stop when the accumulated completed-hypothesis count reaches at least k·p.

identities.value: FCFS beam decoding with controlled patience

rows.name: Maximum candidates per node in sequence beam pruning
rows.definition: A sequence-beam pruning procedure that limits how many retained candidate extensions may come from the same predecessor hypothesis, discarding a candidate when the allowed number of better-scoring siblings is already retained.

identities.value: Maximum candidates per node in sequence beam pruning

rows.name: Persistent contrastive divergence
rows.definition: A learning algorithm that estimates an energy model’s negative-phase statistics with Markov chains whose states persist across parameter updates, rather than restarting those chains at the current data minibatch.

rows.name: Pi-model
rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that combines labeled cross-entropy with squared disagreement between two stochastic predictions of the same input from a shared-parameter network, propagating gradients through both predictions.

rows.name: PoClustering edge-clique-cover heuristic
rows.definition: An approximate PoClustering algorithm that incrementally extends and prunes clique sets to cover the edges of dissimilarity-threshold graphs, retaining a potentially smaller overlapping cluster family than exhaustive maximal-clique enumeration.

rows.name: PointNet
rows.definition: A neural architecture for unordered point clouds that applies shared pointwise feature extraction and symmetric max pooling to produce a global representation, with a per-point prediction extension for segmentation.

rows.name: PointNet++
rows.definition: A hierarchical point-set neural architecture that repeatedly samples centroids, groups metric neighborhoods and applies local PointNet feature extraction, with multi-scale or multi-resolution constructions for variable sampling density.

rows.name: Poisson generalized root model
rows.definition: A generalized root probability model on unbounded nonnegative integer counts, with factorial base measures and symmetric products of j-th roots involving at most j distinct variables, normalizable for every finite parameter tensor on a finite variable set.

rows.name: Poisson square root graphical model
rows.definition: A square-root graphical model on unbounded nonnegative integer counts with factorial base measures, unary square-root and linear count terms and pairwise products of square roots of counts, normalizable for all finite symmetric interaction and unary parameters on a finite graph.

identities.value: Poisson square root Markov random field

rows.name: Population Based Augmentation
rows.definition: An augmentation-schedule learning procedure that jointly trains a population of child classifiers and evolves their augmentation hyperparameters by copying successful members and perturbing their policies over training time.

rows.name: Population-based incremental learning
rows.definition: An optimization method that samples candidate solutions from a probability-vector representation and incrementally moves that representation toward high-evaluation sampled solutions, with probability-vector mutation in its basic formulation.

rows.name: Population Based Training
rows.definition: A population-based neural-network training procedure that interleaves parameter updates with performance-guided copying of partially trained models and exploration of hyperparameters, producing training trajectories with changing hyperparameter settings.

rows.name: Power iteration clustering
rows.definition: A clustering algorithm that uses an early-stopped power iteration of a normalized similarity matrix to embed observations and then applies k-means to their embedding coordinates.

rows.name: Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson sampling
rows.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target whose proposal combines the current state with an independent draw from that reference using a scalar autoregressive coefficient.

rows.name: Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
rows.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that preconditions the potential-gradient drift by the reference covariance and uses a scalar Crank–Nicolson autoregressive update.

rows.name: Bounded word reward with predicted length
rows.definition: A sequence rescoring method that adds a fixed word reward only up to an input-specific length predicted from encoder states, replacing a corpus-level generation-ratio cap with Lpred(x).

identities.value: Bounded word reward with predicted length

rows.name: Principal Curves
rows.definition: A nonlinear statistical summary defined by a smooth curve that is self-consistent for a data distribution: almost every point on the curve equals the conditional mean of observations whose nearest-point projection lands there.

rows.name: Probabilistic latent semantic analysis
rows.definition: A latent-class model of document–word or other dyadic co-occurrences that represents their joint probability as a mixture of conditionally independent distributions over the two observed entities.

rows.name: Probabilistic Principal Component Analysis
rows.definition: A linear Gaussian latent-variable model with a standard-normal latent prior and isotropic observation noise, whose maximum-likelihood loading subspace corresponds to leading principal components under the stated covariance-rank conditions.

rows.name: Product of experts
rows.definition: A probabilistic model family that combines expert factors over the same observations by multiplying their values and normalizing the product over the observation space.

rows.name: Product of hidden Markov models
rows.definition: A sequence-model family that multiplies the marginal probabilities assigned to a complete observation sequence by several hidden Markov models and normalizes the product over sequences of the same length.

rows.name: Product of Student-t
rows.definition: A normalized energy-based density on continuous observations formed from products of Student-t-shaped factors of linear filter responses, with a positive finite joint normalizer and optional grouping of filter energies.

rows.name: Professor forcing
rows.definition: An adversarial recurrent-network training procedure that retains teacher-forced likelihood learning while training an auxiliary discriminator and the generator to reduce differences between teacher-forced and free-running behavior sequences.

rows.name: Prototype-based domain description
rows.definition: A one-class decision rule that accepts a query when its metric distance to at least one prototype, plus that prototype's stored radius offset, is no greater than a common threshold.

rows.name: Proximal policy optimization
rows.definition: A family of policy-gradient algorithms alternating collected interaction data with repeated optimization of a surrogate objective using clipping or an adaptive KL penalty.

rows.name: Pseudo-Label
rows.definition: A semi-supervised neural-network training procedure that recomputes hard labels from the model’s most probable class for unlabeled examples and jointly fits observed and generated targets using a scheduled weight on the unlabeled loss.

rows.name: Pseudo-linear regression estimation
rows.definition: A family of recursive coefficient estimators that uses the current regressor as a surrogate prediction sensitivity, omitting derivatives through parameter-dependent regressors such as past estimated residuals.

rows.name: Q-learning
rows.definition: A model-free reinforcement-learning method that incrementally updates action-value estimates toward an observed reward plus the discounted maximum estimated value of the next state’s actions.

rows.name: Q-routing
rows.definition: A distributed adaptive packet-routing algorithm that learns destination-specific delivery-time estimates by combining observed local queue and transmission delays with a neighboring node’s estimate of remaining delivery time.

rows.name: Quadratic discriminant analysis
rows.definition: Gaussian discriminant classification with class-specific covariance matrices.

rows.name: Quadratic Poisson graphical model
rows.definition: A graphical probability model on nonnegative integer counts whose joint log mass contains unary linear terms, site quadratic terms and symmetric pairwise count products, with parameters restricted to make its infinite-support partition function finite.

rows.name: Rectified Adam
rows.definition: An Adam-family optimizer that rectifies its adaptive update using a time-dependent estimate of the effective history of the second-moment statistic.

rows.name: Recursive best-first search with controlled re-expansion
rows.definition: An RBFS variant that estimates subtree evaluation-value distributions and inflates backed-up values to make later visits expand geometrically more nodes, while retaining original lower-bound information for solution-cost pruning.

identities.value: Recursive best-first search with controlled re-expansion

rows.name: REINFORCE
rows.definition: A family of stochastic reinforcement-learning update rules that multiply a sampled reward relative to an admissible baseline by the derivative of the log probability of the sampled action or unit output, with a nonnegative learning-rate factor.

rows.name: RMSprop
rows.definition: An adaptive gradient optimization method that normalizes coordinate updates using an exponentially weighted estimate of squared gradients.

rows.name: R-Novelty SAT heuristic
rows.definition: A Novelty-derived SAT heuristic whose choice between the best and second-best flips depends on their objective-score gap when the best variable was most recently flipped; its original 1997 search strategy also includes a periodic random clause-variable move.

rows.name: R-Novelty+ SAT heuristic
rows.definition: The 1999 R-Novelty extension that replaces its periodic random override with a fixed per-step probability of a random clause-variable flip and otherwise uses the recency- and score-gap-dependent R-Novelty selector.

rows.name: ROCK clustering
rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering procedure that merges clusters using shared-neighbor link counts divided by a cluster-size normalization derived from a neighborhood model.

rows.name: Radicchi edge-clustering community detection
rows.definition: A divisive graph-community algorithm family that repeatedly removes edges with the lowest modified cycle-based edge-clustering score, updates affected local scores and forms a component hierarchy, optionally retaining branches through the paper’s original-adjacency strong or weak community tests.

rows.name: RandAugment
rows.definition: An image-augmentation procedure that applies a uniformly sampled sequence of operations sharing one magnitude parameter, reducing augmentation selection to tuning the operation count and shared magnitude on the target task.

rows.name: Random Online Aggressive Racing
rows.definition: An algorithm-configuration procedure that proposes uniformly random parameter settings and compares each challenger with an incumbent through adaptive evaluations on shared problem instances and random seeds, without fitting a predictive performance model.

rows.name: Random-only abstraction for abstraction sampling
rows.definition: A randomized abstraction rule for graphical-model sampling that uniformly permutes the current search nodes and divides that order into groups of nearly equal cardinality, within which the surrounding sampler selects and importance-weights representatives.

rows.name: Random Search for Hyperparameter Optimization
rows.definition: A hyperparameter optimization procedure that draws trial configurations independently from a specified search distribution, evaluates their validation performance, and selects a favorable evaluated configuration without adapting subsequent draws to observed trial scores.

rows.name: Random-walk Metropolis–Hastings sampling
rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a new state by adding an increment drawn from a fixed distribution independent of the current state.

rows.name: Randomized latent score conflict diagnostic
rows.definition: A Bayesian hierarchical-model diagnostic that freezes draws from a parent posterior excluding selected child data, draws child latent parameters conditionally, and compares derivatives of an expanded conditional log prior with scores of conditional-prior replicates. The resulting randomized tail values are examined and optionally combined as a model-conflict summary, with calibration depending on the actual sampling law, score direction and aggregation.

rows.name: Rank-based Ant System
rows.definition: An Ant System variant that weights pheromone deposits from a selected number of the current iteration’s best tours by rank and adds a separate reinforced contribution from the best-so-far tour.

rows.name: RAPID support vector data description sampling
rows.definition: A density-based training-subset selection method for support vector data description that prefilters low-density observations and greedily removes high-density inliers while testing a retained-density threshold on the original inlier set.

identities.value: RAPID support vector data description sampling
Reducing samples by pruning of inlier densities

rows.name: Rate-adapting Poisson model
rows.definition: A harmonium model family coupling unbounded visible Poisson counts to finite binomial hidden variables through bilinear interactions that shift conditional log rates and binomial logits.

rows.name: ReMixMatch
rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that adjusts weak-view guessed labels toward an estimated class prior, sharpens and anchors those soft targets across strong augmentations, and trains with interpolated pairs plus unmixed consistency and rotation-prediction losses.

rows.name: Real-time A*
rows.definition: A real-time heuristic search algorithm that moves to a neighbor with minimum edge-cost-plus-heuristic estimate and stores the second-best such estimate at the state it leaves, using bounded lookahead or initial heuristics for previously unvisited states.

rows.name: Real-time recurrent learning
rows.definition: A recurrent-network training algorithm that propagates state sensitivities to adjustable weights forward in time and contracts those sensitivities with current supervised output errors to form weight updates.

rows.name: Real-valued neural autoregressive density estimator
rows.definition: A fully visible neural autoregressive density architecture for real-valued vectors that shares input-to-hidden parameters across ordered scalar conditional mixture-density models.

rows.name: Reciprocal-nearest-neighbors supported clustering
rows.definition: A hierarchical clustering algorithm that follows nearest-neighbor chains to construct sub-clustering trees around reciprocal pairs, prunes overly deep nodes into singleton trees, and recursively clusters representatives formed from the supporting pairs.

rows.name: Rectified flow
rows.definition: A transport-learning method that regresses a velocity field on endpoint differences along straight interpolations of coupled samples and uses the resulting ordinary differential equation to transport the source distribution, optionally repeating rectification using the learned endpoint coupling.

rows.name: RNN-NADE
rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture in which a deterministic recurrent state supplies parameters of a NADE output distribution, combining temporal recurrence with normalized within-frame autoregressive conditionals.

identities.value: Recurrent neural network neural autoregressive distribution estimator

rows.name: RNN-RBM
rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture in which a deterministic recurrent network with its own hidden state supplies parameters of a conditional RBM that models each next visible vector.

identities.value: Recurrent neural network restricted Boltzmann machine

rows.name: Recurrent temporal restricted Boltzmann machine
rows.definition: A recurrent neural sequence architecture whose deterministic state is a conditional RBM hidden-probability vector and sets the next step’s hidden bias, with visible observations drawn from that step’s RBM marginal.

rows.name: Recursive best-first search
rows.definition: A recursive search algorithm that explores the best stored subtree alternative within an upper bound and conditionally passes a previously backed-up value to regenerated children, retaining path and sibling information instead of the full best-first frontier.

rows.name: Recursive prediction-error estimation
rows.definition: A recursive parameter-estimation method that incrementally adjusts a parameterized predictor using prediction errors and search directions based on its parameter sensitivities.

rows.name: Regularized information maximization
rows.definition: A discriminative clustering framework that fits conditional class probabilities by maximizing empirical input–assignment mutual information penalized by classifier complexity, with linear and kernel softmax configurations.

rows.name: Rejection-driven independence Metropolis sampling
rows.definition: An independence Metropolis sampler whose proposals are generated by a rejection procedure with a fixed possibly non-dominating envelope, followed by a Metropolis correction for the resulting clipped proposal law.

rows.name: Rejection sampling
rows.definition: A random-variate generation algorithm that draws proposals from a normalized envelope dominating an unnormalized target and accepts each with the target-to-envelope ratio, yielding independent target draws with fresh independent random trials.

rows.name: Relevance-weighted topic distillation
rows.definition: An iterative web-link ranking procedure that alternates authority and hub score propagation using destination relevance for forward contributions and source relevance for backward contributions, retaining inter-site links and restricting authority eligibility by relevance.

rows.name: Relevant component analysis
rows.definition: A partially supervised linear metric-learning procedure that estimates within-group covariance from positive equivalence constraints and whitens the representation using that covariance.

rows.name: Replicated Softmax
rows.definition: An undirected document model with binary hidden units and a length-dependent set of categorical word units that share visible-to-hidden weights, with hidden biases scaled by document length.

rows.name: Residual Attention Network
rows.definition: A convolutional-network architecture that stacks attention modules combining trunk features with learned bottom-up and top-down masks through residual attention gating.

rows.name: Resilient backpropagation
rows.definition: A gradient-based optimization method that adapts coordinate step sizes using successive gradient signs and takes sign-directed parameter steps.

rows.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine Collaborative Filtering
rows.definition: A family of shared-parameter restricted Boltzmann models for categorical user-item ratings, with a user-specific visible set and optional conditioning on the item-observation mask and low-rank factorization of rating interactions.

rows.name: Retentive network
rows.definition: An autoregressive neural sequence architecture that stacks pre-normalized residual blocks combining gated multi-scale retention with feedforward transformations, with parallel, recurrent and chunkwise forms of retention.

rows.name: Reweighted wake-sleep
rows.definition: A learning procedure for paired generative and inference networks that uses multiple inference samples and normalized importance weights for generative-model updates, with recognition updates from importance-weighted observed-data samples, model-generated sleep samples, or both.

rows.name: Riondato–Kornaropoulos fixed-sample betweenness approximation
rows.definition: A fixed-sample graph betweenness approximation algorithm that chooses a sample count using a VC-dimension bound for shortest-path incidence ranges, then averages internal-vertex indicators from independent uniform endpoint-pair and conditional shortest-path draws.

rows.name: Robust adaptive Metropolis
rows.definition: An adaptive random-walk Metropolis algorithm that updates the proposal shape factor by a rank-one transformation driven by the proposal direction and the difference between its acceptance probability and a chosen target rate.

rows.name: Robust continuous clustering
rows.definition: A clustering algorithm that optimizes one representative per observation using squared data fidelity and robust attraction along a neighborhood graph, then extracts groups from thresholded connectivity between the optimized representatives.

rows.name: Role-author-recipient-topic model
rows.definition: A family of message-content models in which actors have latent-role distributions and ordered sender-role/recipient-role pairs determine topic mixtures, with token-level or message-level role assignments.

rows.name: Structured state space sequence model
rows.definition: A structured linear state-space sequence model whose normal-plus-low-rank state matrix is transformed to diagonal-plus-low-rank form for efficient convolution-kernel computation and recurrent sequence evaluation.

rows.name: Diagonal structured state space model
rows.definition: A diagonal state-space sequence-model family that computes its discretized convolution kernel by a Vandermonde product, with explicit choices of discretization, state-matrix constraint and initialization.

rows.name: SHapley additive explanations
rows.definition: An additive feature-attribution framework assigning Shapley values to a prediction through a specified function for evaluating feature subsets.

rows.name: Submodular pick LIME
rows.definition: A method selecting a budgeted set of local LIME explanations by greedily increasing weighted coverage of explanatory features.

rows.name: STRIPS planning method
rows.definition: A symbolic planning method that uses means–ends analysis and theorem proving over world models to construct a sequence of operators satisfying a goal.

rows.name: SamplePairing
rows.definition: An image-classification augmentation procedure that averages an anchor image with a randomly selected training image using equal pixel weights and trains against the anchor image’s label, with a training schedule that includes phases without pairing.

rows.name: Sarsa
rows.definition: An on-policy temporal-difference control algorithm that updates the current state-action value toward the observed reward plus the discounted estimated value of the next action selected by the same behavior policy.

rows.name: Scheduled sampling
rows.definition: An autoregressive sequence-training procedure that chooses between reference and model-produced previous outputs as feedback, using a schedule that progressively reduces the probability of reference feedback.

rows.name: SeLa
rows.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that alternates neural pseudo-label prediction and dataset-wide self-labelling through an entropy-regularized balanced optimal-transport assignment.

identities.value: Self-labelling via simultaneous clustering and representation learning
Self-labeling via simultaneous clustering and representation learning

rows.name: Semidefinite Maximum Margin Clustering
rows.definition: A binary clustering procedure that relaxes latent label-equivalence matrices to a convex semidefinite program for a fixed-kernel soft-margin objective and recovers soft assignments from the leading matrix eigenvector.

rows.name: Semiparametric linear programming regression
rows.definition: A supervised regression algorithm that jointly fits a finite kernel expansion and an unpenalized supplied parametric basis by minimizing fixed epsilon-insensitive residual loss plus an L1 penalty on the kernel expansion coefficients, yielding a linear program.

rows.name: Semiparametric support vector regression
rows.definition: A supervised regression algorithm that jointly fits an unpenalized finite expansion of supplied basis functions and a kernel component, minimizing fixed epsilon-insensitive residual loss plus a squared feature-space norm penalty on the kernel component.
