rows.name: Semisupervised Semidefinite Maximum Margin Clustering
rows.definition: A semisupervised binary margin-learning procedure that adds observed-label pair constraints and labeled-to-unlabeled linkage constraints to the Xu2004 semidefinite label-matrix relaxation.

rows.name: Separator-node conflict diagnostic
rows.definition: A Bayesian graphical-model diagnostic that duplicates a selected separator node or node vector, partitions the information informing it, and compares the resulting partition-specific distributions on a declared scale. It assesses local incompatibility through explicitly chosen discrete agreement, signed-tail, radial or density-level scores, with nuisance dependence handled by a specified split or cut.

rows.name: A-star beam search for sequence decoding
rows.definition: A sequence-decoding beam framework that ranks active hypotheses by accumulated score plus an optimistic future-score heuristic, uses shorter length to break score ties, and limits accepted expansions to k hypotheses per sequence length.

identities.value: A-star beam search for sequence decoding
A* beam search for sequence decoding

rows.name: Best-first beam search with per-length budgets
rows.definition: The sequence-decoding beam procedure of Meister, Vieira and Cotterell that prioritizes active hypotheses by decreasing accumulated score, breaks score ties by shorter length, and limits accepted expansions to k hypotheses at each sequence length without a future-score heuristic.

identities.value: Best-first beam search with per-length budgets

rows.name: Sequential Model-based Algorithm Configuration
rows.definition: A sequential algorithm-configuration procedure that uses random-forest performance models to propose parameter settings and compares candidate settings with an incumbent through adaptive evaluations on shared problem instances and random seeds.

rows.name: Set Transformer
rows.definition: A neural encoder-decoder architecture for permutation-invariant set-input prediction that uses attention to encode interactions among elements and learned seed queries to aggregate encoded features.

rows.name: Set Transformer++
rows.definition: A Set Transformer architecture revision that replaces its induced-attention encoder blocks with set-normalized blocks retaining identity residual paths, while preserving the aggregation and decoder.

rows.name: Shared inverse-lengthscale variational sparse-spectrum inference
rows.definition: The Tan–Ong–Nott–Jasra sparse-spectrum regression inference procedure that alternates a Gaussian nonconjugate variational proposal for a shared inverse-lengthscale vector with full Gaussian coefficient and half-Cauchy-derived scale-coordinate updates.

rows.name: Sigmoid belief network
rows.definition: A directed acyclic probabilistic network of binary variables whose forward conditional probabilities are logistic functions of weighted parent states and a bias.

rows.name: SimCLR
rows.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that jointly trains an encoder and a nonlinear projection head by contrasting two augmented views of each image against other images’ views in the same minibatch.

identities.value: Simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations

rows.name: SimNet
rows.definition: A neural architecture family built from learned template-similarity operations and MEX log-mean-exp operations that combine shifted similarity responses, with local sharing and pooling available in image-processing configurations.

rows.name: SimSiam
rows.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that trains a shared encoder and predictor to match the encoder output of another augmented view using symmetric negative cosine similarity with stopped gradients on each target output.

rows.name: Simple recursive best-first search
rows.definition: A recursive best-first search procedure that initializes generated children from their static evaluation values, explores the best child within an alternative-derived bound, and backs up returned values to decide which subtree to revisit.

rows.name: Simulated annealing
rows.definition: A stochastic optimization procedure that explores candidate configurations with temperature-controlled acceptance of cost-increasing moves and progressively cools that acceptance process to concentrate search on low-cost configurations.

rows.name: Single-step parametric maxT inference
rows.definition: A simultaneous-inference procedure for a declared family of linear functions of model parameters that standardizes joint estimates and uses the maximum absolute statistic under a centered multivariate normal or t reference to compute multiplicity-adjusted tests and a common critical value for simultaneous intervals. Exact or asymptotic validity depends on the joint sampling law and covariance estimation.

rows.name: Slice sampling
rows.definition: An auxiliary-variable Monte Carlo method that augments a target density with a uniform height below its graph and updates the state using a transition preserving the uniform distribution on the resulting density slice.

rows.name: Smart Augmentation
rows.definition: A learned augmentation procedure that trains a network to synthesize examples from same-class inputs while receiving both a within-class reference loss and feedback through the target classifier’s training loss.

rows.name: SmoothGrad
rows.definition: A sensitivity-map smoothing method that averages maps computed on Gaussian-noise perturbations of an input.

rows.name: Soft actor-critic
rows.definition: An off-policy actor-critic algorithm fitting a stochastic policy and soft value functions under a reward-plus-policy-entropy objective.

rows.name: Space-Alternating Generalized Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: A generalized expectation-maximization method that updates selected parameter blocks using block-specific hidden-data spaces or valid objective-improvement surrogates, refreshing the conditional expectation or surrogate at the current estimate before the next block.

rows.name: Sparse additive generative model
rows.definition: A generative model family for categorical text data that forms word probabilities by normalizing a background log-frequency vector plus sparse component deviations, allowing multiple generative facets to combine additively in log space.

rows.name: Sparse Expectation Maximization
rows.definition: An EM variant that updates relative latent-state probabilities within selected plausible sets while preserving their total mass and all outside probabilities, and fits parameters using the resulting full distributions with occasional complete posterior refreshes.

rows.name: Sparse pachinko allocation inference
rows.definition: An approximate pachinko-allocation fitting procedure that restricts token path resampling to currently active document topics and word-associated subtopics, interleaving full sampling with pruning and optionally growing the training corpus incrementally.

rows.name: Sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process exact moment matching
rows.definition: An uncertain-input prediction algorithm that analytically integrates sine/cosine feature moments of a fixed sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process posterior over an independently prescribed Gaussian input and represents the output by a Gaussian with the resulting exact mean and covariance.

rows.name: Sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process linearized uncertain-input prediction
rows.definition: A local uncertain-input prediction algorithm for a fixed sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process posterior that linearizes the posterior mean at the Gaussian input mean, freezes the conditional variance there, and uses the resulting approximate mean and covariance for a Gaussian output representation.

rows.name: Sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process regression
rows.definition: A Gaussian-process regression model family whose latent prior is a finite sum of paired sine and cosine features with independent Gaussian coefficients, yielding a stationary finite-spectral covariance and Gaussian fixed-input predictions under Gaussian observation noise.

rows.name: Spatial Transformer
rows.definition: A learnable neural-network component that predicts an input-dependent spatial transformation and uses the resulting sampling grid to warp an image or feature tensor.

rows.name: Speaker-Adaptive Training LHUC
rows.definition: An acoustic-model training procedure that jointly learns shared network parameters, training-speaker hidden-unit contribution transforms and a speaker-independent transform by routing each training example through either its own speaker transform or the shared transform.

rows.name: Speaker-Dependent Pooling Adaptation
rows.definition: An acoustic-model adaptation procedure that updates a small set of pooling parameters for a target speaker using decoded acoustic targets while retaining the shared feature projections and output model in its pool-only form.

rows.name: Spectral hashing
rows.definition: An unsupervised binary-code learning algorithm that approximates a spectral similarity-preservation objective using a PCA-aligned rectangular data model and zero-thresholded single-coordinate analytic modes.

rows.name: Square root graphical model
rows.definition: A family of finite undirected graphical probability models that retains univariate base measures while coupling specified square roots of sufficient statistics through unary terms and a symmetric quadratic form, with parameters restricted to a finite joint partition function.

rows.name: Squeeze-and-Excitation block
rows.definition: A neural-network feature recalibration component that globally averages each channel, transforms the resulting descriptor through a learned bottleneck, and applies sigmoid-derived channel weights to the input feature maps.

rows.name: Stack-augmented recurrent neural network

Title: Conflict Diagnostics in Directed Acyclic Graphs, with Applications in Bayesian Evidence Synthesis
Authors: Anne M. Presanis, David Ohlssen, David J. Spiegelhalter, Daniela De Angelis
Date: Wed Oct  2 09:21:28 2013

Complex stochastic models represented by directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) are increasingly employed to synthesise multiple, imperfect and disparate sources of evidence, to estimate quantities that are difficult to measure directly. The various data sources are dependent on shared parameters and hence have the potential to conflict with each other, as well as with the model. In a Bayesian framework, the model consists of three components: the prior distribution, the assumed form of the likelihood and structural assumptions. Any of these components may be incompatible with the observed data. The detection and quantification of such conflict and of data sources that are inconsistent with each other is therefore a crucial component of the model criticism process. We first review Bayesian model criticism, with a focus on conflict detection, before describing a general diagnostic for detecting and quantifying conflict between the evidence in different partitions of a DAG. The diagnostic is a p-value based on splitting the information contributing to inference about a "separator" node or group of nodes into two independent groups and testing whether the two groups result in the same inference about the separator node(s). We illustrate the method with three comprehensive examples: an evidence synthesis to estimate HIV prevalence; an evidence synthesis to estimate influenza case-severity; and a hierarchical growth model for rat weights.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Abstract

Complex stochastic models represented by directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) are increasingly employed to synthesise multiple, imperfect and disparate sources of evidence, to estimate quantities that are difficult to measure directly. The various data sources are dependent on shared parameters and hence have the potential to conflict with each other, as well as with the model. In a Bayesian framework, the model consists of three components: the prior distribution, the assumed form of the likelihood and structural assumptions. Any of these components may be incompatible with the observed data. The detection and quantification of such conflict and of data sources that are inconsistent with each other is therefore a crucial component of the model criticism process. We first review Bayesian model criticism, with a focus on conflict detection, before describing a general diagnostic for detecting and quantifying conflict between the evidence in different partitions of a DAG. The diagnostic is a $p$-value based on splitting the information contributing to inference about a “separator” node or group of nodes into two independent groups and testing whether the two groups result in the same inference about the separator node(s). We illustrate the method with three comprehensive examples: an evidence synthesis to estimate HIV prevalence; an evidence synthesis to estimate influenza case-severity; and a hierarchical growth model for rat weights.

The term node‐splitting may be confusing for some, because the treatment network represents a comparison as an edge rather than a node (or vertex). However, in the Bayesian hierarchical model, each parameter is represented by a node in a directed acyclic graph. When one of these parameters is split into two to evaluate conflict, the term node‐splitting is used. A node‐splitting analysis is thus performed separately for each of the comparisons in the treatment network on which both direct and indirect evidence are available, to assess evidence consistency.

Node‐splitting models are very similar to consistency models, except that the direct evidence for d _{x,y} is used alone to estimate {d}_{x,y}^{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{i}\mathrm{r}}, and a network meta‐analysis of the remaining evidence is used to estimate {d}_{x,y}^{\mathrm{i}\mathrm{n}\mathrm{d}}. The heterogeneity parameter σ ^{2} is shared between direct and indirect evidence to enable estimation even when the direct evidence consists of few trials. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Title: Conflict Diagnostics in Directed Acyclic Graphs, with Applications in Bayesian Evidence Synthesis
Authors: Anne M. Presanis, David Ohlssen, David J. Spiegelhalter, Daniela De Angelis
Date: Wed Oct  2 09:21:28 2013

Complex stochastic models represented by directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) are increasingly employed to synthesise multiple, imperfect and disparate sources of evidence, to estimate quantities that are difficult to measure directly. The various data sources are dependent on shared parameters and hence have the potential to conflict with each other, as well as with the model. In a Bayesian framework, the model consists of three components: the prior distribution, the assumed form of the likelihood and structural assumptions. Any of these components may be incompatible with the observed data. The detection and quantification of such conflict and of data sources that are inconsistent with each other is therefore a crucial component of the model criticism process. We first review Bayesian model criticism, with a focus on conflict detection, before describing a general diagnostic for detecting and quantifying conflict between the evidence in different partitions of a DAG. The diagnostic is a p-value based on splitting the information contributing to inference about a "separator" node or group of nodes into two independent groups and testing whether the two groups result in the same inference about the separator node(s). We illustrate the method with three comprehensive examples: an evidence synthesis to estimate HIV prevalence; an evidence synthesis to estimate influenza case-severity; and a hierarchical growth model for rat weights.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The detection and quantification of such conflict and of data sources that are inconsistent with each other is therefore a crucial component of the model criticism process. We first review Bayesian model criticism, with a focus on conflict detection, before describing a general diagnostic for detecting and quantifying conflict between the evidence in different partitions of a DAG. The diagnostic is a $p$-value based on splitting the information contributing to inference about a “separator” node or group of nodes into two independent groups and testing whether the two groups result in the same inference about the separator node(s). We illustrate the method with three comprehensive examples: an evidence synthesis to estimate HIV prevalence; an evidence synthesis to estimate influenza case-severity; and a hierarchical growth model for rat weights.

The term node‐splitting may be confusing for some, because the treatment network represents a comparison as an edge rather than a node (or vertex). However, in the Bayesian hierarchical model, each parameter is represented by a node in a directed acyclic graph. When one of these parameters is split into two to evaluate conflict, the term node‐splitting is used. A node‐splitting analysis is thus performed separately for each of the comparisons in the treatment network on which both direct and indirect evidence are available, to assess evidence consistency.

Node‐splitting models are very similar to consistency models, except that the direct evidence for d _{x,y} is used alone to estimate {d}_{x,y}^{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{i}\mathrm{r}}, and a network meta‐analysis of the remaining evidence is used to estimate {d}_{x,y}^{\mathrm{i}\mathrm{n}\mathrm{d}}. The heterogeneity parameter σ ^{2} is shared between direct and indirect evidence to enable estimation even when the direct evidence consists of few trials. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

candidate_families.identity: AM changes reversible flow between two disjoint sets. NAM repeatedly applies structured AM steps using a focal value and a nested remaining set. These are construction families; the selection order gives named algorithms.

candidate_families.identity: UNAM uses nondecreasing conditional probabilities and is identified with Frigessi–Hwang–Younes (1992), independently Tjelmeland (2004). DNAM uses nonincreasing order. UDNAM is the equal UNAM/DNAM mixture.
candidate_families.next_work: Read original FHY/Tjelmeland sources for UNAM, full Sections 6–8 for DNAM, and decide whether UDNAM merits a separate identity. Do not attribute all three as original 2024 inventions.
candidate_families.limits: No universal ordering of UNAM and DNAM follows from lower self transitions. Ties and zero-support handling need explicit assessment.

locators: pp.35–36, eigenvalue argument and companion-theorem citation
candidate_families.identity: A named modification of DNAM that detects a step which would cause avoidable self transitions, then jointly handles the next two focal values and remaining tail. Its transition matrix can differ from DNAM; it is not an alias of Liu MHGS.
candidate_families.positive_evidence: The whole defining section and Algorithm 5 were read. Equation 91 presents a concrete distinction: the target (6,5,4,2,1)/18 gives a DNAM self probability 1/28 at the third state, while the ZDNAM example has no diagonal probability. The algorithm includes early handling for mass at least one half.
candidate_families.limits: The name does not promise zero self transitions when a conditional mass exceeds one half. Equation 95 supplies a counterexample to universal ZDNAM-over-DNAM efficiency domination. Source-reported eigenvalues 0.10306, -0.03639 and 0 were not recalculated here. The source efficiency-over-GS statement depends on reversible-kernel spectral theory and random variable selection; it is not a finite-run, systematic-scan or wall-clock guarantee.
next_work: Read full NAM/DNAM antecedents and the exact Neal–Rosenthal theorem version.
Check Algorithm 5 row sums, stationarity, detailed balance, zero tail, ties, point masses and the half-mass boundary with finite arithmetic.
Verify the illustrative transition entries and the counterexample before making calculated claims.
Curate a narrow local identity; assess AIO mapping afresh.

candidate_families.identity: ST shifts cumulative probability towers by the maximum probability and is attributed to Suwa–Todo (2010). HST uses a half-unit shift and is attributed to Suwa (2022). UST/DST choose opposite probability orders; UDST mixes them equally. OHST is an ordered HST variant.
candidate_families.next_work: Retrieve and read original Suwa sources. Distinguish an inherited construction, ordering convention and mixture algorithm before adding records. The report notes an ordering/formula convention issue in Suwa2022 in footnote18 on p.37; compare the original before implementing.
candidate_families.limits: Tower invariance and minimum-self properties do not establish general ergodicity or variance improvement. HST/OHST can be period-two and nonirreducible for uniform distributions with an even number of values (p.49). Implementation/pseudocode was read but not audited by execution.

locators: p.43, ZFSS reordering and boundary discussion
candidate_families.identity: A finite categorical conditional sampler which moves left at an auxiliary height through probability bars, after redistributing excess mass from the highest bar. ZFSS additionally reorders a qualifying blocker beside the highest bar to eliminate avoidable self transitions. The geometric redesign differs from the existing generic slice-sampling record and its interval stepping-out/doubling variants.
candidate_families.positive_evidence: The whole original method section and both algorithms were read. Figure10 was visually inspected: for probabilities (0.1,0.2,0.2,0.05,0.45), the illustrated current-maximum self probabilities are 5/9 for the simple left-slice construction, 1/9 for FSS and 0 for ZFSS. Those are source figures, not independent calculations in this handoff.
candidate_families.limits: FSS need not achieve minimum self probability; ZFSS does according to the section. The generic construction is nonreversible, but the dominant-mass boundary uses a reversible common kernel. Algorithms explicitly handle point masses, small state spaces and zero current mass. No asymptotic-variance or runtime ordering follows solely from self-transition reduction.
next_work: Decide whether to retain FSS and ZFSS separately with an explicit structural distinction or use a family-plus-variant treatment.
Check Algorithms 8–9 agree, including zero-probability current state, ties for maximum, m<=2, dominant mass>=1/2 and no-self regular cases.
Check finite stationarity, nonreversibility and invariant conditional-to-joint composition before curating.
Use the exact 2024 source identity and assess AIO mappings; do not alias generic SliceSampling.

shared_boundaries.assessment: If a conditional state has mass p>1/2, an invariant kernel must retain self probability at least (2p-1)/p there, giving minimum overall self mass 2p-1. At the half-mass boundary the named minimum-self constructions coincide in that special case; this does not make them globally identical.
Removing individual-coordinate self transitions does not ensure ergodicity of a composed sweep. The report gives a three-binary-variable scan example which fails to visit two of eight states.
Minimal self transitions are not a universal variance-optimality certificate. Separate reversibility, irreducibility, scan schedule, asymptotic-estimator and computation-cost assumptions.

shared_boundaries.locator: p.3 random-order discussion versus conclusion p.82
shared_boundaries.assessment: Use the nuanced scan discussion. Do not repeat a broad assertion that only independent random variable selection can yield a reversible overall algorithm; reversal-symmetric scan mixtures require separate treatment.

comparison.reason: Exact Gibbs independently resamples the chosen conditional; NAM changes its finite transition matrix by nested maximal antithetic flow operations, and ZDNAM adds a two-focal completion. These are conditional-invariant transitions, not ordinary exact resampling.

Liu uses one excluded-current proposal and its Metropolis correction. NAM recursively modifies nested remaining sets following a supplied focal permutation; ZDNAM performs a coupled final two-focal/tail replacement. Shared local reversibility and lower self probabilities do not equate kernels.

The generic acceptance or conditional composition framework does not specify the NAM focal/tail recurrences or ZDNAM completion. Representability by a broader invariant-kernel framework is not exact algorithm identity.

That record stores the preceding/current state pair and suppresses return to the preceding value in a conditional update. NAM/ZDNAM are local finite conditional kernels without pair-state memory. They are not the whole pair-state construction.

These retain partition signs, a continuous half-normal proposal direction, or a signed acceptance-uniform variable. NAM/ZDNAM operate on the current finite category using an explicit local reversible transition matrix, without these persistent auxiliary memories.

A slice height and slice-preserving move, continuous interval expansion/shrinkage, or angular Gaussian-prior ellipse is not the nested finite flow modification. NAM/ZDNAM are not claimed as aliases of generic or overrelaxed slice methods.

These use weighted forward candidates, backward-reference correction, or population optimization anchors. Tjelmeland transition alternative 2 is a discrete selection kernel within a different multiple-proposal framework; its equality to UNAM does not identify NAM with every multiple-try or population algorithm.

Planned FSS/ZFSS use ordered finite probability bars, directed predecessor slice movement, maximum-bar mass redistribution and, for ZFSS, blocker relocation. NAM/ZDNAM use reversible nested antithetic flow modification. Generic kernels differ; shared dominant-mass boundary behavior is not global identity. FSS/ZFSS modules were read as source text, not invoked.

methods.label: Antithetic modification (AM)
methods.definition: Modify a finite reversible kernel using two disjoint sets A, B of positive target mass and a positive admissible magnitude δ. Decrease within-A and within-B flows and increase between-set flows according to Eq 19, leaving transitions involving outside states unchanged.
methods.parameters: P,π, A, B,δ; δ bounded by existing within-set transition probabilities.
methods.identity: Broad kernel transformation. It includes singleton-pair Peskun increases, but permits off-diagonal decreases within larger sets; not an exact alias of generic antithetic variates or a single finite Gibbs algorithm.
methods.curation_recommendation: Keep as explanatory framework in the next narrow record(s), rather than automatically create an extra AM umbrella record in this batch.

methods.label: Nested antithetic modification (NAM)
methods.definition: Starting from a finite independent-sampling matrix whose rows equal π, use a supplied focal permutation σ. At each step split the remaining states into singleton{σ(i)} and its remaining tail, apply the largest admissible antithetic modification, and stop once the tail block is zero.
methods.equations: With q=π(σ(i)), tail mass s_i, current block factor r_(i-1): if q<s_i use δ=r*q/s_i and zero the focal diagonal; if q>=s_i use δ=r*s_i/q, zero the tail block and terminate. Algorithm 2 computes just one row via cumulative residual f and tail sum s.
methods.scope: One supplied ordering defines one kernel. Later focal ordering cannot depend on the current label in a way that changes the kernel per row; a conditional-target-dependent ordering can be selected consistently for that update.
limits: Finite normalized positive-support formulation is safest initial scope for theorem-linked curation. Source permits zero probabilities in general; no complete zero-current/floating guard audit was done here.
Any NAM kernel has at most one nonzero diagonal after maximal completion.
Periodicity is possible; a systematic sweep can be reducible.
Bare NAM onp21 denotes fixed focal order; family usage covers other ordering policies.
methods.curation_recommendation: One parameterized construction record may cover fixed-order NAM and the upward/downward ordering specializations. Do not add upward/downward labels as exact aliases of the entire family.

methods.label: Upward / Upwards Nested Antithetic Modification (UNAM)
methods.definition: NAM with focal values in nondecreasing target-probability order. Tied probabilities produce the same final kernel regardless of their order.
methods.historical_identity: Neal attributes the full final kernel to the complete construction implicit in Frigessi–Hwang–Younes1992 Theorem 1 and independently to Tjelmeland2004 Transition alternative2. Original Tjelmeland T2 personally inspected. Original FHY unavailable; its attribution/full-versus-truncated distinction is reported through Neal2024, not invented original reading.
not_equivalent_to: Liu modified Gibbs/MHGS single MH correction. Repeating suitably restricted MH modifications to completion can produce UNAM, but one Liu update generally does not.
Entire Tjelmeland multiple-proposal chain or weighted-estimator framework.
FHY1992 one-stage practical sampler discussed onpp624,626–627 as described by Neal; full construction and truncated version differ.
limits: Only largest-probability label may retain self probability, which can be positive below1/2.
Finite support assumed for Algorithm 3; infinite upward ordering is not generally available.
methods.curation_recommendation: Supported named specialization covered by a family record if using conservative construction-level granularity. A separate UNAM record is defensible at named-kernel granularity, but requires explicit containment and fresh corpus dedup; historical authors do not create additional same-kernel records.

methods.label: Downward Nested Antithetic Modification (DNAM)
methods.definition: NAM with focal values in nonincreasing target-probability order, including a direct branch for a current mass≥1/2.
methods.difference: Can zero entire tail submatrices, retain self mass away from maximum, and distinguish equal-probability labels depending on tie ordering. It is not exactly equivalent to UNAM, despite sharing construction.
limits: Tie policy is part of the specific kernel.
Not guaranteed to increase every off-diagonal transition, nor minimize self transitions.
Special countably infinite geometric construction Eq 81–89 is outside the recommended finite identity scope.
methods.curation_recommendation: Cover as named ordering specialization under a parameterized NAM record; do not collapse into UNAM as exact alias.

methods.label: Upward/downward NAM mixture (UDNAM)
methods.definition: Choose the UNAM or DNAM update with equal probability; the resulting kernel is (P_UNAM+P_DNAM)/2.
methods.boundary: Generally not itself a single-permutation NAM kernel: for π=(4,3,2)/9, the mixture has two positive diagonal entries, while all 6 NAM focal orders have exactly1 in the original bounded check. Its named combination is explicit source evidence, not a label mechanically inferred from inventory.
methods.curation_recommendation: Keep as a distinct composition lead if not curated now. It may support a third record beside NAM-family and ZDNAM; do not mark it covered by exact identity with NAM, UNAM or DNAM.

methods.label: Zero-self DNAM (ZDNAM)
methods.definition: Follow DNAM until just before its next step would create avoidable self probability. Jointly complete transitions for two consecutive focal states and the remaining tail, retaining earlier transitions, zeroing the two diagonals and tail-to-tail transitions, and distributing transitions into the tail proportionally to target mass.
methods.equations: For focal masses q, q2 and remaining tail sum s2>0, A=(q+q2-s2)/2, B=(q-q2+s2)/(2s2), C=(s2+q2-q)/(2s2). Residual factor f scales pair transitions fA/q and fA/q2; tail-to-focal transitions fB, fC; focal-to-tail transitions fBπ(j)/q and fCπ(j)/q2.
methods.trigger: Algorithm 5 looks ahead for q2>=s2, including equality; introductory prose emphasizes strict inequality. Use actual algorithm condition.
methods.guards: Handle maximum mass≥1/2 first; from nonmaximum move to maximum, from maximum use off-diagonalπ(j)/p and self(2p-1)/p. For zero tail, avoid division bys2 using explicit Algorithm 5branch. Do not apply Eq 96eigenformula with denominator zero.
methods.distinctness: For π=(4,3,2)/9, Eq 95ZDNAM has all-zero diagonal; all 6single-permutation NAM kernels retain a positive diagonal. It is a genuine modification of NAM construction, not merely another focal order.
limits: Zero-self name allows unavoidable positive self mass at maximum>1/2.

No universal efficiency dominance over DNAM: sourceEq95 difference has eigenvalues of mixed signs; original bounded illustration checks matrices/invariance only, not numerical eigenvalue recalculation.
Countably infinite extension is suggested by analogy, not included in initial finite record.
No independent exhaustive floating-point, zero-current or tie-invariance audit here.

mathematical_assessments.source: Section 5 p. 10 Eq19; Section 6 pp. 14–20 Eq28–63 and Algorithm2
mathematical_assessments.assessment: The full-matrix implementation determines maximal delta from every affected nonnegativity constraint and applies Eq19 directly. The separately written row procedure uses Algorithm2 residual sums. They agree in 2,607 strictly positive target/order cases. Rows are stochastic and reversible. Zero-label extensions agree on supported submatrices with explicit positive-support construction in 716 cases. The initial record may conservatively retain positive support.

One implementation directly interprets row pseudocode, including equality and dominant-mass branches. The other constructs the AM prefix and solves the independent three-equation system A+B*s2=q, A+C*s2=q2, B+C=1 for the final block. Both agree on positive-support rows for 358 nonnegative target vectors under 2,802 compatible descending orders. All assembled full rows, including 4,030 zero-current rows, are stochastic/reversible for their targets; minimum stationary self mass equals max(0,2*max(pi)-1). These finite cases supplement the source construction and do not prove floating-point robustness.

The literal zero-tail guard is retained but was never executed by the exact normalized test cases. In the regular branch, entering a focal step implies q<q2+s2: initially max(pi)<1/2, and thereafter this is the previous look-ahead continuation condition. Descending order gives q>=q2. Therefore s2>0 whenever the regular special completion is reached. The zero-tail guard still matters for the broader numerical pseudocode; its floating behavior was not audited. No artificial guard test is described as an actually reachable exact case.

mathematical_assessments.source: Section 6 p. 21; Section 7 p. 24 Eq75; Section 8 p. 28; Algorithm5 pp. 33–34
mathematical_assessments.assessment: UNAM tie invariance is supported by the inspected Eq75 derivation and checked examples. DNAM and ZDNAM can distinguish equal-mass labels; exact supported counterexamples are retained. An ordering that places each current label first changes rows inconsistently and fails stationarity at target (4,3,2)/9. A target/conditioning-dependent policy must be consistent across rows for the same conditional. Any extra random policy mixture needs state-independent mixing weights.

mathematical_assessments.source: Section 8 p. 28 UDNAM; Section 9 p. 35 Eq95
mathematical_assessments.assessment: For target (4,3,2)/9 all six NAM focal orders have exactly one positive diagonal. The 50:50 UNAM/DNAM mixture has two; ZDNAM has none. Neither is any single-order NAM kernel. The source-defined UDNAM composition remains a distinct uncurated lead under the preferred two-record scope, not an exact alias or an automatically covered third record.

The printed DNAM and ZDNAM matrices are reproduced exactly. Their difference has one zero eigenvalue, sum of other eigenvalues 1/15, and product −3/800, so the other two have opposite signs. Separately labeled floating values 0.10305500221117297 and −0.0363883355445063 agree with the source rounding. No companion dominance theorem or universal variance result is adopted in drafts.

mathematical_assessments.source: Section 2 p. 3 footnote1; Section 9 pp. 31–34; Section 13 p. 51 Eq112–114
mathematical_assessments.assessment: At a dominant mass h, stationarity bounds P(a,a)>=(2h−1)/h. Algorithm5 reaches it and has no other positive diagonal; with max(pi)<1/2 the completed block and prefix have zero diagonals. At h=1/2 the dominant state has zero self probability; a one-point support is absorbing. Conditional invariance transfers to joint invariance, but does not establish every schedule’s ergodicity. Drafts exclude general variance, burn-in and wall-clock claims.

historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model that only attends to previous tokens in the sequence when generating text modeling the probability distribution autoregressively from left-to-right or causally.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Contrastive Learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A deep neural network self-supervised learning approach that learns to distinguish between similar and dissimilar data samples.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Contrastive Learning LLM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model that is trained to pull semantically similar samples closer together and push dissimilar samples apart in the representation space learning high-quality features useful for downstream tasks.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Data Augmentation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A data enhancement used to increase the diversity and quantity of training data by applying various transformations such as rotation scaling flipping and cropping to existing data samples enhancing the robustness and performance of machine learning models.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Data Generation Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising from adding synthetic or redundant data samples to a dataset.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Deep Active Learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A deep neural network that combines deep learning and active learning to maximize model performance while annotating the fewest samples possible.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Deep Belief Network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An unsupervised pretrained network composed of multiple layers of latent variables that learns to probabilistically reconstruct inputs and perform classification.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Deep Convolutional Inverse Graphics Network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An autoencoder network that learns interpretable disentangled image representations through convolution and de-convolution layers trained with the stochastic gradient variational Bayes algorithm.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Detection Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias characterized by systematic differences between groups in how outcomes are determined potentially over- or underestimating effect size.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Dot Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A layer that computes a dot product between samples in two tensors.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Dynamic Conditional Correlation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A model that allows for time-varying correlations between different time series, used in financial econometrics to model and forecast covariances.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Ecological Fallacy Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias occurring when an inference about an individual is made based on their group membership.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Energy-Based LLM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model which models the explicit probability density over token sequences using an energy function, rather than an autoregressive factorization. This can improve modeling of long-range dependencies and global coherence.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Evaluation Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising when testing populations do not equally represent user populations or when inappropriate performance metrics are used.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Exclusion Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias occurring when specific groups of user populations are excluded from testing and analysis.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Federated Learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A deep neural network trained across decentralized edge devices or servers holding local data samples without exchanging them.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A model that incorporates lagged conditional variances, allowing for more flexibility in modeling time-varying volatility.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Generalized Few-shot Learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A deep neural network that learns novel classes from few samples per class, preventing catastrophic forgetting of base classes and ensuring classifier calibration.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Implicit Language Model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A language model that uses an energy function to score entire sequences instead of factorizing probabilities autoregressively better capturing global properties and long-range dependencies.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Language Model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A model designed to predict the next word in a sequence or assign probabilities to sequences of words in natural language.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Logistic Regression
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A regression analysis that estimates the probability of an event occurring by modeling the log-odds of the event as a linear combination of one or more independent variables.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Markov Chain
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A network that is a stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events where the probability of each event depends only on the previous event's state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Measurement Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising when features and labels are proxies for desired quantities potentially leading to differential performance.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Mixture-of-Experts LLM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model which dynamically selects and combines outputs from multiple expert submodels, allowing for efficient scaling by conditionally activating only a subset of model components for each input.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Neuro-Symbolic LLM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model which combines neural language modeling with symbolic reasoning components, leveraging structured knowledge representations and logical inferences to improve reasoning capabilities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Ordinal LLM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model that is trained to model ordinal relationships and rank outputs rather than model probability distributions over text sequences directly.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Policy Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A layer that, after taking a set of states or values as input, predicts a probability distribution of actions to take.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Pooling Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A layer that serves to mitigate the sensitivity of convolutional layers to location and spatially downsample representations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Popularity Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias where more popular items are more exposed under-representing less popular items.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Population Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias characterized by systematic distortions in demographics or other user characteristics between represented users and the target population.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Probabilistic Graphical Model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A machine learning task in which a graph expresses the conditional dependence structure between random variables.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Probabilistic Hidden Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hidden layer that estimates the probability of a sample being within a certain category.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Probabilistic Topic Model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probabilistic graphical model that uses statistical techniques to analyze the words in each text to discover common themes their connections and their changes over time.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Reasoning LLM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A large language model that incorporates explicit reasoning capabilities leveraging logical rules axioms or external knowledge to make deductive inferences during language tasks.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Representation Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias due to non-random sampling of subgroups making trends non-generalizable to new populations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Boltzmann machine network that learns the probability distribution of its input data.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Selection And Sampling Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A computational bias introduced by non-random selection of individuals groups or data failing to ensure representativeness.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Simpson's Paradox Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias where the association between two variables changes when controlling for another variable.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Temporal Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias arising from differences in populations and behaviors over time.

historical_semantic_rows.name: TimeDistributed Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A recurrent layer that applies a layer to every temporal slice of an input.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Uncertainty Bias
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A selection and sampling bias favoring groups better represented in training data due to less prediction uncertainty.

historical_semantic_rows.name: UpSampling1D Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A reshaping layer that upsamples the input by repeating each temporal step size times along the time axis.

historical_semantic_rows.name: UpSampling2D Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A layer that upsamples the input by repeating each row and column size times.

historical_semantic_rows.name: UpSampling3D Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A layer that upsamples the input by repeating each depth, height and width size times.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Variational Auto Encoder
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An autoencoder network that imposes a probabilistic structure on the latent space for unsupervised learning.

historical_semantic_rows.name: t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor embedding
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A dimensionality reduction for visualizing high-dimensional data by giving each datapoint a location in a two or three-dimensional map.

historical_semantic_rows.name: ABRA-s-fix fixed-sample betweenness approximation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fixed-sample static-graph betweenness algorithm that averages shortest-path fractions over a user-specified number of uniform endpoint pairs and returns both the estimates and a simultaneous Rademacher-based additive error bound, regardless of the size of that bound.

historical_semantic_rows.name: ABRA-s progressive betweenness approximation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A progressive sampling algorithm for static-graph betweenness that averages fractions of shortest paths through each node over uniformly sampled endpoint pairs and checks a predetermined sequence of sample sizes and stops when a Rademacher-based simultaneous error bound meets the requested additive tolerance.

historical_semantic_rows.name: AND/OR abstraction sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An importance-sampling algorithm for partition functions of discrete graphical models that samples representatives in a pseudo-tree-guided AND/OR search space, allowing abstractions across branching-ancestor contexts through interleaved ancestor pruning and relative-weight value backup.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Adam
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Stochastic gradient optimization using bias-corrected exponential estimates of first and second gradient moments to scale parameter updates.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Adaptive Metropolis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A history-adaptive random-walk Metropolis sampler whose Gaussian proposal covariance is estimated from the accumulated retained states, including repetitions after rejected proposals.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Adaptive parallel tempering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A parallel-tempering algorithm that adapts temperature gaps and within-replica random-walk proposal parameters through projected stochastic approximation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Adaptive rejection sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The Gilks–Wild univariate rejection sampler that uses tangents to a concave log density as a piecewise-linear upper hull and chords as a lower hull, updating these bounds from evaluated proposals.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Adaptive scaling Metropolis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A random-walk Metropolis algorithm that adapts its proposal scale through stochastic approximation driven by the proposal acceptance probability relative to a chosen target rate.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Adaptive scaling within adaptive Metropolis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An adaptive Metropolis algorithm that combines acceptance-rate-driven scalar proposal scaling with recursive mean and covariance-shape adaptation from retained samples.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family that draws each document from a proper Poisson-MRF base distribution whose canonical unary and interaction parameters are convex combinations of topic parameters under document-specific simplex weights.

identities.value: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields

historical_semantic_rows.name: Alternating Expectation Conditional Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A likelihood-optimization framework that alternates cycles of expectation and constrained maximization, permitting the admissible data augmentation and constraint functions to change between cycles while collectively covering the parameter directions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Alternating Kullback-Leibler Minimization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A paired-distribution optimization procedure that alternately minimizes Kullback-Leibler divergence in its first and second arguments over specified convex probability families.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Ancestral Gumbel-Top-k sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An exact without-replacement sampler for finite discrete Bayesian-network configurations that propagates conditional Gumbel subtree maxima through a bounded priority frontier, with a configurable number of parallel expansions and parent-respecting variable selection.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Annealed importance sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Monte Carlo estimation algorithm that draws from a tractable base distribution, applies Markov transitions invariant for a prescribed sequence of intermediate distributions, and weights each resulting path by successive unnormalized-density ratios to estimate target expectations and normalizing-constant ratios.

historical_semantic_rows.name: AntNet
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A distributed adaptive routing algorithm in which forward agents sample network paths and backward agents use the measured trip times to update local traffic models and probabilistic routing tables.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Ant System
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A constructive combinatorial optimization method in which artificial ants sample solution components using shared pheromone trails and problem-specific heuristic information, then modify those trails through reinforcement and evaporation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Attention-based Dropout Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A training-time convolutional feature-map layer that stochastically applies either a thresholded spatial drop mask or sigmoid importance weights derived from channel-averaged activations, developed for weakly supervised object localization.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Author-persona-topic model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family in which each author has a mixture of personas, each persona has a topic distribution, and one persona shared across a document generates its token topics.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Auto-binomial Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for bounded site counts whose full conditionals are binomial with fixed trial counts and log odds linear in neighboring counts, using symmetric interaction coefficients.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Auto-exponential Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for nonnegative continuous site values with exponential full conditionals whose rates are positive baseline terms plus nonnegative symmetric linear neighbor interactions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Auto-normal Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A proper finite Gaussian Markov-field model specified by linear full-conditional means and positive, value-independent site conditional variances, with compatibility enforced by a symmetric positive-definite joint precision matrix.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Auto-Poisson Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for unbounded nonnegative integer counts whose full conditionals are Poisson with log means linear in neighboring counts and whose symmetric interaction coefficients are nonpositive.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Autoregressive conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture that models each current vector with a conditional RBM whose visible and hidden biases are affine functions of a fixed window of preceding observed vectors, without hidden-to-hidden temporal links.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Averaged stochastic gradient descent
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic gradient optimization method that maintains an average of parameter iterates in addition to the current iterate.

historical_semantic_rows.name: BOHB
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hyperparameter optimization algorithm combining Hyperband resource brackets with model-guided configuration proposals from performance-split multivariate kernel density estimates and a continuing random-sampling component.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Beam search using limited discrepancy backtracking
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A memory-bounded beam search that explores heuristic-ranked slices using increasing limited-discrepancy budgets and removes backtracked slices so that alternative beams can be examined.

identities.value: Beam search using limited discrepancy backtracking

historical_semantic_rows.name: Bagging
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Ensemble learning that aggregates predictors trained on bootstrap samples.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Barber–Agakov mutual information bound
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational lower bound on mutual information formed by adding input entropy to the expected log probability assigned by a normalized conditional decoder to the input given the output.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Barker acceptance rule
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An acceptance-probability rule for reversible Monte Carlo proposals that uses R/(1+R), where R is the target-density ratio times the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Bayesian Data Augmentation for Deep Models
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Tran et al.’s supervised deep-learning procedure that treats synthetic labeled examples as latent data, repeatedly samples them from an evolving learned model and updates model parameters through a generalized Monte Carlo expectation-maximization formulation.

identities.value: Bayesian Data Augmentation for Deep Models

historical_semantic_rows.name: Black box variational inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational-inference procedure that estimates evidence-lower-bound gradients from samples of a tractable variational distribution using its score function and model log joint, with mean-field local signals and score control variates to manage estimator variance.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Boltzmann chain
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of tied-weight undirected Boltzmann sequence models with hidden temporal variables, observed variables and chain-derived connectivity chosen to permit exact elimination.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Bootstrap classifier-instability novelty detection
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A novelty-detection procedure that trains classifiers on bootstrap resamples of reference data, estimates the variance of their outputs at a query, and rejects queries with unusually high variability relative to a chosen reference-score threshold.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Bottleneck Attention Module
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A convolutional feature refinement component that combines parallel channel and spatial attention branches and adds the resulting gated features back to its input, originally proposed for network downsampling bottlenecks.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Bounded adaptive reward for sequence scoring
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A beam-dependent sequence rescoring rule that adds per-step rewards derived from the beam’s mean negative log token probability, accumulating them only up to a predicted output-length cap.

identities.value: Bounded adaptive reward for sequence scoring

historical_semantic_rows.name: Brandes–Fleischer sampled-pair current-flow betweenness
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A randomized network-analysis algorithm that estimates normalized, endpoint-excluded current-flow betweenness by independently sampling uniform source–sink pairs, solving their grounded electrical-network systems, and averaging scaled vertex throughputs.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Brevity-penalty normalization for sequence scoring
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A sequence rescoring rule that adds a predicted-length brevity penalty in log space to average token log probability: S(x,y)/|y| + min(1−Lpred(x)/|y|,0).

historical_semantic_rows.name: CD-PercLoss
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional RBM training algorithm that contrasts the observed output free energy with that of a prediction selected by input-initialized stochastic search, treating the selected prediction as fixed during differentiation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: CTAugment
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An online augmentation-policy adaptation procedure that samples image operations and adjusts their parameter-selection weights using classifier feedback on labeled probe images during training.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Classification Annealing Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic hard-clustering algorithm that samples component assignments from current mixture posterior probabilities raised to an inverse positive temperature, maximizes the completed-data classification likelihood, and lowers the temperature according to a chosen schedule.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Conditional Distribution Prediction for IDA*
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A search-effort estimation procedure that predicts the number of expanded nodes in a complete IDA* threshold iteration by recursively propagating conditional heuristic-value frequencies and branching counts while excluding pruned ancestor paths.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional neural probability model that represents an output vector with an RBM whose biases or interactions are determined by a supplied conditioning vector.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Conjugate-gradient Monte Carlo
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A population Markov sampler that obtains a local-optimization anchor from one population member and updates another member along the anchor line with a multiple-try transition targeting a radial-Jacobian-adjusted density.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Consistency model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generative model family that learns a noise- or time-conditioned function mapping points on a probability-flow ODE trajectory to its common low-noise endpoint, enabling a sample to be obtained with one model evaluation and allowing optional multistep refinement.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Context-sensitive emission hidden Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hidden-state sequence-model family with a first-order Markov prior whose observation distributions depend jointly on hidden states at multiple temporal positions, introducing context beyond the contemporaneous hidden state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Contrastive divergence
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A parameter-learning algorithm for energy-based or product-of-experts models that replaces the equilibrium negative-phase expectation by configurations obtained from a short model-invariant Markov chain restarted at observed data, without differentiating through the chain distribution.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Contrastive predictive coding
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A representation-learning procedure that encodes observations, summarizes preceding representations as context, and jointly trains these components to distinguish future representations from sampled alternatives using InfoNCE.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Counterfactual fairness
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fairness criterion in a specified causal model requiring a predictor's conditional output distribution, given an individual's observed attributes and protected-attribute value, to remain unchanged under counterfactual interventions that assign other attainable protected-attribute values.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An evolution strategy for continuous optimization that samples a multivariate normal search distribution and adapts its mean, covariance and global step size from ranked offspring and accumulated selected-step paths.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that combines a Crank–Nicolson treatment of the reference precision with an explicit gradient drift of the remaining target potential.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Crank–Nicolson Metropolis sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target using a Crank–Nicolson discretization of the unpreconditioned reference Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics as its proposal.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Cross-entropy optimization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic optimization method that iteratively samples a parameterized search distribution, selects high-performing samples using an adaptive threshold, and refits the distribution by maximum likelihood on those selected samples.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Cross-validated prior-likelihood conflict diagnostic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian hierarchical-model diagnostic that leaves an assessed unit out of population-parameter fitting, generates predictive-prior and reference-prior likelihood replicates of its unit effect, and measures their signed conflict under an explicitly specified replication law. Shared nuisance parameters require controlled feedback and dependence handling.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Curriculum Dropout
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural-network training procedure that starts without unit suppression and gradually increases Bernoulli dropout by decreasing the probability of retaining each unit toward a specified layer-dependent limit.

historical_semantic_rows.name: DINO self-distillation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that matches cross-view student probabilities to centered and sharpened probabilities from a momentum teacher, without a separate prediction head or explicit negative-pair objective.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Deep autoregressive network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generative neural architecture that combines directed stochastic hidden layers with autoregressive within-layer conditional dependencies and a separately parameterized recognition network for approximate latent inference.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Delayed-rejection Metropolis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis-Hastings sampling procedure that can propose another candidate after rejection within the same transition, correcting acceptance for the probabilities of the forward and reversed rejected paths.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Diaconis–Holmes–Neal fiber sampler
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite-state Metropolis sampler that uses partitions into ordered lines, retains a binary direction for each partition, and combines a neighbor proposal with a separate probabilistic sign update to preserve a target distribution on the augmented state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Differentiable scheduled sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A scheduled-sampling training procedure that replaces discrete model-feedback embeddings with differentiable soft mixtures, allowing later sequence losses to propagate credit through earlier relaxed decoding choices.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Diffusion Maps
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of spectral embedding algorithms that normalizes a nonnegative symmetric affinity kernel into a reversible Markov operator and represents points by its nontrivial eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Direct preference optimization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Preference-based policy fitting using a classification objective on policy-to-reference probability ratios for preferred and dispreferred responses.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Diverse beam search
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The inference procedure of Vijayakumar and colleagues that partitions a sequence beam budget into groups and updates each group using model log-probability scores augmented by a weighted dissimilarity to the already-updated earlier groups at the same decoding step.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Document NADE
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural autoregressive document model that predicts successive words from shared additive embeddings of the preceding words, using normalized word conditionals and a deterministic document representation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Doubling slice sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A univariate slice-sampling algorithm that expands a randomly placed initial interval by randomly directed doublings and uses shrinkage with a retrospective acceptability test to preserve the target.

historical_semantic_rows.name: DropConnect
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic neural-network layer that masks individual weights and biases during training, so each example is processed through a randomly selected subset of the layer’s connections.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Dual-averaging step-size adaptation for Hamiltonian samplers
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A warmup procedure that tunes the logarithm of a Hamiltonian sampler’s integration step size using cumulative discrepancy from a target acceptance statistic, a shrinkage point and a smoothed sequence of iterates.

identities.value: Dual-averaging step-size adaptation for Hamiltonian samplers

historical_semantic_rows.name: Dynamic Convolutional Layer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural layer that convolves feature maps with filters generated from the current input by a learned subnetwork, allowing the applied kernels to vary between examples during inference.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Dynamic topic model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A time-sliced topic-model family that links the softmax natural parameters of corresponding topic-word distributions across slices through Gaussian state transitions, allowing a fixed set of topics to change over time.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Elliptical slice sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Markov-chain update for a target factored into a Gaussian prior and a likelihood, which performs an angular slice search along the ellipse defined by the current state and an independent prior draw.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Eppstein–Wang RAND closeness approximation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A randomized graph-analysis algorithm that estimates closeness centrality from independent uniformly sampled source vertices, averaging scaled shortest-path distances to estimate mean distance and taking its reciprocal where defined.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Epsilon-truncation for Conditional Distribution Prediction
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A modification of conditional distribution prediction for IDA* tree size that removes conditional child-type probabilities below a calibrated level-specific cutoff, renormalizes the surviving probabilities and uses the modified tables in node-count propagation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Equal opportunity in binary classification
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A binary-classification fairness criterion requiring equal probabilities of a positive prediction across specified protected groups among individuals whose target outcome is the designated positive outcome.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Equalized odds
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fairness criterion requiring a predictor's output to be conditionally independent of a specified protected attribute given the target outcome; for binary predictions and outcomes, it requires equal true-positive and false-positive rates across the compared groups.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Expectation Conditional Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An extension of expectation maximization that replaces a joint maximization of the expected complete-data log likelihood with a sequence of constrained maximizations, holding the E-step expectation fixed throughout that sequence.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Expectation Conditional Maximization Either
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An extension of expectation conditional maximization that replaces selected final conditional maximizations of expected complete-data log likelihood with conditional maximizations of actual observed-data likelihood.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Exponential-family harmonium
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A bipartite undirected model family coupling visible and hidden exponential-family sufficient statistics through bilinear interactions, with variables conditionally independent within either layer given the other and a finite global joint normalizer.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Exponential generalized root model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generalized root probability model on nonnegative continuous variables with exponential base measure and symmetric root-product interactions, restricted to parameters with a finite joint integral; uniform negative degree-one terms provide a sufficient normalizable regime.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Exponential square root graphical model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A graphical probability model on nonnegative continuous variables with unary square-root terms and symmetric products of square roots, derived from an exponential base measure and restricted to parameters giving a finite joint integral.

identities.value: Exponential square root Markov random field

historical_semantic_rows.name: Extended Guided Local Search
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The Tsang–Mills–Ford extension of Guided Local Search that combines cost-scaled penalty weighting, aspiration for a new best original-objective solution despite an augmented-objective penalty, and probabilistic random neighborhood moves.

historical_semantic_rows.name: FABOLAS
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian hyperparameter optimization algorithm that jointly chooses a model configuration and training-data subset size using surrogate models of loss and evaluation cost, directing evaluations toward information about the best configuration on the full dataset.

identities.value: Fast Bayesian Optimization on Large Data Sets

historical_semantic_rows.name: Factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional neural word model that factorizes position-specific word-to-hidden weights through a shared word-embedding matrix and couples the next categorical word to binary hidden units in a context-conditioned restricted Boltzmann machine.

identities.value: Factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model

historical_semantic_rows.name: Factorial hidden Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A directed latent sequence-model family in which several independently evolving hidden Markov chains jointly determine the observation distribution at each time.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Factorized variational sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The Gal–Turner finite spectral regression inference procedure that explicitly optimizes diagonal Gaussian output-coefficient factors and independent spectral variational factors using an evidence lower bound written as a sum of per-observation expected log likelihoods and global KL penalties.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Family-of-harmonium
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A classification model family comprising separately parameterized harmoniums for each class, with binary text features and Gaussian image features coupled to Gaussian latent variables and compared through normalized class-conditional likelihoods.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fast condensed prototype-based domain description
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A heuristic for selecting PDD prototypes that samples remaining reference observations, computes their radius offsets against the full dataset, accumulates eligible candidates, and greedily selects them by uncovered-reference gain with an adaptive sampling schedule.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fast Dropout Training
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A dropout approximation procedure that replaces masked weighted sums by Gaussian distributions with matched means and variances, using Gaussian sampling or moment integration to approximate training and prediction computations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fast persistent contrastive divergence
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A persistent-chain RBM learning algorithm that adds rapidly updated, rapidly decaying auxiliary parameters to the sampling energy while retaining separate regular parameters for the model distribution.

historical_semantic_rows.name: FiLM Parameter-Arithmetic Inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A post-training visual-question-answering procedure that uses a parser to construct related questions and combines their generated FiLM scale/shift vectors by addition and subtraction before running the conditioned visual network.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fixed-length Poisson MRF topic model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probabilistic topic model that allocates a document total among topics, draws an independent fixed-length Poisson-MRF count vector for each allocated topic total, and sums those latent vectors to produce the observed document counts.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fixed-length Poisson Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite-total count distribution whose probability on nonnegative integer vectors summing to a specified total is proportional to a Poisson factorial base measure times exponentiated linear and symmetric quadratic count potentials.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Flow matching
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generative-model training method that fits a time-dependent vector field by regression to velocities associated with a chosen probability path between a base distribution and a data distribution, with conditional flow matching providing a tractable training objective.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fully factorized mean-field inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational inference method that restricts its approximating distribution to a product of single-variable factors and adjusts those factors to reduce the approximation-to-target Kullback–Leibler divergence.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Fully visible sigmoid belief network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fully observed binary autoregressive probabilistic model whose conditional probability at each position is a logistic function of a bias and a weighted sum of preceding visible variables.

historical_semantic_rows.name: GSAT with random walk
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A GSAT variant that mixes a uniformly chosen flip from the distinct variables currently occurring in unsatisfied clauses with a globally best GSAT flip, using a fixed probability to choose the focused random move.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gaussian Differentiable Pooling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A spatial pooling and unpooling component whose nonnegative, unit-L2 weights are square-root normalized axis-aligned Gaussian samples, with each region’s location and precision inferred jointly with image-specific features under a reconstruction objective.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gaussian Factor Analysis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A linear Gaussian latent-variable model in which observed variables share a lower-dimensional Gaussian factor and have conditionally independent residuals with variable-specific nonnegative variances.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gaussian loss-smoothed mixed-model variational inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A nonconjugate variational inference procedure for a loss-defined mixed-effects generalized posterior that retains a joint Gaussian over fixed and random coefficients, factors inverse-gamma random-effect variances, and uses one-dimensional Gaussian expected-loss derivatives to alternate exact variance coordinates with a full-Gaussian natural proposal.
