This record denotes the base NCVB-UF procedure with the precision sign reconciled against its gradient/Hessian derivation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gaussian message conflict diagnostic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian GLMM screening procedure that separates Gaussian prior and likelihood natural-parameter messages at local variational fixed points and computes conflict scores from an approximately independent Gaussian difference. It approximates predictive-prior versus unit-likelihood disagreement using full-data fitted factors.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gaussian process regression
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Probabilistic regression conditioning a Gaussian-process prior on observed training data.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Generalized component analysis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An undirected latent-component model family coupling categorical text and heterogeneous document attributes to positive lognormal hidden variables, with variables conditionally independent within either layer given the other and shared attribute-specific interaction weights.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Generalized root model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of finite undirected probability models that retains univariate exponential-family base measures and couples coordinatewise roots of sufficient statistics in symmetric interactions of configurable order, restricted to parameters with a finite joint partition function.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Generic tree sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An importance-sampling generalization of Chen heuristic tree sampling that merges representatives of ordered tree strata using specified positive selection probabilities and inverse-probability survivor weights to estimate an additive tree functional.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gibbs sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that repeatedly draws a coordinate or block from its full conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining coordinates.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Group-topic model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probabilistic model family jointly assigning topics to relation-bearing events and topic-specific latent groups to entities, using event text and event-specific group-pair agreement probabilities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Guided Grad-CAM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A visualization method combining an upsampled Grad-CAM localization map with guided-backpropagation input-space scores.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gumbel-Top-k trick
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A categorical sampling construction that adds independent standard Gumbel noise to each category’s log weight and returns the indices of the k largest perturbed values in descending order, producing an ordered sample without replacement under successive renormalization of the remaining weights.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Gustafson guided-walk Metropolis sampler
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A continuous-state Metropolis sampler that augments a univariate state with a binary direction, proposes a half-normal displacement along that direction, retains direction after acceptance and reverses it after rejection.

historical_semantic_rows.name: HAC-E network clustering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hierarchical network-clustering variant that greedily guides agglomeration by the observed edge density between two vertex groups and uses the resulting group hierarchy for link-probability estimation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: HAC-ML network clustering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A greedy network-clustering algorithm that builds a hierarchical stochastic block structure by merging groups with the least loss of profiled network likelihood, using separate Bayesian criteria to collapse terminal groups and stop top-level merging.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for differentiable continuous targets that augments positions with momenta, proposes a state through reversible volume-preserving numerical Hamiltonian dynamics, and applies a Metropolis correction for the Hamiltonian change.

historical_semantic_rows.name: HashCRBM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional RBM training and prediction method that uses spectral hashing of inputs to retrieve distinct training-output configurations and normalizes the conditional model only over that input-dependent support.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Helmholtz machine
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hierarchical probabilistic neural model that pairs a top-down generative model with a separately parameterized bottom-up recognition model approximating the distribution of hidden causes given observed input.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Heuristic tree sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A randomized estimator of additive properties of an implicit rooted tree that processes ordered strata using one sampled representative and an accumulated weight per stratum.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden Markov decision tree
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family that extends a probabilistic hierarchical decision tree by coupling each decision level to the same level at the previous time.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A sequence model whose hidden Markov states generate observations through state-dependent emission distributions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden Markov model with auxiliary memory
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hidden-state symbol-sequence model family in which paired states write emitted symbols to auxiliary memory and later read them to condition emissions and memory-dependent state transitions.

identities.value: Hidden Markov model with auxiliary memory

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-variable graphical-model family whose unobserved label field has the Markov property on a specified neighborhood graph, with observations conditionally independent across sites given the labels and each depending only on its corresponding hidden state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden Markov tree
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-variable model on a fixed rooted tree in which hidden states factor into a root distribution and conditionally independent parent-to-child transitions, with observations emitted independently by their corresponding hidden states.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden–observed pair Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-variable spatial-model family in which each site contains a hidden label and an observation, and their joint paired field has a normalized Gibbs factorization on a specified neighborhood graph, without requiring either marginal field to be Markov on that graph.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hidden semi-Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-state sequence-model family that assigns explicit distributions to state sojourn durations, with state changes governed by an embedded transition process and observations conditioned on the hidden states.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hierarchical harmonium
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A labeled harmonium model family coupling binary words, Gaussian image features and binary category indicators to shared Gaussian latent variables, with a proper joint Gaussian precision and classification through posterior label probabilities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hierarchical log-bilinear language model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A next-word language architecture that computes one linear context feature vector and uses its dot products with internal-node vectors to assign normalized vocabulary-tree probabilities, summing path probabilities when a word has multiple codes.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hierarchical mixture of experts
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional mixture-model family that organizes output experts as leaves of a tree and forms each leaf’s mixture weight by multiplying input-dependent probabilistic gates along its root-to-leaf path.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural next-word architecture that factors word probabilities along a binary vocabulary tree and shares a nonlinear branch predictor conditioned on context-word embeddings and a separate embedding of the current tree node.

identities.value: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model

historical_semantic_rows.name: Hierarchical softmax
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural categorical-output component that assigns a probability to each vocabulary leaf by multiplying normalized branch probabilities along its path through a word tree.

historical_semantic_rows.name: IDA* with an Incremental Model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An iterative-deepening heuristic search algorithm that learns a conditional model of search-tree cost increments, predicts later cost thresholds to target increased expansion counts, and completes the goal-finding iteration by branch-and-bound.

historical_semantic_rows.name: INLA group node conflict diagnostic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A group-wise Bayesian model diagnostic for latent Gaussian models that uses two INLA fits per selected group to compare remaining-data and within-group information about its latent linear predictor vector. Fitted mean and covariance summaries yield a quadratic conflict score with a rank-based Gaussian chi-square reference. Nuisance-parameter updating, replication dependence and numerical rank choices determine the interpretation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Improved consistency training
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The consistency-model training procedure of Song and Dhariwal that learns directly from paired shared-noise data perturbations using a stop-gradient teacher with current student parameters, a Pseudo-Huber discrepancy, revised noise weighting and sampling, and a staged increase in noise-discretization intervals.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Independence Metropolis–Hastings sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler whose proposal distribution is fixed independently of the current state, with proposal-density ratios still included in acceptance.

historical_semantic_rows.name: InfoNCE
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A contrastive log-softmax objective that identifies a joint positive among sampled candidates and, under independent marginal-negative sampling, gives an expectation-level lower bound on mutual information.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Input-output hidden Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family whose discrete hidden-state transitions and state-specific observation distributions depend on the current external input.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Interpolated variational information bound
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of multi-sample mutual-information lower bounds that interpolates the critic’s empirical partition estimate with a positive variational normalizer inside a ratio, connecting NWJ and InfoNCE parameterizations.

identities.value: Nonlinearly interpolated mutual information lower bound

historical_semantic_rows.name: Invariant information clustering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural clustering procedure that maximizes mutual information between discrete cluster-assignment variables for paired unlabeled samples, estimating their joint distribution from the network’s soft assignment probabilities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Iterated conditional modes
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A deterministic conditional-mode optimization algorithm that repeatedly updates one variable to a mode of its conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining variables, seeking a coordinatewise mode of a fixed joint distribution.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Iterative conditional estimation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An incomplete-data parameter-estimation procedure that repeatedly replaces a chosen complete-data estimator by its conditional expectation given observed data under the current parameter estimate.

historical_semantic_rows.name: KADABRA adaptive betweenness approximation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An adaptive sampling algorithm for static-graph betweenness that averages internal-node indicators of uniformly sampled shortest paths and stops when node-specific confidence radii meet an additive tolerance or a predetermined sample horizon is reached.

historical_semantic_rows.name: KADABRA balanced bidirectional shortest-path sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A shortest-path sampling algorithm that expands complete breadth-first-search frontiers from opposite endpoints according to frontier edge volume, then samples a connecting edge and its two path segments with shortest-path-count weights to obtain a uniform shortest path.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Knuth backtrack-tree estimation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A randomized estimator of additive properties of a fixed backtracking tree that follows a sampled root-to-terminal path and weights each visited node contribution by the inverse probability of reaching it.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Local interpretable model-agnostic explanations
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A prediction-explanation method fitting an interpretable surrogate to locally weighted samples of a model's behavior.

historical_semantic_rows.name: LargeVis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A dimensionality-reduction and graph-visualization algorithm that constructs an approximate weighted nearest-neighbor graph and learns low-dimensional coordinates with sampled attractive-edge and repulsive-pair likelihood terms.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Layer-wise adaptive rate control
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A parameter-block learning-rate control rule whose clipping form limits a vanilla stochastic-gradient step by using the smaller of a global learning rate and a trust coefficient times the block parameter-norm to gradient-norm ratio.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Learning Fair Representations
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A prototype-based representation-learning algorithm that jointly balances reconstruction, supervised prediction and differences between group-average prototype assignment probabilities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Leave-one-out mutual information upper bound
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An expectation-level upper bound on mutual information that compares a known conditional density for each paired sample with a mixture of conditional densities from the other independent inputs in its batch.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Liu modified discrete-state Gibbs sampler
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A discrete conditional sampling algorithm that proposes a category from the full conditional distribution with the current category excluded, then applies a Metropolis correction to preserve the original conditional distribution.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Logarithmic opinion pool
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probability-aggregation method that forms a normalized weighted geometric mean of expert distributions over the same outcomes, using nonnegative exponent weights that sum to one.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Lookup Conditional Distribution Prediction
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A computational variant of conditional distribution prediction that precomputes or memoizes fixed-model subtree expansion-count estimates for type and remaining-cost contexts, then reuses those estimates when predicting a complete IDA* iteration from a shallow search frontier.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Markov Chain Monte Carlo Stochastic Approximation Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic approximation EM extension that advances a persistent latent-state Markov chain targeting the conditional distribution at the current parameter, updates an averaged sufficient statistic from that state, and maximizes the resulting complete-data objective.

identities.value: Markov Chain Monte Carlo Stochastic Approximation Expectation Maximization

historical_semantic_rows.name: Markov decision process
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A sequential decision model with states, actions, Markov transitions, and rewards.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Markov random field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An undirected graphical probability model associating potential functions with variable groups.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Maximum coding likelihood estimation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A conditional parameter-estimation method that selects mutually non-neighboring sites in a Markov field and maximizes their joint conditional likelihood, which factors into sitewise full conditionals given the remaining observed sites.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Maximum pseudolikelihood estimation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A parameter-estimation method that maximizes the product of a specified model’s sitewise full conditional probabilities or densities evaluated at the observed configuration.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Mean-field Boltzmann learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A deterministic approximation to Boltzmann-machine parameter learning that substitutes mean-field phase statistics for stochastic equilibrium correlations in the positive-minus-negative weight update.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Memory Network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of learning models that combines an addressable memory with input conversion, memory updating, output inference and response components, allowing predictions to use stored information through learned or otherwise specified component implementations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a Gaussian step with drift proportional to the target log-density gradient and corrects the asymmetric proposal with an accept/reject test.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Metropolis–Hastings sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that proposes a new state from a specified transition distribution and accepts it with the smaller of one and the target-density ratio multiplied by the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio, otherwise retaining the current state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A componentwise Monte Carlo scheme that uses Metropolis–Hastings transitions targeting full conditional distributions for one or more coordinate blocks, optionally combined with exact Gibbs updates for other blocks.

historical_semantic_rows.name: MixMatch
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that averages predictions over augmented unlabeled inputs, sharpens the resulting soft targets, mixes augmented labeled and unlabeled input-target pairs, and optimizes labeled cross-entropy plus an unlabeled squared-probability loss.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Mixed memory Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of compact temporal probability models whose component transition distributions are convex mixtures of transition tables indexed by a single selected predecessor lag or component.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Mixture density network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural conditional-density architecture whose input-dependent outputs parameterize the mixing weights and component distributions of a finite mixture over target variables.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analyzers
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite Gaussian mixture whose components each have a linear standard-normal latent factor and component-specific isotropic observation noise, giving covariance W_i W_i^T+sigma_i^2 I and probabilistic assignments to local principal-component models.

identities.value: Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analyzers
Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analysers

historical_semantic_rows.name: Monotonic Gaussian process with virtual derivatives
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Gaussian-process inference procedure that promotes monotonicity in selected input coordinates by combining observed outputs with finite virtual derivative-sign factors and approximating the resulting posterior using expectation propagation.

identities.value: Monotonic Gaussian process with virtual derivatives

historical_semantic_rows.name: Monte Carlo Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An expectation-maximization method that approximates the current conditional expected complete-data log objective by Monte Carlo integration and maximizes that sampled objective to update the parameters.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Multiple-testing node conflict diagnostic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian evidence-synthesis diagnostic that partitions information at replicated separator nodes, stacks declared contrasts between transformed copies, and uses their joint covariance and a multivariate reference distribution to assess global and multiplicity-adjusted local conflict. Its single-step max-absolute-statistic adjustment accounts for correlation within an explicitly selected family of comparisons.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Multiple-try Metropolis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis sampling algorithm that selects a candidate from several weighted forward proposals, draws a backward reference set containing the original state, and corrects acceptance using the ratio of their total weights.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Multiple-try Metropolis within Gibbs
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A coordinate-update sampler that applies a multiple-try Metropolis transition to a conditional target while holding all other coordinates fixed.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Mutual information neural estimation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A mutual-information estimation procedure that trains a neural statistics function to maximize a Donsker–Varadhan objective contrasting joint samples with product-of-marginals samples, using stochastic optimization and an optional moving-average denominator for gradient estimation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Naive Bayes
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Probabilistic classification assuming feature independence conditional on the class.

historical_semantic_rows.name: NeXO ontology construction
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A network-based ontology-construction procedure that starts from a probabilistic hierarchy of gene communities, removes unsupported binary restrictions to permit multiway joins, and adds supported second-parent connections to produce an overlapping term hierarchy.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Neal backtracking-suppressed MCMC
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite-state MCMC construction that augments a reversible chain with its preceding state and replaces a conditional resampling step with a balanced conditional kernel that suppresses immediate backtracking while preserving the target marginal.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Neighbourhood components analysis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A supervised metric-learning algorithm that learns a linear transformation by maximizing the expected number of correctly classified training examples under stochastic leave-one-out neighbor selection.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Neural autoregressive distribution estimator
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fully visible autoregressive density model whose ordered variable conditionals are computed by neural networks that share input-to-hidden parameters and recursively reuse prefix computations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Neural probabilistic language model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural finite-context language architecture that jointly learns a shared word-embedding lookup and a nonlinear predictor of the next-word distribution using concatenated context embeddings and a vocabulary softmax.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Neural variational inference and learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A method for jointly training a directed latent-variable model and an amortized stochastic inference network by maximizing a variational log-likelihood bound, using score-function inference gradients with learned baselines and adaptive learning-signal normalization.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Newman random-walk betweenness matrix computation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An exact network-analysis algorithm that computes random-walk betweenness from an embedded inverse of a grounded graph Laplacian, explicitly enumerates source–target pairs, and averages their incident-current magnitudes with a specified endpoint convention.

identities.value: Newman matrix algorithm for random-walk betweenness

historical_semantic_rows.name: Noh–Rieger random-walk centrality
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A node-scoring method for an undirected random walk that divides each node’s stationary visitation probability by its integrated excess return probability, yielding a centrality whose reciprocal differences determine pairwise mean first-passage-time asymmetry.

identities.value: Random walk centrality of Noh and Rieger

historical_semantic_rows.name: Noisy-OR belief network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A directed acyclic binary probabilistic network that models a node’s inactivity as the product of a leak-failure factor and failure factors for its active parents.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Noisy rectifier
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic activation that adds zero-mean noise to a preactivation and then applies the positive-part rectifier, producing h=max(0,a+z).

historical_semantic_rows.name: Non-conjugate variational message passing
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An approximate inference algorithm that restricts variational blocks to exponential families and updates their natural parameters by matching expected-log-factor gradients through the sufficient-statistic covariance.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Nonparametric Bayes pachinko allocation model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian pachinko topic-model family using coupled hierarchical Dirichlet-process allocations to infer occupied supertopics and shared subtopics, with subtopic allocation groups determined by latent supertopic assignments.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Nonreversible Metropolis uniform update
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis transition algorithm that retains a signed uniform acceptance variable, updates it by wrapped translation, and rescales it after an accepted state proposal to preserve a joint target distribution while changing the temporal dependence of acceptance decisions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Novelty+ SAT heuristic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Novelty extension that, at each SAT search step, chooses a random variable from a randomly selected unsatisfied clause with a fixed walk probability and otherwise uses Novelty’s recency-conditioned best/second-best selector.

historical_semantic_rows.name: NovoGrad
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic gradient optimizer that rescales each parameter block gradient by a scalar running second moment of that block gradient norm before accumulating momentum, with an optional weight-decay contribution added after gradient normalization.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Order-agnostic NADE training
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic training procedure that shares neural conditional parameters across variable orderings and estimates the order-averaged NADE log-likelihood objective using a sampled observed prefix and losses for all remaining variables.

historical_semantic_rows.name: No-U-Turn sampler (original slice formulation)
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The original 2014 slice-based NUTS algorithm, which adapts a Hamiltonian trajectory’s length through randomly directed binary-tree doubling and selects a valid next state while enforcing subtree U-turn and reversibility conditions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: PHATE
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A dimensionality-reduction algorithm that computes diffusion transition probabilities, measures Euclidean distances between their negative-log rows, and uses metric multidimensional scaling to embed those potential distances.

identities.value: Potential of Heat Diffusion for Affinity-based Transition Embedding

historical_semantic_rows.name: Pachinko allocation model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A topic-model family that generates each word by traversing a directed acyclic graph from a root through topic nodes to a word leaf, using probability distributions over each node's children.

historical_semantic_rows.name: PageRank
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A link-analysis ranking algorithm that assigns node scores using a random walk mixing normalized outgoing-link transitions with teleportation to a specified restart distribution, under an explicit policy for nodes with no outgoing weight.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Pairwise Markov chain
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hidden-state sequence-model family in which the joint process of a hidden variable and its corresponding observation is first-order Markov, without requiring either marginal process to be Markov or observations to be conditionally independent given the hidden path.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Pairwise Markov tree
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-variable tree-model family whose paired hidden and observed states factor into a root distribution and parent-to-child conditional kernels on a fixed rooted tree, without requiring the hidden marginal to be Markov on that tree.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Papadimitriou 2-SAT random walk
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A randomized 2-SAT search procedure that starts from any complete truth assignment and repeatedly selects an unsatisfied clause and flips a uniformly chosen literal’s variable until a satisfying assignment is reached or a selected move budget ends.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Parallel alternating Newton-like algorithm for APM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A block-alternating Newton-like method for fitting an admixture of Poisson Markov random fields through a sparsity-penalized nodewise Poisson regression surrogate, alternating topic coefficients with document-specific simplex weights and parallelizing independent subproblems.

identities.value: Parallel alternating Newton-like algorithm for APM

historical_semantic_rows.name: Parallel tempering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A population Monte Carlo method that combines within-temperature target-preserving updates with corrected exchanges between replicas targeting differently tempered densities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Parametric UMAP
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A parametric dimensionality-reduction algorithm that trains a neural mapping from input points to embedding coordinates using sampled attractive and repulsive losses derived from a UMAP neighborhood graph.

identities.value: Parametric Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection

historical_semantic_rows.name: Partially noncentered GLMM variational inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian generalized linear mixed-model inference procedure that uses cluster-specific partial noncentering to define independent Gaussian fixed-effect and transformed random-effect blocks, factors an inverse-Wishart random-effect covariance, and alternates nonconjugate Gaussian message proposals with an exact covariance coordinate.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Partially observable Markov decision process
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Markov decision model in which observations provide incomplete information about the current state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Particle swarm optimization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A population-based optimization method that moves candidate particles through a search space using retained velocities and stochastic attraction toward remembered personal and shared best positions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Path integral clustering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An agglomerative clustering algorithm that merges clusters with the greatest increase in their size-normalized sums of discounted random-walk paths when paths are allowed through the proposed union.

identities.value: Agglomerative clustering via maximum incremental path integral

historical_semantic_rows.name: Persistent contrastive divergence
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A learning algorithm that estimates an energy model’s negative-phase statistics with Markov chains whose states persist across parameter updates, rather than restarting those chains at the current data minibatch.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Pi-model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that combines labeled cross-entropy with squared disagreement between two stochastic predictions of the same input from a shared-parameter network, propagating gradients through both predictions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: PointNet++
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A hierarchical point-set neural architecture that repeatedly samples centroids, groups metric neighborhoods and applies local PointNet feature extraction, with multi-scale or multi-resolution constructions for variable sampling density.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Poisson generalized root model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generalized root probability model on unbounded nonnegative integer counts, with factorial base measures and symmetric products of j-th roots involving at most j distinct variables, normalizable for every finite parameter tensor on a finite variable set.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Population-based incremental learning
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An optimization method that samples candidate solutions from a probability-vector representation and incrementally moves that representation toward high-evaluation sampled solutions, with probability-vector mutation in its basic formulation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target whose proposal combines the current state with an independent draw from that reference using a scalar autoregressive coefficient.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that preconditions the potential-gradient drift by the reference covariance and uses a scalar Crank–Nicolson autoregressive update.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Principal Curves
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A nonlinear statistical summary defined by a smooth curve that is self-consistent for a data distribution: almost every point on the curve equals the conditional mean of observations whose nearest-point projection lands there.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Probabilistic latent semantic analysis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-class model of document–word or other dyadic co-occurrences that represents their joint probability as a mixture of conditionally independent distributions over the two observed entities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Probabilistic Principal Component Analysis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A linear Gaussian latent-variable model with a standard-normal latent prior and isotropic observation noise, whose maximum-likelihood loading subspace corresponds to leading principal components under the stated covariance-rank conditions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Product of experts
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A probabilistic model family that combines expert factors over the same observations by multiplying their values and normalizing the product over the observation space.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Product of hidden Markov models
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A sequence-model family that multiplies the marginal probabilities assigned to a complete observation sequence by several hidden Markov models and normalizes the product over sequences of the same length.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Quadratic Poisson graphical model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A graphical probability model on nonnegative integer counts whose joint log mass contains unary linear terms, site quadratic terms and symmetric pairwise count products, with parameters restricted to make its infinite-support partition function finite.

historical_semantic_rows.name: REINFORCE
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of stochastic reinforcement-learning update rules that multiply a sampled reward relative to an admissible baseline by the derivative of the log probability of the sampled action or unit output, with a nonnegative learning-rate factor.

historical_semantic_rows.name: R-Novelty+ SAT heuristic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The 1999 R-Novelty extension that replaces its periodic random override with a fixed per-step probability of a random clause-variable flip and otherwise uses the recency- and score-gap-dependent R-Novelty selector.

historical_semantic_rows.name: RandAugment
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An image-augmentation procedure that applies a uniformly sampled sequence of operations sharing one magnitude parameter, reducing augmentation selection to tuning the operation count and shared magnitude on the target task.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Random-only abstraction for abstraction sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A randomized abstraction rule for graphical-model sampling that uniformly permutes the current search nodes and divides that order into groups of nearly equal cardinality, within which the surrounding sampler selects and importance-weights representatives.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Random-walk Metropolis–Hastings sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a new state by adding an increment drawn from a fixed distribution independent of the current state.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Randomized latent score conflict diagnostic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian hierarchical-model diagnostic that freezes draws from a parent posterior excluding selected child data, draws child latent parameters conditionally, and compares derivatives of an expanded conditional log prior with scores of conditional-prior replicates. The resulting randomized tail values are examined and optionally combined as a model-conflict summary, with calibration depending on the actual sampling law, score direction and aggregation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: RAPID support vector data description sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A density-based training-subset selection method for support vector data description that prefilters low-density observations and greedily removes high-density inliers while testing a retained-density threshold on the original inlier set.

identities.value: RAPID support vector data description sampling
Reducing samples by pruning of inlier densities

historical_semantic_rows.name: Rate-adapting Poisson model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A harmonium model family coupling unbounded visible Poisson counts to finite binomial hidden variables through bilinear interactions that shift conditional log rates and binomial logits.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Real-valued neural autoregressive density estimator
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fully visible neural autoregressive density architecture for real-valued vectors that shares input-to-hidden parameters across ordered scalar conditional mixture-density models.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Rectified flow
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A transport-learning method that regresses a velocity field on endpoint differences along straight interpolations of coupled samples and uses the resulting ordinary differential equation to transport the source distribution, optionally repeating rectification using the learned endpoint coupling.

historical_semantic_rows.name: RNN-NADE
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture in which a deterministic recurrent state supplies parameters of a NADE output distribution, combining temporal recurrence with normalized within-frame autoregressive conditionals.

identities.value: Recurrent neural network neural autoregressive distribution estimator

historical_semantic_rows.name: RNN-RBM
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture in which a deterministic recurrent network with its own hidden state supplies parameters of a conditional RBM that models each next visible vector.

identities.value: Recurrent neural network restricted Boltzmann machine

historical_semantic_rows.name: Recurrent temporal restricted Boltzmann machine
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A recurrent neural sequence architecture whose deterministic state is a conditional RBM hidden-probability vector and sets the next step’s hidden bias, with visible observations drawn from that step’s RBM marginal.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Recursive best-first search
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A recursive search algorithm that explores the best stored subtree alternative within an upper bound and conditionally passes a previously backed-up value to regenerated children, retaining path and sibling information instead of the full best-first frontier.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Regularized information maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A discriminative clustering framework that fits conditional class probabilities by maximizing empirical input–assignment mutual information penalized by classifier complexity, with linear and kernel softmax configurations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Rejection-driven independence Metropolis sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An independence Metropolis sampler whose proposals are generated by a rejection procedure with a fixed possibly non-dominating envelope, followed by a Metropolis correction for the resulting clipped proposal law.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Rejection sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A random-variate generation algorithm that draws proposals from a normalized envelope dominating an unnormalized target and accepts each with the target-to-envelope ratio, yielding independent target draws with fresh independent random trials.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine Collaborative Filtering
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of shared-parameter restricted Boltzmann models for categorical user-item ratings, with a user-specific visible set and optional conditioning on the item-observation mask and low-rank factorization of rating interactions.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Reweighted wake-sleep
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A learning procedure for paired generative and inference networks that uses multiple inference samples and normalized importance weights for generative-model updates, with recognition updates from importance-weighted observed-data samples, model-generated sleep samples, or both.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Riondato–Kornaropoulos fixed-sample betweenness approximation
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A fixed-sample graph betweenness approximation algorithm that chooses a sample count using a VC-dimension bound for shortest-path incidence ranges, then averages internal-vertex indicators from independent uniform endpoint-pair and conditional shortest-path draws.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Robust adaptive Metropolis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An adaptive random-walk Metropolis algorithm that updates the proposal shape factor by a rank-one transformation driven by the proposal direction and the difference between its acceptance probability and a chosen target rate.

historical_semantic_rows.name: SamplePairing
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An image-classification augmentation procedure that averages an anchor image with a randomly selected training image using equal pixel weights and trains against the anchor image’s label, with a training schedule that includes phases without pairing.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Scheduled sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An autoregressive sequence-training procedure that chooses between reference and model-produced previous outputs as feedback, using a schedule that progressively reduces the probability of reference feedback.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Separator-node conflict diagnostic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Bayesian graphical-model diagnostic that duplicates a selected separator node or node vector, partitions the information informing it, and compares the resulting partition-specific distributions on a declared scale. It assesses local incompatibility through explicitly chosen discrete agreement, signed-tail, radial or density-level scores, with nuisance dependence handled by a specified split or cut.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Shared inverse-lengthscale variational sparse-spectrum inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The Tan–Ong–Nott–Jasra sparse-spectrum regression inference procedure that alternates a Gaussian nonconjugate variational proposal for a shared inverse-lengthscale vector with full Gaussian coefficient and half-Cauchy-derived scale-coordinate updates.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Sigmoid belief network
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A directed acyclic probabilistic network of binary variables whose forward conditional probabilities are logistic functions of weighted parent states and a bias.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Simulated annealing
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic optimization procedure that explores candidate configurations with temperature-controlled acceptance of cost-increasing moves and progressively cools that acceptance process to concentrate search on low-cost configurations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Single-step parametric maxT inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A simultaneous-inference procedure for a declared family of linear functions of model parameters that standardizes joint estimates and uses the maximum absolute statistic under a centered multivariate normal or t reference to compute multiplicity-adjusted tests and a common critical value for simultaneous intervals. Exact or asymptotic validity depends on the joint sampling law and covariance estimation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Slice sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An auxiliary-variable Monte Carlo method that augments a target density with a uniform height below its graph and updates the state using a transition preserving the uniform distribution on the resulting density slice.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Soft actor-critic
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An off-policy actor-critic algorithm fitting a stochastic policy and soft value functions under a reward-plus-policy-entropy objective.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Space-Alternating Generalized Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generalized expectation-maximization method that updates selected parameter blocks using block-specific hidden-data spaces or valid objective-improvement surrogates, refreshing the conditional expectation or surrogate at the current estimate before the next block.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Sparse additive generative model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A generative model family for categorical text data that forms word probabilities by normalizing a background log-frequency vector plus sparse component deviations, allowing multiple generative facets to combine additively in log space.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Sparse Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An EM variant that updates relative latent-state probabilities within selected plausible sets while preserving their total mass and all outside probabilities, and fits parameters using the resulting full distributions with occasional complete posterior refreshes.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Sparse pachinko allocation inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An approximate pachinko-allocation fitting procedure that restricts token path resampling to currently active document topics and word-associated subtopics, interleaving full sampling with pruning and optionally growing the training corpus incrementally.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process linearized uncertain-input prediction
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A local uncertain-input prediction algorithm for a fixed sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process posterior that linearizes the posterior mean at the Gaussian input mean, freezes the conditional variance there, and uses the resulting approximate mean and covariance for a Gaussian output representation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Spatial Transformer
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A learnable neural-network component that predicts an input-dependent spatial transformation and uses the resulting sampling grid to warp an image or feature tensor.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Square root graphical model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of finite undirected graphical probability models that retains univariate base measures while coupling specified square roots of sufficient statistics through unary terms and a symmetric quadratic form, with parameters restricted to a finite joint partition function.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stepping-out slice sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A univariate slice-sampling algorithm that randomly places a width-w interval around the current point, expands it in width-w steps under a randomly divided budget, and samples by slice-aware interval shrinkage.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic Approximation Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An incomplete-data fitting method that recursively averages simulated complete-data log objectives or sufficient statistics using a step-size sequence, then maximizes the accumulated objective to update the model parameters.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic beam search
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The sequence-sampling algorithm of Kool, van Hoof and Welling that implements Gumbel-Top-k without replacement implicitly on a locally normalized sequence tree by propagating conditional perturbed subtree maxima and retaining the k highest-scoring prefixes at each level.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic depth
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A residual-network training procedure that randomly bypasses residual transformations during training and uses all residual transformations with survival-probability scaling during inference.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic Expectation Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite-mixture fitting algorithm that draws one hard component assignment for each observation from its current posterior responsibilities, fits the resulting completed-data model, and recomputes the responsibilities for the next iteration.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic factorized variational sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The Gal–Turner stochastic extension of factorized variational sparse-spectrum regression that estimates its full-data evidence lower bound with uniformly sampled observation minibatches, scaling likelihood contributions by the population-to-batch ratio while retaining global KL penalties once.

identities.value: Stochastic factorized variational sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process inference

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic gradient descent
historical_semantic_rows.definition: Optimization using gradients estimated from sampled training observations.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic nonconjugate GLMM variational inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite-population Bayesian GLMM inference procedure that iterates selected cluster-local Gaussian factors and uses expanded cluster minibatch contributions to damp global Gaussian and inverse-Wishart natural parameters. This record follows the Tan–Nott natural-gradient derivation with its complete covariance target and explicit sampling and local-solution qualifications.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic Pooling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A spatial neural pooling layer that samples one activation per region with probability proportional to its nonnegative value during training and uses an activation-weighted regional mean during deterministic inference.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Stochastic-times-smooth unit
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A stochastic activation that sets p=sigmoid(a), samples a Bernoulli gate with success probability sqrt(p), and outputs the gate multiplied by sqrt(p).

historical_semantic_rows.name: Straight-through estimator
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A surrogate-gradient rule that keeps a hard threshold or sampled binary output in the forward computation while propagating its downstream derivative backward as though the hard operation were the identity function.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Straight-through Gumbel-Softmax estimator
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A surrogate-gradient estimator that uses a hard one-hot argmax of a Gumbel-Softmax sample in the forward computation and substitutes the corresponding continuous softmax relaxation’s derivative in the backward computation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Structured mean-field inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational inference method that approximates a target distribution with a tractable family retaining selected dependencies, choosing its parameters to reduce the approximation-to-target Kullback–Leibler divergence.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Structured variational inference for factorial HMMs
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational inference procedure for factorial hidden Markov models that approximates the posterior by independent chain-path distributions while retaining temporal dependence within each chain.

identities.value: Structured variational inference for factorial HMMs
Structured mean-field inference for factorial HMMs

historical_semantic_rows.name: Supplemented Expectation Conditional Maximization
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A numerical supplement to expectation conditional maximization that recovers observed-data asymptotic parameter covariance from expected complete-data information and the local derivatives of both the ECM update and its frozen-expectation conditional-maximization sweep.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A minority-class oversampling method that generates synthetic labeled feature vectors by interpolating between an observed minority example and selected neighbors from the same class.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Tempered transitions
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo transition algorithm that proposes a new target state through a prescribed outward and return sequence of mutually reversed kernels for auxiliary distributions, then accepts or rejects the endpoint using density ratios evaluated along the complete path.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Temporal ensembling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A semi-supervised classifier-training procedure that regularizes a current stochastic prediction toward a bias-corrected exponential average of earlier predictions for the same indexed training example, alongside labeled cross-entropy.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Temporal factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A sequential extension of the factored RBM language model that directs information from the preceding binary hidden state into the current hidden bias, propagating context beyond the explicit word window.

identities.value: Temporal factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model

historical_semantic_rows.name: Temporal restricted Boltzmann machine
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture that multiplies time-indexed conditional RBM distributions whose visible and hidden biases depend on preceding visible and hidden states through shared temporal weights.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Topographic Independent Component Analysis
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A linear latent-component model whose otherwise conditionally independent source components share random scales through fixed overlapping neighborhoods, allowing nearby component energies to be dependent while supporting a topographic organization of the representation.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Triplet Markov chain
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-variable sequence-model family that introduces an auxiliary process so that the joint hidden, auxiliary and observed process is first-order Markov, while the hidden–observed pair obtained by marginalizing the auxiliary process need not be Markov.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Triplet Markov field
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A latent-variable spatial-model family that introduces an auxiliary field so the complete hidden, auxiliary and observed triplet has a normalized Gibbs factorization on a specified neighborhood graph, while its hidden–observed projection need not remain Markov on that graph.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Truncated Poisson graphical model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A finite pairwise count graphical model with a fixed upper count limit, factorial base measures and Poisson-kernel full conditionals renormalized over the bounded support, allowing finite symmetric interactions of either sign.

historical_semantic_rows.name: UMAP
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A nonlinear embedding algorithm that constructs a locally scaled, symmetrized nearest-neighbor similarity graph and places its vertices in a lower-dimensional space using sampled attractive and repulsive updates.

identities.value: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction

historical_semantic_rows.name: Unadjusted Langevin algorithm
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An approximate sampling algorithm that discretizes overdamped Langevin dynamics by an explicit gradient drift and Gaussian noise without a Metropolis acceptance correction.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Value-based abstraction functions for abstraction sampling
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A family of graphical-model sampling abstractions that assigns a positive scalar value to each current search node and partitions nodes in value order into abstract states used by the surrounding importance-weighted representative sampler.

identities.value: Value-based abstraction functions for abstraction sampling

historical_semantic_rows.name: Variational Fair Autoencoder
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational autoencoder architecture for learning representations with reduced sensitive or nuisance information, combining sensitive-variable-conditioned inference and generation with an MMD penalty on group-conditional aggregated latent distributions and a semi-supervised predictive component.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Variational message passing
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A variational inference algorithm that organizes conjugate-exponential coordinate updates as local messages carrying expected sufficient statistics and natural-parameter contributions through a Bayesian network.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Variational sparse-spectrum Gaussian-process inference
historical_semantic_rows.definition: The Gal–Turner finite spectral regression inference procedure that factorizes spectral parameters from output coefficients, analytically optimizes an unrestricted Gaussian coefficient factor, and optimizes the resulting evidence lower bound over the spectral variational distribution and model hyperparameters.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Voting classifier
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A classifier combining base predictions through class votes or aggregated class probabilities.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Wake-sleep algorithm
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An alternating learning procedure that trains a generative network from observed data and recognition-sampled hidden states during wake, and trains a recognition network from generative-model samples during sleep.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Wavelet-domain hidden Markov model
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A statistical wavelet-coefficient model family using latent mixture states to represent coefficient distributions and Markov dependencies among those states to capture within-scale clustering or cross-scale persistence.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Zeta merging
historical_semantic_rows.definition: An agglomerative graph-clustering algorithm that selects the pair with the largest sum of conditional increases in average log-diagonal resolvent popularity.

historical_semantic_rows.name: Zhou random-walk distance-profile dissimilarity
historical_semantic_rows.definition: A pairwise graph dissimilarity that compares the mean first-passage-time profiles of two adjacent vertices by taking the Euclidean norm of their differences to all other vertices and dividing that norm by N-2, for a graph of N vertices.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Bayesian Network
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A network that is a probabilistic graphical model representing variables and their conditional dependencies via a directed acyclic graph.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Boltzmann Machine Network
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A symmetrically connected network that is a type of stochastic recurrent neural network and Markov random field.

identities.value: stochastic Hopfield network with hidden units

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Markov Chain
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A network that is a stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events where the probability of each event depends only on the previous event's state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Probabilistic Graphical Model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A machine learning task in which a graph expresses the conditional dependence structure between random variables.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Probabilistic Hidden Layer
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A hidden layer that estimates the probability of a sample being within a certain category.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Probabilistic Topic Model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A probabilistic graphical model that uses statistical techniques to analyze the words in each text to discover common themes their connections and their changes over time.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Boltzmann machine network that learns the probability distribution of its input data.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Selection And Sampling Bias
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A computational bias introduced by non-random selection of individuals groups or data failing to ensure representativeness.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: UpSampling1D Layer
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A reshaping layer that upsamples the input by repeating each temporal step size times along the time axis.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: UpSampling2D Layer
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A layer that upsamples the input by repeating each row and column size times.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: UpSampling3D Layer
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A layer that upsamples the input by repeating each depth, height and width size times.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: ABRA-s-fix fixed-sample betweenness approximation
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A fixed-sample static-graph betweenness algorithm that averages shortest-path fractions over a user-specified number of uniform endpoint pairs and returns both the estimates and a simultaneous Rademacher-based additive error bound, regardless of the size of that bound.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: AND/OR abstraction sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An importance-sampling algorithm for partition functions of discrete graphical models that samples representatives in a pseudo-tree-guided AND/OR search space, allowing abstractions across branching-ancestor contexts through interleaved ancestor pruning and relative-weight value backup.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Adaptive Metropolis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A history-adaptive random-walk Metropolis sampler whose Gaussian proposal covariance is estimated from the accumulated retained states, including repetitions after rejected proposals.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Adaptive rejection sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: The Gilks–Wild univariate rejection sampler that uses tangents to a concave log density as a piecewise-linear upper hull and chords as a lower hull, updating these bounds from evaluated proposals.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Adaptive scaling Metropolis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A random-walk Metropolis algorithm that adapts its proposal scale through stochastic approximation driven by the proposal acceptance probability relative to a chosen target rate.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Adaptive scaling within adaptive Metropolis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An adaptive Metropolis algorithm that combines acceptance-rate-driven scalar proposal scaling with recursive mean and covariance-shape adaptation from retained samples.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family that draws each document from a proper Poisson-MRF base distribution whose canonical unary and interaction parameters are convex combinations of topic parameters under document-specific simplex weights.

identities.value: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Ancestral Gumbel-Top-k sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An exact without-replacement sampler for finite discrete Bayesian-network configurations that propagates conditional Gumbel subtree maxima through a bounded priority frontier, with a configurable number of parallel expansions and parent-respecting variable selection.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Annealed importance sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Monte Carlo estimation algorithm that draws from a tractable base distribution, applies Markov transitions invariant for a prescribed sequence of intermediate distributions, and weights each resulting path by successive unnormalized-density ratios to estimate target expectations and normalizing-constant ratios.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Auto-binomial Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for bounded site counts whose full conditionals are binomial with fixed trial counts and log odds linear in neighboring counts, using symmetric interaction coefficients.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Auto-exponential Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for nonnegative continuous site values with exponential full conditionals whose rates are positive baseline terms plus nonnegative symmetric linear neighbor interactions.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Auto-normal Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A proper finite Gaussian Markov-field model specified by linear full-conditional means and positive, value-independent site conditional variances, with compatibility enforced by a symmetric positive-definite joint precision matrix.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Auto-Poisson Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for unbounded nonnegative integer counts whose full conditionals are Poisson with log means linear in neighboring counts and whose symmetric interaction coefficients are nonpositive.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Autoregressive conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A neural sequence architecture that models each current vector with a conditional RBM whose visible and hidden biases are affine functions of a fixed window of preceding observed vectors, without hidden-to-hidden temporal links.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Boltzmann chain
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A family of tied-weight undirected Boltzmann sequence models with hidden temporal variables, observed variables and chain-derived connectivity chosen to permit exact elimination.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Brandes–Fleischer sampled-pair current-flow betweenness
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A randomized network-analysis algorithm that estimates normalized, endpoint-excluded current-flow betweenness by independently sampling uniform source–sink pairs, solving their grounded electrical-network systems, and averaging scaled vertex throughputs.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A conditional neural probability model that represents an output vector with an RBM whose biases or interactions are determined by a supplied conditioning vector.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Conjugate-gradient Monte Carlo
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A population Markov sampler that obtains a local-optimization anchor from one population member and updates another member along the anchor line with a multiple-try transition targeting a radial-Jacobian-adjusted density.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Context-sensitive emission hidden Markov model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A hidden-state sequence-model family with a first-order Markov prior whose observation distributions depend jointly on hidden states at multiple temporal positions, introducing context beyond the contemporaneous hidden state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that combines a Crank–Nicolson treatment of the reference precision with an explicit gradient drift of the remaining target potential.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Crank–Nicolson Metropolis sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target using a Crank–Nicolson discretization of the unpreconditioned reference Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics as its proposal.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Delayed-rejection Metropolis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis-Hastings sampling procedure that can propose another candidate after rejection within the same transition, correcting acceptance for the probabilities of the forward and reversed rejected paths.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Diaconis–Holmes–Neal fiber sampler
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A finite-state Metropolis sampler that uses partitions into ordered lines, retains a binary direction for each partition, and combines a neighbor proposal with a separate probabilistic sign update to preserve a target distribution on the augmented state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Differentiable scheduled sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A scheduled-sampling training procedure that replaces discrete model-feedback embeddings with differentiable soft mixtures, allowing later sequence losses to propagate credit through earlier relaxed decoding choices.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Doubling slice sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A univariate slice-sampling algorithm that expands a randomly placed initial interval by randomly directed doublings and uses shrinkage with a retrospective acceptability test to preserve the target.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Dual-averaging step-size adaptation for Hamiltonian samplers
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A warmup procedure that tunes the logarithm of a Hamiltonian sampler’s integration step size using cumulative discrepancy from a target acceptance statistic, a shrinkage point and a smoothed sequence of iterates.

identities.value: Dual-averaging step-size adaptation for Hamiltonian samplers

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Elliptical slice sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Markov-chain update for a target factored into a Gaussian prior and a likelihood, which performs an angular slice search along the ellipse defined by the current state and an independent prior draw.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A conditional neural word model that factorizes position-specific word-to-hidden weights through a shared word-embedding matrix and couples the next categorical word to binary hidden units in a context-conditioned restricted Boltzmann machine.

identities.value: Factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Factorial hidden Markov model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A directed latent sequence-model family in which several independently evolving hidden Markov chains jointly determine the observation distribution at each time.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Fixed-length Poisson Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A finite-total count distribution whose probability on nonnegative integer vectors summing to a specified total is proportional to a Poisson factorial base measure times exponentiated linear and symmetric quadratic count potentials.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Generic tree sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An importance-sampling generalization of Chen heuristic tree sampling that merges representatives of ordered tree strata using specified positive selection probabilities and inverse-probability survivor weights to estimate an additive tree functional.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Gibbs sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that repeatedly draws a coordinate or block from its full conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining coordinates.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Gustafson guided-walk Metropolis sampler
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A continuous-state Metropolis sampler that augments a univariate state with a binary direction, proposes a half-normal displacement along that direction, retains direction after acceptance and reverses it after rejection.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for differentiable continuous targets that augments positions with momenta, proposes a state through reversible volume-preserving numerical Hamiltonian dynamics, and applies a Metropolis correction for the Hamiltonian change.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Heuristic tree sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A randomized estimator of additive properties of an implicit rooted tree that processes ordered strata using one sampled representative and an accumulated weight per stratum.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden Markov decision tree
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family that extends a probabilistic hierarchical decision tree by coupling each decision level to the same level at the previous time.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden Markov model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A sequence model whose hidden Markov states generate observations through state-dependent emission distributions.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden Markov model with auxiliary memory
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A hidden-state symbol-sequence model family in which paired states write emitted symbols to auxiliary memory and later read them to condition emissions and memory-dependent state transitions.

identities.value: Hidden Markov model with auxiliary memory

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A latent-variable graphical-model family whose unobserved label field has the Markov property on a specified neighborhood graph, with observations conditionally independent across sites given the labels and each depending only on its corresponding hidden state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden Markov tree
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A latent-variable model on a fixed rooted tree in which hidden states factor into a root distribution and conditionally independent parent-to-child transitions, with observations emitted independently by their corresponding hidden states.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden–observed pair Markov random field
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A latent-variable spatial-model family in which each site contains a hidden label and an observation, and their joint paired field has a normalized Gibbs factorization on a specified neighborhood graph, without requiring either marginal field to be Markov on that graph.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hidden semi-Markov model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A latent-state sequence-model family that assigns explicit distributions to state sojourn durations, with state changes governed by an embedded transition process and observations conditioned on the hidden states.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Hierarchical probabilistic neural network language model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A neural next-word architecture that factors word probabilities along a binary vocabulary tree and shares a nonlinear branch predictor conditioned on context-word embeddings and a separate embedding of the current tree node.
