historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Independence Metropolis–Hastings sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler whose proposal distribution is fixed independently of the current state, with proposal-density ratios still included in acceptance.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Input-output hidden Markov model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family whose discrete hidden-state transitions and state-specific observation distributions depend on the current external input.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: KADABRA balanced bidirectional shortest-path sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A shortest-path sampling algorithm that expands complete breadth-first-search frontiers from opposite endpoints according to frontier edge volume, then samples a connecting edge and its two path segments with shortest-path-count weights to obtain a uniform shortest path.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Liu modified discrete-state Gibbs sampler
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A discrete conditional sampling algorithm that proposes a category from the full conditional distribution with the current category excluded, then applies a Metropolis correction to preserve the original conditional distribution.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Markov Chain Monte Carlo Stochastic Approximation Expectation Maximization

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Markov decision process

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Mean-field Boltzmann learning

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a Gaussian step with drift proportional to the target log-density gradient and corrects the asymmetric proposal with an accept/reject test.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Metropolis–Hastings sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that proposes a new state from a specified transition distribution and accepts it with the smaller of one and the target-density ratio multiplied by the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio, otherwise retaining the current state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A componentwise Monte Carlo scheme that uses Metropolis–Hastings transitions targeting full conditional distributions for one or more coordinate blocks, optionally combined with exact Gibbs updates for other blocks.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Mixed memory Markov model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A family of compact temporal probability models whose component transition distributions are convex mixtures of transition tables indexed by a single selected predecessor lag or component.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Mixtures of Probabilistic Principal Component Analyzers

historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An expectation-maximization method that approximates the current conditional expected complete-data log objective by Monte Carlo integration and maximizes that sampled objective to update the parameters.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Multiple-try Metropolis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis sampling algorithm that selects a candidate from several weighted forward proposals, draws a backward reference set containing the original state, and corrects acceptance using the ratio of their total weights.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Multiple-try Metropolis within Gibbs
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A coordinate-update sampler that applies a multiple-try Metropolis transition to a conditional target while holding all other coordinates fixed.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Neural probabilistic language model
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A neural finite-context language architecture that jointly learns a shared word-embedding lookup and a nonlinear predictor of the next-word distribution using concatenated context embeddings and a vocabulary softmax.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Nonreversible Metropolis uniform update
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis transition algorithm that retains a signed uniform acceptance variable, updates it by wrapped translation, and rescales it after an accepted state proposal to preserve a joint target distribution while changing the temporal dependence of acceptance decisions.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: No-U-Turn sampler (original slice formulation)
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: The original 2014 slice-based NUTS algorithm, which adapts a Hamiltonian trajectory’s length through randomly directed binary-tree doubling and selects a valid next state while enforcing subtree U-turn and reversibility conditions.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Pairwise Markov chain
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A hidden-state sequence-model family in which the joint process of a hidden variable and its corresponding observation is first-order Markov, without requiring either marginal process to be Markov or observations to be conditionally independent given the hidden path.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Pairwise Markov tree
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A latent-variable tree-model family whose paired hidden and observed states factor into a root distribution and parent-to-child conditional kernels on a fixed rooted tree, without requiring the hidden marginal to be Markov on that tree.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Partially observable Markov decision process
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Markov decision model in which observations provide incomplete information about the current state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target whose proposal combines the current state with an independent draw from that reference using a scalar autoregressive coefficient.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Preconditioned Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that preconditions the potential-gradient drift by the reference covariance and uses a scalar Crank–Nicolson autoregressive update.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Probabilistic latent semantic analysis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A latent-class model of document–word or other dyadic co-occurrences that represents their joint probability as a mixture of conditionally independent distributions over the two observed entities.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Probabilistic Principal Component Analysis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A linear Gaussian latent-variable model with a standard-normal latent prior and isotropic observation noise, whose maximum-likelihood loading subspace corresponds to leading principal components under the stated covariance-rank conditions.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Product of hidden Markov models
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A sequence-model family that multiplies the marginal probabilities assigned to a complete observation sequence by several hidden Markov models and normalizes the product over sequences of the same length.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Random-only abstraction for abstraction sampling

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Random-walk Metropolis–Hastings sampling
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a new state by adding an increment drawn from a fixed distribution independent of the current state.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: RAPID support vector data description sampling

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Rejection-driven independence Metropolis sampling

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Robust adaptive Metropolis
historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An adaptive random-walk Metropolis algorithm that updates the proposal shape factor by a rank-one transformation driven by the proposal direction and the difference between its acceptance probability and a chosen target rate.

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: SamplePairing

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Scheduled sampling

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Slice sampling

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Stepping-out slice sampling

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique

historical_selected_definition_rows.name: Temporal factored restricted Boltzmann machine language model

historical_selected_definition_rows.definition: An approximate sampling algorithm that discretizes overdamped Langevin dynamics by an explicit gradient drift and Gaussian noise without a Metropolis acceptance correction.

first_script.text:
"""Original exact finite checks of Neal 2024 NAM and ZDNAM constructions.

Stdlib only; no author code, randomness, network, files or timestamps. JSON stdout.
Row procedures interpret the mathematical pseudocode of Algorithms 2, 3 and 5.
Matrix constructions independently apply Eq19 or solve the Eq93 balance equations.
Finite cases are evidence, not a universal performance or convergence theorem.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import product, permutations
from math import gcd, sqrt
import json


def norm(w):
    assert w and min(w) >= 0 and sum(w) > 0
    return [F(x, sum(w)) for x in w]


def verify(p, P):
    n = len(p)
    assert len(P) == n and all(len(row) == n for row in P)
    assert all(min(row) >= 0 and sum(row) == 1 for row in P)
    assert all(p[i]*P[i][j] == p[j]*P[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
    assert after(p, P) == p


def after(p, P):
    return [sum(p[i]*P[i][j] for i in range(len(p))) for j in range(len(p))]


def nam_row(p, order, k):
    """Algorithm 2, including zero residual and final focal guards."""
    n = len(p); row = [None]*n; s = F(1); f = F(1); i = 0
    while order[i] != k:
        a = order[i]
        if f <= 0:
            row[a] = F(0)
        else:
            q = p[a]; s -= q
            if q >= s:
                row[a] = f; f = F(0)
            else:
                row[a] = (q/s)*f; f -= row[a]
        i += 1
    if f <= 0:
        row[k] = F(0)
        for a in order[i+1:]: row[a] = F(0)
    else:
        q = p[k]; s -= q
        if q > s:
            row[k] = (q-s)/q*f
            for a in order[i+1:]: row[a] = min(f, p[a]/q*f)
        else:
            row[k] = F(0)
            for a in order[i+1:]: row[a] = min(f, p[a]/s*f)
    assert all(v is not None for v in row)
    return row


def unam_row(p, order, k):
    """Algorithm 3, separate from general NAM row code."""
    assert all(p[a] <= p[b] for a,b in zip(order, order[1:]))
    row = [None]*len(p); s = F(1); f = F(1); i = 0
    while order[i] != k:
        a = order[i]; q = p[a]; s -= q
        row[a] = min(f, q/s*f); f -= row[a]; i += 1
    if i == len(p)-1:
        row[k] = f
    else:
        s -= p[k]; row[k] = F(0)
        for a in order[i+1:]: row[a] = min(f, p[a]/s*f)
    assert all(v is not None for v in row)
    return row


def am_step(p, P, a, tail):
    """Maximal singleton/tail Eq19 change; independent of row recurrences."""
    q = p[a]; s = sum(p[j] for j in tail)
    assert q > 0 and s > 0
    bounds = [P[a][a]/s]
    bounds += [P[j][k]*s/(p[k]*q) for j in tail for k in tail]
    delta = min(bounds)
    Q = [row[:] for row in P]
    Q[a][a] -= delta*s
    for j in tail:
        Q[a][j] += delta*p[j]
        Q[j][a] += delta*q
        for k in tail: Q[j][k] -= delta*p[k]*q/s
    verify(p, Q)
    return Q


def nam_matrix(p, order):
    """Positive-support full AM construction, not row-pseudocode assembly."""
    assert min(p) > 0 and sorted(order) == list(range(len(p)))
    P = [p[:] for _ in p]
    for i,a in enumerate(order[:-1]):
        tail = order[i+1:]
        P = am_step(p, P, a, tail)
        if all(P[j][k] == 0 for j in tail for k in tail): break
    return P


def solve(A, b):
    n = len(b); M = [[F(x) for x in row]+[F(v)] for row,v in zip(A,b)]
    for c in range(n):
        r = next(i for i in range(c,n) if M[i][c]); M[c],M[r] = M[r],M[c]
        d = M[c][c]; M[c] = [x/d for x in M[c]]
        for i in range(n):
            if i != c:
                q = M[i][c]; M[i] = [x-q*y for x,y in zip(M[i],M[c])]
    return [row[-1] for row in M]


def zdnam_row(p, order, k, traces=None):
    """Algorithm 5 with explicit zero-tail branch, missing brackets restored."""
    n = len(p); assert all(p[a] >= p[b] for a,b in zip(order,order[1:]))
    row = [None]*n
    if p[k] >= F(1,2):
        row = [p[j]/p[k] if j != k else (2*p[k]-1)/p[k] for j in range(n)]
        if traces is not None: traces.append('current_half_or_more')
        return row
    if p[order[0]] >= F(1,2):
        row = [F(j == order[0]) for j in range(n)]
        if traces is not None: traces.append('other_half_or_more')
        return row
    s = F(1); f = F(1); i = 0
    while f > 0 and order[i] != k and p[order[i+1]] < s-p[order[i]]-p[order[i+1]]:
        a = order[i]; q = p[a]; s -= q
        row[a] = q/s*f; f -= row[a]; i += 1
    a = order[i]; q = p[a]; s -= q
    if f > 0 and s > 0 and i < n-1:
        b = order[i+1]; q2 = p[b]; s2 = max(F(0),s-q2)
        if q2 >= s2:
            A = (q+q2-s2)/2
            if k == a: row[a] = F(0); row[b] = f*A/q
            elif k == b: row[a] = f*A/q2; row[b] = F(0)
            if s2 <= 0:
                i += 2
                if traces is not None: traces.append('zero_tail_guard')
            else:
                B = (q-q2+s2)/(2*s2); C = (s2+q2-q)/(2*s2)
                if traces is not None: traces.append('completion_equality' if q2 == s2 else 'completion_strict')
                if k == a:
                    i += 2
                    while i < n: row[order[i]] = f*B*p[order[i]]/q; i += 1
                elif k == b:
                    i += 2
                    while i < n: row[order[i]] = f*C*p[order[i]]/q2; i += 1
                else:
                    row[a] = f*B; row[b] = f*C; i += 2
        else:
            assert k == a
            row[a] = F(0); i += 1
            while i < n: row[order[i]] = p[order[i]]/s*f; i += 1
    while i < n: row[order[i]] = F(0); i += 1
    assert all(x is not None for x in row), (p,order,k,row)
    return row


def zdnam_matrix(p, order):

"""Original exact rational illustrations; not author code or a general proof."""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import permutations
import json

def nam(pi, order):
    m=len(pi); out=[]
    for k in range(m):
        row=[F(0)]*m; s=f=F(1)
        for i,a in enumerate(order):
            if f==0:break
            q=pi[a];s-=q
            if a==k:
                if q>s:
                    row[a]=f*(q-s)/q
                    for b in order[i+1:]:row[b]=f*pi[b]/q
                else:
                    for b in order[i+1:]:row[b]=f*pi[b]/s
                break
            row[a]=f if q>=s else f*q/s
            f-=row[a]
        out.append(row)
    return out

def t2(pi):
    n=len(pi);P=[list(pi) for _ in pi]
    for _ in range(n):
        A=[i for i in range(n) if P[i][i]>0]
        if len(A)<=1:return P
        u=min((1-sum(P[k][l] for l in range(n) if l not in A))/sum(P[k][l] for l in A if l!=k) for k in A)
        Q=[r[:] for r in P]
        for k in A:
            for l in A:
                if l!=k:Q[k][l]=u*P[k][l]
            Q[k][k]=1-sum(Q[k][l] for l in range(n) if l!=k)
        P=Q
    raise AssertionError('Did not terminate')

def verify(pi,P):
    return all(sum(r)==1 and min(r)>=0 for r in P) and all(pi[i]*P[i][j]==pi[j]*P[j][i] for i in range(len(pi)) for j in range(len(pi)))

def encode(x):
    if isinstance(x,F):return str(x)
    if isinstance(x,list):return [encode(v) for v in x]
    if isinstance(x,dict):return {k:encode(v) for k,v in x.items()}
    return x

pi=[F(4,9),F(3,9),F(2,9)]
u=nam(pi,sorted(range(3),key=lambda i:pi[i]));d=nam(pi,sorted(range(3),key=lambda i:-pi[i])); mix=[[(u[i][j]+d[i][j])/2 for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
z=[[F(0),F(15,24),F(9,24)],[F(20,24),F(0),F(4,24)],[F(18,24),F(6,24),F(0)]]
all_orders=[{'order_1_based':[i+1 for i in o],'diagonal':[nam(pi,o)[i][i] for i in range(3)]} for o in permutations(range(3))]
assert all(verify(pi,P) for P in [u,d,mix,z])
assert d==[[F(0),F(9,15),F(6,15)],[F(12,15),F(1,15),F(2,15)],[F(12,15),F(3,15),F(0)]]
assert all(sum(v>0 for v in x['diagonal'])==1 for x in all_orders)
assert sum(mix[i][i]>0 for i in range(3))==2
examples=[]
for weights in [(4,3,2),(1,2,3,4),(1,3,3,5),(1,1),(1,1,1),(1,2,2)]:
    p=[F(w,sum(weights)) for w in weights]
    U=nam(p,sorted(range(len(p)),key=lambda i:p[i]));T=t2(p)
    assert U==T and verify(p,U)
    examples.append({'weights':list(weights),'UNAM_equals_Tjelmeland_T2':True})
print(json.dumps(encode({'scope':'Six finite strictly-positive rational targets for T2/UNAM equality; one three-state kernel-boundary example, all six focal orders. No general theorem, convergence, scan, floating implementation or author-code claim.','pi':pi,'UNAM':u,'DNAM':d,'UDNAM':mix,'ZDNAM_eq95':z,'all_orders':all_orders,'NAM_orders_have_one_self_entry':True,'UDNAM_has_two_self_entries':True,'ZDNAM_has_no_self_entries':True,'all_example_kernels_reversible_and_stochastic':True,'historical_equality_examples':examples}),indent=2))
